Brisbane is in the southeast corner of Queensland. The city is centred along the Brisbane River, and its eastern suburbs line the shores of Moreton Bay, a bay of the Coral Sea. The greater Brisbane region is on the coastal plain east of the [Great Dividing Range](./Great_Dividing_Range "Great Dividing Range"), with the [Taylor](./Taylor_Range "Taylor Range") and [D'Aguilar](./D'Aguilar_Range "D'Aguilar Range") ranges extending into the metropolitan area. Brisbane's metropolitan area sprawls along the Moreton Bay floodplain between the [Gold](./Gold_Coast,_Queensland "Gold Coast, Queensland") and [Sunshine](./Sunshine_Coast,_Queensland "Sunshine Coast, Queensland") coasts, approximately from [Caboolture](./Caboolture "Caboolture") in the north to [Beenleigh](./Beenleigh "Beenleigh") in the south, and across to [Ipswich](./Ipswich,_Queensland "Ipswich, Queensland") in the south west.

The Brisbane River is a wide [tidal](./Tide "Tide") [estuary](./Estuary "Estuary") and its waters throughout most of the metropolitan area are [brackish](./Brackish "Brackish") and [navigable](./Navigable "Navigable"). The river takes a winding course through the metropolitan area with many steep curves from the southwest to its mouth at Moreton Bay in the east. The metropolitan area is also traversed by several other rivers and creeks including the [North Pine](./North_Pine_River "North Pine River") and [South Pine](./South_Pine_River "South Pine River") rivers in the northern suburbs, which converge to form the [Pine River](./Pine_River_(Queensland) "Pine River (Queensland)") estuary at [Bramble Bay](./Bramble_Bay "Bramble Bay"), the [Caboolture River](./Caboolture_River "Caboolture River") further north, the [Logan](./Logan_River "Logan River") and [Albert](./Albert_River_(Queensland) "Albert River (Queensland)") rivers in the south-eastern suburbs, and [tributaries](./Tributaries "Tributaries") of the Brisbane River including the [Bremer River](./Bremer_River_(Queensland) "Bremer River (Queensland)") in the south-western suburbs, [Breakfast Creek](./Breakfast_Creek "Breakfast Creek") in the inner-north, [Norman Creek](./Norman_Creek_(Queensland) "Norman Creek (Queensland)") in the inner-south, [Oxley Creek](./Oxley_Creek "Oxley Creek") in the south, [Bulimba Creek](./Bulimba_Creek "Bulimba Creek") in the inner south-east and [Moggill Creek](./Moggill_Creek "Moggill Creek") in the west. The city is on a low-lying [floodplain](./Floodplain "Floodplain"),[[54]](./Brisbane#cite_note-55) with the risk of flooding addressed by various state and local government regulations and plans.[[55]](./Brisbane#cite_note-56)

The waters of Moreton Bay are sheltered from large [swells](./Swell_(ocean) "Swell (ocean)") by [Moreton](./Moreton_Island "Moreton Island"), [Stradbroke](./North_Stradbroke_Island "North Stradbroke Island") and [Bribie](./Bribie_Island "Bribie Island") islands, so whilst the bay can become rough in windy conditions, the waves at the Moreton Bay coastline are generally not [surfable](./Surfing "Surfing"). Unsheltered surf beaches lie on the eastern coasts of [Moreton](./Moreton_Island "Moreton Island"), [Stradbroke](./North_Stradbroke_Island "North Stradbroke Island") and [Bribie](./Bribie_Island "Bribie Island") islands and on the Gold Coast and Sunshine Coast to the south and north respectively. The southern part of Moreton Bay also contains smaller islands such as [St Helena Island](./St_Helena_Island_National_Park "St Helena Island National Park"), [Peel Island](./Peel_Island_(Queensland) "Peel Island (Queensland)"), [Coochiemudlo Island](./Coochiemudlo_Island "Coochiemudlo Island"), [Russell Island](./Russell_Island_(Moreton_Bay) "Russell Island (Moreton Bay)"), [Lamb Island](./Lamb_Island,_Queensland "Lamb Island, Queensland") and [Macleay Island](./Macleay_Island "Macleay Island").

The city of Brisbane is hilly.[[56]](./Brisbane#cite_note-thenandnow-57) The urban area, including the central business district, are partially elevated by spurs of the [Herbert Taylor Range](./Herbert_Taylor_Range "Herbert Taylor Range"), such as the summit of [Mount Coot-tha](./Mount_Coot-tha "Mount Coot-tha"), reaching up to 300 m (980 ft) and [Enoggera Hill](./Enoggera_Hill "Enoggera Hill"). The [D'Aguilar National Park](./D'Aguilar_National_Park "D'Aguilar National Park"), encompassing the [D'Aguilar Range](./D'Aguilar_Range "D'Aguilar Range"), bounds the north-west of Brisbane's built-up area, and contains the taller peaks of [Mount Nebo](./Mount_Nebo_(Queensland) "Mount Nebo (Queensland)"), [Camp Mountain](./Camp_Mountain "Camp Mountain"), [Mount Pleasant](./Mount_Pleasant,_Queensland_(Moreton_Bay) "Mount Pleasant, Queensland (Moreton Bay)"), [Mount Glorious](./Mount_Glorious "Mount Glorious"), [Mount Samson](./Mount_Samson "Mount Samson") and [Mount Mee](./Mount_Mee "Mount Mee"). Other prominent rises in Brisbane are [Mount Gravatt](./Mount_Gravatt "Mount Gravatt"), [Toohey Mountain](./Toohey_Mountain "Toohey Mountain"), [Mount Petrie](./Mount_Petrie "Mount Petrie"), [Highgate Hill](./Highgate_Hill,_Queensland "Highgate Hill, Queensland"), [Mount Ommaney](./Mount_Ommaney "Mount Ommaney"), [Stephens Mountain](./Stephens_Mountain "Stephens Mountain"), and [Whites Hill](./Whites_Hill "Whites Hill"), which are dotted across the city.

Much of the rock upon which Brisbane is located is the characteristic [Brisbane tuff](./Brisbane_tuff "Brisbane tuff"), a form of welded [ignimbrite](./Ignimbrite "Ignimbrite"),[[57]](./Brisbane#cite_note-wdhs-58) which is most prominently found at the [Kangaroo Point Cliffs](./Kangaroo_Point_Cliffs "Kangaroo Point Cliffs") at [Kangaroo Point](./Kangaroo_Point,_Queensland "Kangaroo Point, Queensland") and the New Farm Cliffs on the [Petrie Bight](./Petrie_Bight "Petrie Bight") reach of the Brisbane River. The stone was used in the construction of historical buildings such as the [Commissariat Store](./Commissariat_Store,_Brisbane "Commissariat Store, Brisbane") and [Cathedral of St Stephen](./Cathedral_of_St_Stephen,_Brisbane "Cathedral of St Stephen, Brisbane"), and the roadside [kerbs](./Kerbs "Kerbs") in inner areas of Brisbane are still manufactured of Brisbane tuff.

### Ecology

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/75/Jacaranda_mimosifolia_trees_in_New_Farm_Park%2C_Queensland%2C_07.jpg/250px-Jacaranda_mimosifolia_trees_in_New_Farm_Park%2C_Queensland%2C_07.jpg)](./File:Jacaranda_mimosifolia_trees_in_New_Farm_Park,_Queensland,_07.jpg)

[Jacaranda](./Jacaranda_mimosifolia "Jacaranda mimosifolia") trees in bloom at [New Farm Park](./New_Farm_Park "New Farm Park")

Brisbane is located within the [South East Queensland](./South_East_Queensland "South East Queensland") [biogeographic region](./Interim_Biogeographic_Regionalisation_for_Australia "Interim Biogeographic Regionalisation for Australia"), and is home to numerous [Eucalyptus](./Eucalyptus "Eucalyptus") varieties. Common trees in Brisbane include the [Moreton Bay fig](./Moreton_Bay_fig "Moreton Bay fig"), an evergreen [banyan](./Banyan "Banyan") with large [buttress roots](./Buttress_roots "Buttress roots") named for the region which are often lit with [decorative lights](./Christmas_lights "Christmas lights") in the inner city, as well as the [jacaranda](./Jacaranda_mimosifolia "Jacaranda mimosifolia"), a subtropical tree native to [South America](./South_America "South America") which line many avenues and parks and bloom with purple flowers during October.[[58]](./Brisbane#cite_note-59) Other trees common to the metropolitan area include [Moreton Bay chestnut](./Moreton_Bay_chestnut "Moreton Bay chestnut"), [broad-leaved paperbark](./Broad-leaved_paperbark "Broad-leaved paperbark"), [poinciana](./Delonix_regia "Delonix regia"), [weeping lilli pilli](./Weeping_lilli_pilli "Weeping lilli pilli") and [Bangalow palm](./Bangalow_palm "Bangalow palm"). Some of the banks of the [Brisbane River](./Brisbane_River "Brisbane River") and [Moreton Bay](./Moreton_Bay "Moreton Bay") are home to [mangrove](./Australian_mangroves "Australian mangroves") wetlands. The [red poinsettia](./Poinsettia "Poinsettia") is the original official floral emblem of Brisbane, however it is native to Central America.[[59]](./Brisbane#cite_note-:1-60) An additional floral emblem, the [Brisbane wattle](./Acacia_fimbriata "Acacia fimbriata"), which is native to the Brisbane area, was added in 2023.[[60]](./Brisbane#cite_note-61)

Brisbane is home to numerous bird species, with common species including [rainbow lorikeets](./Rainbow_lorikeet "Rainbow lorikeet"), [kookaburras](./Kookaburra "Kookaburra"), [galahs](./Galah "Galah"), [Australian white ibises](./Australian_white_ibis "Australian white ibis"), [Australian brushturkeys](./Australian_brushturkey "Australian brushturkey"), [Torresian crows](./Torresian_crow "Torresian crow"), [Australian magpies](./Australian_magpie "Australian magpie") and [noisy miners](./Noisy_miner "Noisy miner"). Common reptiles include [common garden skinks](./Common_garden_skink "Common garden skink"), [Australian water dragons](./Australian_water_dragon "Australian water dragon"), [bearded dragons](./Bearded_dragons "Bearded dragons") and [blue-tongued lizards](./Blue-tongued_skink "Blue-tongued skink"). [Common ringtail possums](./Common_ringtail_possum "Common ringtail possum") and [flying foxes](./Flying_foxes "Flying foxes") are common in parks and yards throughout the city, as are [common crow butterflies](./Euploea_core "Euploea core"), [blue triangle butterflies](./Graphium_sarpedon "Graphium sarpedon"), [golden orb-weaver spiders](./Nephila "Nephila") and [St Andrew's Cross spiders](./Argiope_keyserlingi "Argiope keyserlingi"). The [Brisbane River](./Brisbane_River "Brisbane River") is home to many fish species including [yellowfin bream](./Acanthopagrus_australis "Acanthopagrus australis"), [flathead](./Flathead_(fish) "Flathead (fish)"), [Australasian snapper](./Australasian_snapper "Australasian snapper"), and [bull sharks](./Bull_shark "Bull shark"). The waters of [Moreton Bay](./Moreton_Bay "Moreton Bay") are home to [dugongs](./Dugong "Dugong"), [humpback whales](./Humpback_whale "Humpback whale"), [dolphins](./Dolphin "Dolphin"), [mud crabs](./Scylla_serrata "Scylla serrata"), [soldier crabs](./Mictyris_longicarpus "Mictyris longicarpus"), [Moreton Bay bugs](./Moreton_Bay_bug "Moreton Bay bug") and numerous [shellfish](./Shellfish "Shellfish") species. The [koala](./Koala "Koala") and the [graceful tree frog](./Graceful_tree_frog "Graceful tree frog") are the official faunal emblems of Brisbane, however both are increasingly less common due to the effects of increased development and climate change.[[59]](./Brisbane#cite_note-:1-60)[[61]](./Brisbane#cite_note-62)

### Climate

Main article: [Climate of Brisbane](./Climate_of_Brisbane "Climate of Brisbane")

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/ba/Storm_over_the_Brisbane_city_centre.jpg/250px-Storm_over_the_Brisbane_city_centre.jpg)](./File:Storm_over_the_Brisbane_city_centre.jpg)

Lightning over the Brisbane city centre, February 2020

Brisbane has a [humid subtropical climate](./Humid_subtropical_climate "Humid subtropical climate") ([Köppen climate classification](./Köppen_climate_classification "Köppen climate classification"): *Cfa*)[[62]](./Brisbane#cite_note-63) with hot, wet summers and moderately drier, mild winters.[[63]](./Brisbane#cite_note-64)[[64]](./Brisbane#cite_note-65) Brisbane experiences an annual mean minimum of 16.6 °C (62 °F) and mean maximum of 26.6 °C (80 °F), making it Australia's second-hottest capital city after [Darwin](./Darwin,_Northern_Territory "Darwin, Northern Territory").[[65]](./Brisbane#cite_note-auto1-66) Seasonality is not pronounced, and average maximum temperatures of above 26 °C (79 °F) persist from October through to April.

Due to its proximity to the Coral Sea and a warm ocean current, Brisbane's overall temperature variability is somewhat less than most Australian capitals. Summers are long, hot, and wet, but temperatures only occasionally reach 35 °C (95 °F) or more. Eighty percent of summer days record a maximum temperature of 27 to 33 °C (81 to 91 °F). Winters are short and warm, with average maximums of about 22 °C (72 °F); maximum temperatures below 20 °C (68 °F) are rare.

The city's highest recorded temperature was 43.2 °C (109.8 °F) on [Australia Day](./Australia_Day "Australia Day") 1940 at the Brisbane Regional Office,[[66]](./Brisbane#cite_note-ReferenceB-67) with the highest temperature at the current station being 41.7 °C (107.1 °F) on 22 February 2004;[[67]](./Brisbane#cite_note-68) but temperatures above 38 °C (100 °F) are uncommon. On 19 July 2007, Brisbane's temperature fell below the freezing point for the first time since records began, registering −0.1 °C (31.8 °F) at the airport station.[[68]](./Brisbane#cite_note-69) The city station has never dropped below 2 °C (36 °F),[[69]](./Brisbane#cite_note-ReferenceA-70) with the average coldest night during winter being around 6 °C (43 °F), however locations in the west of the metropolitan area such as [Ipswich](./Ipswich,_Queensland "Ipswich, Queensland") have dropped as low as −5 °C (23 °F) with heavy ground frost.[[70]](./Brisbane#cite_note-71)

In 2009, Brisbane recorded its hottest winter day (from June to August) at 35.4 °C (95.7 °F) on 24 August;[[71]](./Brisbane#cite_note-72) The average July day however is around 22 °C (72 °F) with sunny skies and low humidity, occasionally as high as 27 °C (81 °F), whilst maximum temperatures below 18 °C (64 °F) are uncommon and usually associated with brief periods of cloud and winter rain.[[69]](./Brisbane#cite_note-ReferenceA-70) The highest minimum temperature ever recorded in Brisbane was 28.0 °C (82.4 °F) on 29 January 1940 and again on 21 January 2017, whilst the lowest maximum temperature was 10.2 °C (50.4 °F) on 12 August 1954.[[66]](./Brisbane#cite_note-ReferenceB-67)

Sleet or snow is exceptionally rare in Brisbane. The Bureau of Meteorology has only three official records of snow in Brisbane: June 1927, June 1932 (witnessed by seven people), and September 1958 (light flakes were seen by four people at 5:15pm in Moorooka, Wooloowin, Bowen Hills and Taringa).
Unofficial reports exist of earlier snowfalls, such as follows from July 1882:[*[This quote needs a citation](./Wikipedia:Inline_citation#When_you_must_use_inline_citations "Wikipedia:Inline citation")*]
"The snow was most noticeable in Woolloongabba, but in Stanley Street, South Brisbane it was sufficiently heavy to allow of people wiping it from their clothing.
"In the vicinity of the museum the fall was, though very slight, plainly noticeable.
"It is said that snow fell in this city 35 years ago, and the summer following the period of the fall was remarkable for its excessive heat."[*[citation needed](./Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")*]

Annual precipitation is ample. From November to March, thunderstorms are common over Brisbane, with the more severe events accompanied by large damaging hail stones, torrential rain and destructive winds. To the west of Brisbane, [supercell thunderstorms](./Supercell "Supercell") often form during the late spring and summer months. These can include tornadic supercells.[[72]](./Brisbane#cite_note-73) On an annual basis, Brisbane averages 124 clear days, with overcast skies more common in the warmer months.[[73]](./Brisbane#cite_note-74) Dewpoints in the summer average at around 20 °C (68 °F); the [apparent temperature](./Apparent_temperature "Apparent temperature") exceeds 30 °C (86 °F) on almost all summer days.[[69]](./Brisbane#cite_note-ReferenceA-70) Brisbane's wettest day occurred on 21 January 1887, when 465 millimetres (18.3 in) of rain fell on the city, the highest maximum daily rainfall of Australia's capital cities. The wettest month on record was February 1893, when 1,025.9 millimetres (40.39 in) of rain fell, although in the last 30 years the record monthly rainfall has been a much lower 479.8 millimetres (18.89 in) from December 2010. Very occasionally a whole month will pass with no recorded rainfall, the last time this happened was August 1991.[[66]](./Brisbane#cite_note-ReferenceB-67) The city has suffered four major floods since its founding, in [February 1893](./1893_Brisbane_flood "1893 Brisbane flood"), [January 1974](./1974_Brisbane_Flood "1974 Brisbane Flood") (partially a result of [Cyclone Wanda](./Cyclone_Wanda "Cyclone Wanda")), [January 2011](./2010–2011_Queensland_floods "2010–2011 Queensland floods") (partially a result of [Cyclone Tasha](./Cyclone_Tasha "Cyclone Tasha")) and [February 2022](./2022_eastern_Australia_floods "2022 eastern Australia floods").

Brisbane is within the southern reaches of the [tropical cyclone](./Tropical_cyclone "Tropical cyclone") risk zone. Full-strength tropical cyclones rarely affect Brisbane, but occasionally do so, the most recent being [Cyclone Alfred](./Cyclone_Alfred "Cyclone Alfred"), making landfall as a category 1 around [Bribie Island](./Bribie_Island "Bribie Island") on the 8th of March, 2025, bringing destructive winds and causing significant flooding throughout parts of south-eastern Queensland and north-eastern New South Wales. The more common risk is from ex-tropical cyclones (tropical low systems), which typically bring destructive winds and flooding rains.[[74]](./Brisbane#cite_note-75)

The temperature of the ocean ranges from 21 °C (70 °F) in August to 27 °C (81 °F) in February.[[75]](./Brisbane#cite_note-seatemperature-76)

Urban structure

The [Brisbane CBD](./Brisbane_CBD "Brisbane CBD") and surrounds from the [Mount Coot-tha Lookout](./Mount_Coot-tha_Lookout "Mount Coot-tha Lookout") in the [Taylor Range](./Taylor_Range "Taylor Range")

The [Brisbane central business district](./Brisbane_central_business_district "Brisbane central business district") (CBD, colloquially referred to as "the city") lies in a curve of the Brisbane river. The CBD covers 2.2 km2 (0.8 sq mi) and is walkable. Most central streets are named after members of the [House of Hanover](./House_of_Hanover "House of Hanover"). [Queen Street](./Queen_Street,_Brisbane "Queen Street, Brisbane") (named in honour of [Queen Victoria](./Queen_Victoria "Queen Victoria")) is Brisbane's traditional [main street](./Main_street "Main street") and contains its largest [pedestrian mall](./Pedestrian_mall "Pedestrian mall"), the [Queen Street Mall](./Queen_Street_Mall "Queen Street Mall"). Streets named after female members ([Adelaide](./Adelaide_Street,_Brisbane "Adelaide Street, Brisbane"), [Alice](./Alice_Street,_Brisbane "Alice Street, Brisbane"), [Ann](./Ann_Street,_Brisbane "Ann Street, Brisbane"), [Charlotte](./Charlotte_Street,_Brisbane "Charlotte Street, Brisbane"), [Elizabeth](./Elizabeth_Street,_Brisbane "Elizabeth Street, Brisbane"), [Margaret](./Margaret_Street,_Brisbane "Margaret Street, Brisbane"), and [Mary](./Mary_Street,_Brisbane "Mary Street, Brisbane")) run parallel to [Queen Street](./Queen_Street,_Brisbane "Queen Street, Brisbane") and perpendicular to streets named after male members ([Albert](./Albert_Street,_Brisbane "Albert Street, Brisbane"), [Edward](./Edward_Street,_Brisbane "Edward Street, Brisbane"), [George](./George_Street,_Brisbane "George Street, Brisbane"), and [William](./William_Street,_Brisbane "William Street, Brisbane")).

The CBD's [squares](./Town_square "Town square") include [King George Square](./King_George_Square "King George Square"), [Post Office Square](./Post_Office_Square,_Brisbane "Post Office Square, Brisbane") and [ANZAC Square](./ANZAC_Square,_Brisbane "ANZAC Square, Brisbane") (home to the city's central [war memorial](./War_memorial "War memorial")).

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0d/River_views_of_Brisbane_CBD%2C_October_2018%2C_03.jpg/250px-River_views_of_Brisbane_CBD%2C_October_2018%2C_03.jpg)](./File:River_views_of_Brisbane_CBD,_October_2018,_03.jpg)

The [CBD](./Brisbane_CBD "Brisbane CBD") and [South Bank](./South_Bank,_Queensland "South Bank, Queensland") fronts the [Brisbane River](./Brisbane_River "Brisbane River")

At the broadest level, Brisbane's metropolitan area is informally divided into the northside and the southside, with the dividing line being the [Brisbane River](./Brisbane_River "Brisbane River"),[[77]](./Brisbane#cite_note-78) as crossing one of the 15 [bridges across the river](./Bridges_over_the_Brisbane_River "Bridges over the Brisbane River") is required to travel to the opposite side by land transport. Due to the river's winding trajectory, this results in many areas which are south of the CBD being classified as located in the northside, and vice versa. At a more specific level, the metropolitan area contains informal regions including the northern, southern, eastern and western suburbs, the bayside suburbs along the Moreton Bay coastline, and the Moreton Bay, Redland, Logan and Ipswich regions in the outer north, east, south and west respectively.

Greater Brisbane had a density of 159 inhabitants per square kilometre (410/sq mi) in 2021.[[7]](./Brisbane#cite_note-auto5-7) Like most Australian cities, Brisbane has a sprawling metropolitan area which takes in excess of one hour to traverse either north to south or east to west by car without traffic.

From the 1970s onwards, there has been a large increase in the construction of [apartment](./Apartment "Apartment") developments, including [mid-rise](./Mid-rise "Mid-rise") and [high rise](./High_rise "High rise") buildings, which has quickened in the 21st century. At the 2021 census, 73.4% of residents lived in [separate houses](./Separate_houses "Separate houses"), 14.7% lived in [apartments](./Apartment "Apartment"), and 11.4% lived in [townhouses](./Townhouse "Townhouse"), [terrace houses](./Terrace_house "Terrace house"), or [semidetached](./Semidetached "Semidetached") houses.[[7]](./Brisbane#cite_note-auto5-7)

### Parklands

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/48/Tree_lined_avenue_at_the_City_Botanic_Gardens%2C_Brisbane.jpg/250px-Tree_lined_avenue_at_the_City_Botanic_Gardens%2C_Brisbane.jpg)](./File:Tree_lined_avenue_at_the_City_Botanic_Gardens,_Brisbane.jpg)

[Moreton Bay figs](./Moreton_Bay_fig "Moreton Bay fig") at the [City Botanic Gardens](./City_Botanic_Gardens "City Botanic Gardens")

Brisbane's major parklands include the riverside [City Botanic Gardens](./City_Botanic_Gardens "City Botanic Gardens") at [Gardens Point](./Gardens_Point "Gardens Point"),[[78]](./Brisbane#cite_note-79) [Roma Street Parkland](./Roma_Street_Parkland "Roma Street Parkland"), the 27-hectare [Victoria Park](./Victoria_Park,_Brisbane "Victoria Park, Brisbane") at [Spring Hill](./Spring_Hill,_Queensland "Spring Hill, Queensland") and [Herston](./Herston,_Queensland "Herston, Queensland"), [South Bank Parklands](./South_Bank_Parklands "South Bank Parklands") along the river at [South Bank](./South_Bank,_Queensland "South Bank, Queensland"), the [Brisbane Botanic Gardens](./Brisbane_Botanic_Gardens,_Mount_Coot-tha "Brisbane Botanic Gardens, Mount Coot-tha") at [Mount Coot-tha](./Mount_Coot-tha "Mount Coot-tha") and the riverside [New Farm Park](./New_Farm_Park "New Farm Park") at [New Farm](./New_Farm "New Farm").

There are many national parks surrounding the Brisbane metropolitan area. The [D'Aguilar National Park](./D'Aguilar_National_Park "D'Aguilar National Park") is a major [national park](./National_park "National park") along the northwest of the metropolitan area in the [D'Aguilar Range](./D'Aguilar_Range "D'Aguilar Range"). The [Glass House Mountains National Park](./Glass_House_Mountains_National_Park "Glass House Mountains National Park") is located to the north of the metropolitan area in the [Glass House Mountains](./Glass_House_Mountains,_Queensland "Glass House Mountains, Queensland") and provides green space between the Brisbane metropolitan area and the [Sunshine Coast](./Sunshine_Coast,_Queensland "Sunshine Coast, Queensland"). The [Tamborine National Park](./Tamborine_National_Park "Tamborine National Park") at [Tamborine Mountain](./Tamborine_Mountain "Tamborine Mountain") is located in the [Gold Coast hinterland](./Gold_Coast_hinterland "Gold Coast hinterland") to the south of the metropolitan area.

The eastern metropolitan area is built along the [Moreton Bay Marine Park](./Moreton_Bay_Marine_Park "Moreton Bay Marine Park"), encompassing [Moreton Bay](./Moreton_Bay "Moreton Bay"). Significant areas of [Moreton](./Moreton_Island "Moreton Island"), [North Stradbroke](./North_Stradbroke_Island "North Stradbroke Island") and [Bribie](./Bribie_Island "Bribie Island") islands also covered by the [Moreton Island National Park](./Moreton_Island_National_Park "Moreton Island National Park"), [Naree Budjong Djara National Park](./Naree_Budjong_Djara_National_Park "Naree Budjong Djara National Park") and the [Bribie Island National Park](./Bribie_Island_National_Park "Bribie Island National Park") respectively. The [Boondall Wetlands](./Boondall_Wetlands "Boondall Wetlands") in the suburb of [Boondall](./Boondall "Boondall") include 1,100 hectares of wetlands which are home to [mangroves](./Australian_mangroves "Australian mangroves") and [shorebirds](./Shorebirds "Shorebirds") as well as walking tracks.

### Architecture

Further information: [List of tallest buildings in Brisbane](./List_of_tallest_buildings_in_Brisbane "List of tallest buildings in Brisbane") and [Queenslander (architecture)](./Queenslander_(architecture) "Queenslander (architecture)")

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7a/Commissariat_Store%2C_Brisbane_10.jpg/250px-Commissariat_Store%2C_Brisbane_10.jpg)](./File:Commissariat_Store,_Brisbane_10.jpg)

The [Commissariat Store](./Commissariat_Store,_Brisbane "Commissariat Store, Brisbane") dates back to 1828 and was built by convicts.

Brisbane has a number of heritage buildings, some of which date back to the 1820s, including [The Old Windmill](./The_Old_Windmill,_Brisbane "The Old Windmill, Brisbane") in [Wickham Park](./Wickham_Park,_Brisbane "Wickham Park, Brisbane"), built by convict labour in 1824,[[79]](./Brisbane#cite_note-80) which is the oldest surviving building in Brisbane, and the [Commissariat Store](./Commissariat_Store,_Brisbane "Commissariat Store, Brisbane") on [William Street](./William_Street,_Brisbane "William Street, Brisbane"), built by convict labour in 1828, which was originally used as a grain house, and is now the home of the Royal Historical Society of Brisbane and contains a museum.[[80]](./Brisbane#cite_note-81)[[81]](./Brisbane#cite_note-82)[[82]](./Brisbane#cite_note-83) Other 19th and early 20th-century buildings of architectural significance include the [Treasury Building](./Treasury_Building,_Brisbane "Treasury Building, Brisbane"), [City Hall](./Brisbane_City_Hall "Brisbane City Hall"), [Customs House](./Customs_House,_Brisbane "Customs House, Brisbane"), [Land Administration Building](./Land_Administration_Building "Land Administration Building"), [MacArthur Chambers](./MacArthur_Chambers "MacArthur Chambers"), [The Mansions](./The_Mansions,_Brisbane "The Mansions, Brisbane"), [National Australia Bank Building](./National_Australia_Bank_(308_Queen_Street) "National Australia Bank (308 Queen Street)"), the [Old Museum Building](./Old_Museum_Building,_Brisbane "Old Museum Building, Brisbane") and the [Federation-style](./Federation_architecture "Federation architecture") [People's Palace](./People's_Palace,_Brisbane "People's Palace, Brisbane"), a former temperance hotel on [Edward Street](./Edward_Street,_Brisbane "Edward Street, Brisbane").

One of the oldest synagogues in the Queensland area is the Brisbane Synagogue located on Margaret Street in Brisbane city. This historic synagogue can be attributed as the "centerpiece of the Jewish community's presence in the state" It was established in 1866 and designed by architect Arthur Morry. Another architect by the name of Andrea Stombuco has also been credited as a designer of the synagogue by previous members of the community. The architectural design of this historic synagogue is in the style of Neo-Moorish also known as Byzantine style.[[83]](./Brisbane#cite_note-84)

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/72/Queenslander_style_house_in_Sherwood%2C_Queensland%2C_2022%2C_03.jpg/250px-Queenslander_style_house_in_Sherwood%2C_Queensland%2C_2022%2C_03.jpg)](./File:Queenslander_style_house_in_Sherwood,_Queensland,_2022,_03.jpg)

[Queenslander](./Queenslander_(architecture) "Queenslander (architecture)")-style house in [Sherwood](./Sherwood,_Queensland "Sherwood, Queensland"), a suburb of Brisbane

[Queenslander](./Queenslander_(architecture) "Queenslander (architecture)")-style housing is common in Brisbane.[[84]](./Brisbane#cite_note-LinOsb-85) Queenslander homes typically feature timber construction with large [verandahs](./Verandah "Verandah"), [gabled](./Gable_roof "Gable roof") corrugated iron roofs, and high ceilings. Most of these houses are elevated on stumps (also called stilts), traditionally built of timber, which allow for a void under the houses which aids in cooling. The relatively low cost of timber in south-east Queensland meant that until recently, most residences were constructed of timber, rather than brick or stone.[*[citation needed](./Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")*] Early legislation decreed a minimum size for residential blocks leading to few [terrace houses](./Terrace_house "Terrace house") being constructed in Brisbane.[*[citation needed](./Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")*] The high-density housing that historically existed came in the form of miniature [Queenslander](./Queenslander_(architecture) "Queenslander (architecture)")-style houses which resemble the much larger traditional styles, but are sometimes only one-quarter the size.[*[citation needed](./Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")*] These houses are most common in the inner-city suburbs.

Brisbane is home to several of [Australia's tallest buildings](./List_of_tallest_buildings_in_Australia "List of tallest buildings in Australia"). All of Brisbane's skyscrapers (buildings with a height greater than 150 m (490 ft)) are located within the CBD, but the inner suburbs are also home to a number of high-density buildings, [Torbreck](./Torbreck,_Brisbane "Torbreck, Brisbane") being the first high-rise and mix-use residential development in [Queensland](./Queensland "Queensland"). Brisbane's 91-metre City Hall was the city's tallest building for decades after its completion in 1930 and was finally surpassed in 1970, which marked the beginning of the widespread construction of high-rise buildings.[*[citation needed](./Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")*]

[Brisbane's tallest building](./List_of_tallest_buildings_in_Brisbane "List of tallest buildings in Brisbane") is currently [Brisbane Skytower](./Brisbane_Skytower "Brisbane Skytower"), which has a height of 270 m (890 ft).[[85]](./Brisbane#cite_note-86) Architecturally prominent skyscrapers include the [Harry Seidler](./Harry_Seidler "Harry Seidler")-designed [Riparian Plaza](./Riparian_Plaza "Riparian Plaza"), [One One One Eagle Street](./One_One_One_Eagle_Street "One One One Eagle Street"), which incorporates [LED lighting](./LED_lamp "LED lamp") resembling the [buttress roots](./Buttress_root "Buttress root") of the [Moreton Bay fig](./Moreton_Bay_fig "Moreton Bay fig"), and [1 William Street](./1_William_Street,_Brisbane "1 William Street, Brisbane"), the headquarters of the [Queensland Government](./Queensland_Government "Queensland Government").

Demographics
------------

Main article: [Demographics of Brisbane](./Demographics_of_Brisbane "Demographics of Brisbane")

Brisbane's Greater Capital City Statistical Area includes the Local Government Areas of [City of Brisbane](./City_of_Brisbane "City of Brisbane"), [City of Ipswich](./City_of_Ipswich "City of Ipswich"), [City of Moreton Bay](./City_of_Moreton_Bay "City of Moreton Bay"), [Logan City](./Logan_City "Logan City") and [Redland City](./Redland_City "Redland City"), as well as parts of [Lockyer Valley Region](./Lockyer_Valley_Region "Lockyer Valley Region"), [Scenic Rim Region](./Scenic_Rim_Region "Scenic Rim Region") and [Somerset Region](./Somerset_Region "Somerset Region"), which form a continuous metropolitan area. The [Australian Bureau of Statistics](./Australian_Bureau_of_Statistics "Australian Bureau of Statistics") estimates that the population of Greater Brisbane is 2,780,063 as of June 2024,[[9]](./Brisbane#cite_note-abs.gov.au-9) making it the [third-largest city](./List_of_cities_in_Australia_by_population "List of cities in Australia by population") in Australia.

The 2021 census showed that 20.7% of Brisbane's inhabitants were [born overseas](./Immigration_to_Australia "Immigration to Australia") and 25.2% of inhabitants had at least one parent born overseas.[[87]](./Brisbane#cite_note-auto4-91) Brisbane has the [26th largest immigrant population](./Foreign_born#Metropolitan_and_Urban_regions_with_largest_foreign_born_populations "Foreign born") among world metropolitan areas. Of inhabitants born outside of Australia, the five most prevalent countries of birth were New Zealand, England, India, mainland China and the Philippines. Brisbane has the largest community of New Zealanders outside of New Zealand.

The areas of [Sunnybank](./Sunnybank,_Queensland "Sunnybank, Queensland"),[[88]](./Brisbane#cite_note-92) [Sunnybank Hills](./Sunnybank_Hills "Sunnybank Hills"),[[89]](./Brisbane#cite_note-93) [Stretton](./Stretton,_Queensland "Stretton, Queensland"),[[90]](./Brisbane#cite_note-94) [Robertson](./Robertson,_Queensland "Robertson, Queensland"),[[91]](./Brisbane#cite_note-95) [Calamvale](./Calamvale "Calamvale"),[[92]](./Brisbane#cite_note-96) [Macgregor](./MacGregor,_Queensland "MacGregor, Queensland"),[[93]](./Brisbane#cite_note-97) [Eight Mile Plains](./Eight_Mile_Plains "Eight Mile Plains"),[[94]](./Brisbane#cite_note-98) [Runcorn](./Runcorn,_Queensland "Runcorn, Queensland"),[[95]](./Brisbane#cite_note-99) and [Rochedale](./Rochedale,_Queensland "Rochedale, Queensland"),[[96]](./Brisbane#cite_note-100) are home to a large proportion of Brisbane's Mainland China, Taiwan and Hong Kong-born population, with Chinese being the most commonly-reported ancestry in each of these areas. ### Language

At the 2021 census, 77.3% of inhabitants spoke only English at home,[[87]](./Brisbane#cite_note-auto4-91) with the next most common languages being [Mandarin](./Mandarin_Chinese "Mandarin Chinese") (2.5%), [Vietnamese](./Vietnamese_language "Vietnamese language") (1.1%), [Punjabi](./Punjabi_language "Punjabi language") (0.9%), [Cantonese](./Cantonese "Cantonese") (0.9%), and [Spanish](./Spanish_language "Spanish language") (0.8%).[[87]](./Brisbane#cite_note-auto4-91)

### Religion

At the 2021 census, the most commonly cited religious affiliation was "No religion" (41.4%).
Brisbane's most popular religion at the 2021 census was [Christianity](./Christianity "Christianity") at 44.3%, the most popular denominations of which were [Catholicism](./Catholic_Church_in_Australia "Catholic Church in Australia") (18.6%) and [Anglicanism](./Anglican_Church_of_Australia "Anglican Church of Australia") (9.7%). [Brisbane's CBD](./Brisbane's_CBD "Brisbane's CBD") is home to two cathedrals – [St John's](./St_John's_Cathedral_(Brisbane) "St John's Cathedral (Brisbane)") (Anglican) and [St Stephen's](./Cathedral_of_St_Stephen,_Brisbane "Cathedral of St Stephen, Brisbane") (Catholic).

The most popular non-Christian religions at the 2021 census were [Hindu](./Hinduism "Hinduism") (2%), [Buddhist](./Buddhist "Buddhist") (1.9%), and [Muslim](./Islam "Islam") (1.8%).[[104]](./Brisbane#cite_note-Archived_copy-109)

Economy
-------

Main articles: [Economy of Brisbane](./Economy_of_Brisbane "Economy of Brisbane") and [Port of Brisbane](./Port_of_Brisbane "Port of Brisbane")

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/dc/River_views_of_Brisbane_CBD_seen_from_Kangaroo_Point%2C_Queensland_in_April_2019%2C_04.jpg/250px-River_views_of_Brisbane_CBD_seen_from_Kangaroo_Point%2C_Queensland_in_April_2019%2C_04.jpg)](./File:River_views_of_Brisbane_CBD_seen_from_Kangaroo_Point,_Queensland_in_April_2019,_04.jpg)

The Golden Triangle financial precinct surrounding [Eagle Street Pier](./Eagle_Street_Pier_ferry_wharf "Eagle Street Pier ferry wharf") in the [CBD](./Brisbane_central_business_district "Brisbane central business district")

[Categorised as](./Globalization_and_World_Cities_Research_Network "Globalization and World Cities Research Network") a [global city](./Global_city "Global city"), Brisbane is among [Asia-Pacific](./Asia-Pacific "Asia-Pacific") [cities with largest GDPs](./List_of_cities_by_GDP "List of cities by GDP") and is one of the major business hubs in Australia, with strengths in [mining](./Mining "Mining"), [banking](./Banking "Banking"), [insurance](./Insurance "Insurance"), [transportation](./Transportation "Transportation"), [information technology](./Information_technology "Information technology"), [real estate](./Real_estate "Real estate") and [food](./Food_industry "Food industry").[[105]](./Brisbane#cite_note-110)

Some of the largest companies headquartered in Brisbane, all among Australia's largest, include [Suncorp Group](./Suncorp_Group "Suncorp Group"), [Virgin Australia](./Virgin_Australia "Virgin Australia"), [Aurizon](./Aurizon "Aurizon"), [Bank of Queensland](./Bank_of_Queensland "Bank of Queensland"), [Flight Centre](./Flight_Centre "Flight Centre"), [Great Southern Bank](./Great_Southern_Bank "Great Southern Bank"), [Australian Retirement Trust](./Australian_Retirement_Trust "Australian Retirement Trust"), [Domino's Pizza Enterprises](./Domino's_Pizza_Enterprises "Domino's Pizza Enterprises"), [Star Entertainment Group](./Star_Entertainment_Group "Star Entertainment Group"), [ALS](./ALS_Limited "ALS Limited"), [TechnologyOne](./TechnologyOne "TechnologyOne"), [NEXTDC](./NEXTDC "NEXTDC"), [Super Retail Group](./Super_Retail_Group "Super Retail Group"), [New Hope Coal](./New_Hope_Coal "New Hope Coal"), [Jumbo Interactive](./Jumbo_Interactive "Jumbo Interactive"), [National Storage](./National_Storage "National Storage"), [Collins Foods](./Collins_Foods "Collins Foods"), and [Boeing Australia](./Boeing_Australia "Boeing Australia").[[106]](./Brisbane#cite_note-111) Most major Australian companies, as well as numerous international companies, have contact offices in Brisbane.

Brisbane throughout its history has been one of Australia's most important [seaport](./Seaport "Seaport") cities. The [Port of Brisbane](./Port_of_Brisbane "Port of Brisbane") is located at the Brisbane River's mouth on [Moreton Bay](./Moreton_Bay "Moreton Bay") and on the adjacent Fisherman's Island, created by means of [land reclamation](./Land_reclamation "Land reclamation"). It is the 3rd busiest port in Australia for value of goods.[[107]](./Brisbane#cite_note-Port_Technology-112) [Container freight](./Containerization "Containerization"), sugar, grain, coal and bulk liquids are the major exports. Most of the port facilities are less than three decades old and some are built on reclaimed [mangroves](./Mangrove "Mangrove") and [wetlands](./Wetlands "Wetlands"). The Port is a part of the [Australia TradeCoast](./Australia_TradeCoast "Australia TradeCoast"), which includes the [Brisbane Airport](./Brisbane_Airport "Brisbane Airport") along with large industrial estates located along both banks at the mouth of the Brisbane River.[[108]](./Brisbane#cite_note-TradeCoast-113)

White-collar industries include information technology, [financial services](./Financial_services "Financial services"), higher education and [public sector](./Public_sector "Public sector") administration generally concentrated in and around the central business district and satellite hubs located in the inner suburbs such as [South Brisbane](./South_Brisbane "South Brisbane"), [Fortitude Valley](./Fortitude_Valley "Fortitude Valley"), [Spring Hill](./Spring_Hill,_Queensland "Spring Hill, Queensland"), [Milton](./Milton,_Queensland "Milton, Queensland"), and [Toowong](./Toowong "Toowong"), [Upper Mount Gravatt](./Upper_Mount_Gravatt,_Queensland "Upper Mount Gravatt, Queensland") could be considered as a 2nd CBD to the city.

Blue-collar industries, including petroleum refining, [stevedoring](./Stevedoring "Stevedoring"), paper milling, [metalworking](./Metalworking "Metalworking") and [QR](./Queensland_Rail "Queensland Rail") railway workshops, tend to be located on the lower reaches of the Brisbane River proximal to the [Port of Brisbane](./Port_of_Brisbane "Port of Brisbane") and in new industrial zones on the urban fringe.

[Tourism](./Tourism_in_Brisbane "Tourism in Brisbane") is an important part of the Brisbane economy, both in its own right and as a gateway to other areas of Queensland,[[109]](./Brisbane#cite_note-114) as is [international education](./International_students "International students"), with over 95,000 international students enrolled in universities and other tertiary education institutions in the central [City of Brisbane](./City_of_Brisbane "City of Brisbane") [local government area](./Local_government_area "Local government area") alone in 2018.[[110]](./Brisbane#cite_note-choosebrisbane.com.au-115)

### Retail

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d1/Queen_Street_Mall%2C_Brisbane_in_Jan_2020.jpg/250px-Queen_Street_Mall%2C_Brisbane_in_Jan_2020.jpg)](./File:Queen_Street_Mall,_Brisbane_in_Jan_2020.jpg)

The [Queen Street Mall](./Queen_Street_Mall "Queen Street Mall"), Queensland's largest pedestrian mall

[Retail](./Retail "Retail") in the [CBD](./Brisbane_central_business_district "Brisbane central business district") is centred around the [Queen Street Mall](./Queen_Street_Mall "Queen Street Mall"), which is Queensland's largest pedestrian mall. [Shopping centres](./Shopping_mall "Shopping mall") in the CBD include [Uptown (formerly the Myer Centre)](./Uptown,_Brisbane "Uptown, Brisbane"), the [Wintergarden](./Wintergarden,_Brisbane "Wintergarden, Brisbane"), [MacArthur Central](./MacArthur_Central "MacArthur Central") and [QueensPlaza](./QueensPlaza "QueensPlaza"), with the last of these along with [Edward Street](./Edward_Street,_Brisbane "Edward Street, Brisbane") forming the city's focus for [luxury brands](./Luxury_goods "Luxury goods"). There are historical shopping arcades at [Brisbane Arcade](./Brisbane_Arcade "Brisbane Arcade") and [Tattersalls Arcade](./Tattersalls_Club "Tattersalls Club"). Suburbs adjacent to the CBD such as [Fortitude Valley](./Fortitude_Valley "Fortitude Valley") (particularly [James Street](./Fortitude_Valley,_Queensland#Commercial_area "Fortitude Valley, Queensland")), [South Brisbane](./South_Brisbane "South Brisbane") and [West End](./West_End,_Queensland "West End, Queensland") are also a major inner-city retail hubs.

Outside of the inner-city, retail is focused on indoor [shopping centres](./Shopping_mall "Shopping mall"), including numerous regional shopping centres along with six super regional shopping centres, all of which are [among Australia's largest](./List_of_largest_shopping_centres_in_Australia "List of largest shopping centres in Australia"), namely: [Westfield Chermside](./Westfield_Chermside "Westfield Chermside") in the north; [Westfield Mt Gravatt](./Westfield_Mt_Gravatt "Westfield Mt Gravatt") in the south; [Westfield Carindale](./Westfield_Carindale "Westfield Carindale") in the east; [Indooroopilly Shopping Centre](./Indooroopilly_Shopping_Centre "Indooroopilly Shopping Centre") in the west; [Westfield North Lakes](./Westfield_North_Lakes "Westfield North Lakes") in the outer-north; and [Logan Hyperdome](./Logan_Hyperdome "Logan Hyperdome") in the outer-south. Brisbane's major [factory outlet centres](./Outlet_store "Outlet store") are the [Direct Factory Outlets](./Direct_Factory_Outlet "Direct Factory Outlet") at [Skygate](./DFO_Brisbane "DFO Brisbane") and [Jindalee](./DFO_Jindalee "DFO Jindalee").

The 100-hectare (250-acre) [Brisbane Markets](./Rocklea#Fruit_and_vegetable_market "Rocklea") at [Rocklea](./Rocklea "Rocklea") are Brisbane's largest [wholesale markets](./Wholesale_markets "Wholesale markets"), whilst smaller markets operate at numerous locations throughout the city including [South Bank Parklands](./South_Bank_Parklands "South Bank Parklands"), [Davies Park](./Davies_Park "Davies Park") in [West End, Queensland](./West_End,_Queensland "West End, Queensland"), and the Eat Street Markets at [Hamilton](./Hamilton,_Queensland "Hamilton, Queensland").

Culture and sport
-----------------

Main article: [Culture of Brisbane](./Culture_of_Brisbane "Culture of Brisbane")

See also: [Popular entertainment in Brisbane](./Popular_entertainment_in_Brisbane "Popular entertainment in Brisbane"), [Brisbane punk rock](./Brisbane_punk_rock "Brisbane punk rock"), and [Cuisine of Brisbane](./Cuisine_of_Brisbane "Cuisine of Brisbane")

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2c/%22Under_the_Jacaranda%22_by_R_Godfrey_Rivers_-_Queensland_Art_Gallery_-_Joy_of_Museums_-_2.jpg/250px-%22Under_the_Jacaranda%22_by_R_Godfrey_Rivers_-_Queensland_Art_Gallery_-_Joy_of_Museums_-_2.jpg)](./File:"Under_the_Jacaranda"_by_R_Godfrey_Rivers_-_Queensland_Art_Gallery_-_Joy_of_Museums_-_2.jpg)

One of the most popular works in the [Queensland Art Gallery](./Queensland_Art_Gallery "Queensland Art Gallery")'s collection, *Under The Jacaranda* (1903) by [Richard Godfrey Rivers](./Richard_Godfrey_Rivers "Richard Godfrey Rivers") shows the first jacaranda tree planted in Brisbane.

Brisbane is home to several art galleries, the largest of which are the [Queensland Art Gallery](./Queensland_Art_Gallery "Queensland Art Gallery") and the [Queensland Gallery of Modern Art](./Queensland_Gallery_of_Modern_Art "Queensland Gallery of Modern Art") (GOMA), which is the largest modern art gallery in Australia. GOMA holds the Asia Pacific Triennial (APT) which focuses on contemporary art from the Asia and Pacific in a variety of media from painting to video work. In addition, its size enables the gallery to exhibit particularly large shows.

GOMA houses the [Australian Cinémathèque](./Australian_Cinémathèque "Australian Cinémathèque"), a dedicated film facility offering a diverse program of screenings, including international cinema, influential filmmakers, rare prints, restorations and silent films with a live musical accompaniment. Screenings take place Wednesday and Friday nights, as well as matinees on weekends. Most screenings are free admission.[[111]](./Brisbane#cite_note-116)

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f2/QPAC_Exterior.jpg/250px-QPAC_Exterior.jpg)](./File:QPAC_Exterior.jpg)

[Queensland Performing Arts Centre](./Queensland_Performing_Arts_Centre "Queensland Performing Arts Centre")

Dramatic and musical theatre performances are held at the multiple large theatres located at [Queensland Performing Arts Centre](./Queensland_Performing_Arts_Centre "Queensland Performing Arts Centre") (QPAC). The [Brisbane Powerhouse](./Brisbane_Powerhouse "Brisbane Powerhouse") in [New Farm](./New_Farm "New Farm") and the [Judith Wright Arts Centre](./Judith_Wright_Arts_Centre "Judith Wright Arts Centre") in [Fortitude Valley](./Fortitude_Valley "Fortitude Valley") also feature diverse programs featuring exhibitions and festivals of visual art, music and dance. Brisbane is also home to numerous small theatres including the [Brisbane Arts Theatre](./Brisbane_Arts_Theatre "Brisbane Arts Theatre") in [Petrie Terrace](./Petrie_Terrace "Petrie Terrace"), the [La Boite Theatre Company](./La_Boite_Theatre_Company "La Boite Theatre Company") which performs at the [Roundhouse Theatre](./Roundhouse_Theatre "Roundhouse Theatre") at [Kelvin Grove](./Kelvin_Grove,_Queensland "Kelvin Grove, Queensland"), the [Twelfth Night Theatre](./Twelfth_Night_Theatre "Twelfth Night Theatre") at [Bowen Hills](./Bowen_Hills "Bowen Hills"), the [Metro Arts Theatre](./Metro_Arts_Theatre "Metro Arts Theatre") in [Edward Street](./Edward_Street,_Brisbane "Edward Street, Brisbane"), and the Queensland Theatre Company's [Bille Brown Theatre](./Bille_Brown_Theatre "Bille Brown Theatre") in [West End](./West_End,_Queensland "West End, Queensland").

The [Queensland Performing Arts Centre](./Queensland_Performing_Arts_Centre "Queensland Performing Arts Centre") (QPAC) at [South Bank](./South_Bank,_Queensland "South Bank, Queensland"), consists of the Lyric Theatre, the Concert Hall, the Cremorne Theatre and the Playhouse Theatre and is home to the [Queensland Ballet](./Queensland_Ballet "Queensland Ballet"), [Opera Queensland](./Opera_Queensland "Opera Queensland"), the [Queensland Theatre Company](./Queensland_Theatre_Company "Queensland Theatre Company"), and the [Queensland Symphony Orchestra](./Queensland_Symphony_Orchestra "Queensland Symphony Orchestra"). The [Queensland Conservatorium](./Queensland_Conservatorium "Queensland Conservatorium"), a musical conservatorium in which professional music companies and conservatorium students also stage performances, is located within the [South Bank Parklands](./South_Bank_Parklands "South Bank Parklands"). Numerous choirs present performances across the city annually. These choirs include the Brisbane Chorale, Queensland Choir, Brisbane Chamber Choir, Canticum Chamber Choir, ChoirWorks, Imogen Children's Chorale, and [Brisbane Birralee Voices](./Brisbane_Birralee_Voices "Brisbane Birralee Voices").

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/fe/Go_between_bridge.jpg/250px-Go_between_bridge.jpg)](./File:Go_between_bridge.jpg)

[Go Between Bridge](./Go_Between_Bridge "Go Between Bridge"), named after local jangle pop band [the Go-Betweens](./The_Go-Betweens "The Go-Betweens")

Brisbane's live music scene is diverse and its history is often intertwined with social unrest and authoritarian politics, as retold by journalist Andrew Stafford in [*Pig City: From The Saints to Savage Garden*](./Pig_City_(music_festival)#Pig_City_(book) "Pig City (music festival)"). Popular live music venues, including pubs and clubs, can be found within both the CBD and [Fortitude Valley](./Fortitude_Valley "Fortitude Valley").[[112]](./Brisbane#cite_note-117)[[113]](./Brisbane#cite_note-118) The [Brisbane Entertainment Centre](./Brisbane_Entertainment_Centre "Brisbane Entertainment Centre") at [Boondall](./Boondall "Boondall") hosts many musical concerts, with some of the largest being held at [Lang Park](./Lang_Park "Lang Park"). Musicians from Brisbane include the [Bee Gees](./Bee_Gees "Bee Gees") (raised in [Redcliffe](./Redcliffe,_Queensland "Redcliffe, Queensland") and [Cribb Island](./Cribb_Island "Cribb Island")), [the Saints](./The_Saints_(Australian_band) "The Saints (Australian band)") (based in Brisbane since 1974, one of the first [punk rock](./Punk_rock "Punk rock") bands), [the Go-Betweens](./The_Go-Betweens "The Go-Betweens") (after whom Brisbane's [Go Between Bridge](./Go_Between_Bridge "Go Between Bridge") is named, and whose songs and albums, such as *[Spring Hill Fair](./Spring_Hill_Fair "Spring Hill Fair")*, reflect the attitudes of 1980s Brisbane), [Savage Garden](./Savage_Garden "Savage Garden"), [Powderfinger](./Powderfinger "Powderfinger") (who met at [Brisbane Grammar School](./Brisbane_Grammar_School "Brisbane Grammar School") and the [University of Queensland](./University_of_Queensland "University of Queensland")), and [the Veronicas](./The_Veronicas "The Veronicas") (born and raised in [Albany Creek](./Albany_Creek "Albany Creek")). The city is featured in music including the Saints' "[Brisbane (Security City)](./Prehistoric_Sounds "Prehistoric Sounds")" (1978); [the Stranglers](./The_Stranglers "The Stranglers")' "[Nuclear Device](./Nuclear_Device_(The_Wizard_of_Aus) "Nuclear Device (The Wizard of Aus)")" (1979) about [Joh Bjelke-Petersen](./Joh_Bjelke-Petersen "Joh Bjelke-Petersen"); [Midnight Oil](./Midnight_Oil "Midnight Oil")'s single "[Dreamworld](./Dreamworld_(Midnight_Oil_song) "Dreamworld (Midnight Oil song)")" (1987); and Powderfinger's album *[Vulture Street](./Vulture_Street_(album) "Vulture Street (album)")* (2003).

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/cc/Exterior_of_the_State_Library_of_Queensland%2C_2021.jpg/250px-Exterior_of_the_State_Library_of_Queensland%2C_2021.jpg)](./File:Exterior_of_the_State_Library_of_Queensland,_2021.jpg)

[State Library of Queensland](./State_Library_of_Queensland "State Library of Queensland")

Prominent writers from Brisbane include [David Malouf](./David_Malouf "David Malouf") (whose 1975 novel *Johnno* is set in Brisbane and at [Brisbane Grammar School](./Brisbane_Grammar_School "Brisbane Grammar School") during [World War II](./World_War_II "World War II")), [Nick Earls](./Nick_Earls "Nick Earls") (whose 1996 novel *Zigzag Street* is set at Zigzag Street in [Red Hill](./Red_Hill,_Queensland "Red Hill, Queensland")), and [Li Cunxin](./Li_Cunxin "Li Cunxin"), author of [Mao's Last Dancer](./Mao's_Last_Dancer_(book) "Mao's Last Dancer (book)") and artistic director of the Queensland Ballet. *Brisbane* is a 2018 novel by Russian writer [Eugene Vodolazkin](./Eugene_Vodolazkin "Eugene Vodolazkin"). In the novel, the city serves as a metaphor of the [promised land](./Promised_land "Promised land") for the protagonist. The [State Library of Queensland](./State_Library_of_Queensland "State Library of Queensland"), the state's largest library, is located at the [Queensland Cultural Centre](./Queensland_Cultural_Centre "Queensland Cultural Centre").

Since the late 20th century, numerous [films have been shot in Brisbane](./List_of_films_shot_in_Brisbane "List of films shot in Brisbane"), and the popular children's animated television series *[Bluey](./Bluey_(TV_series) "Bluey (TV series)")* is produced and set in Brisbane.

Brisbane is home to over 6,000 restaurants and dining establishments,[[114]](./Brisbane#cite_note-119) with [outdoor dining](./Outdoor_dining "Outdoor dining") featuring prominently. The most popular cuisines by number of dining establishments are [Japanese](./Japanese_cuisine "Japanese cuisine"),[[115]](./Brisbane#cite_note-120) [Chinese](./Chinese_cuisine "Chinese cuisine"),[[116]](./Brisbane#cite_note-121) [Modern Australian](./Modern_Australian "Modern Australian"),[[117]](./Brisbane#cite_note-122) [Italian](./Italian_cuisine "Italian cuisine"),[[118]](./Brisbane#cite_note-123) [American](./American_cuisine "American cuisine"),[[119]](./Brisbane#cite_note-124) [Indian](./Indian_cuisine "Indian cuisine"),[[120]](./Brisbane#cite_note-125) and [Vietnamese](./Vietnamese_cuisine "Vietnamese cuisine").[[121]](./Brisbane#cite_note-126) [Moreton Bay bugs](./Moreton_Bay_bug "Moreton Bay bug"), less commonly known as flathead lobsters, are an ingredient named for the Brisbane region and which feature commonly in [the city's cuisine](./Cuisine_of_Brisbane "Cuisine of Brisbane"), along with [macadamia nuts](./Macadamia_nuts "Macadamia nuts"), also native to the region.

### Annual events

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b1/Brisbane_Riverfire_2009_Bridge.jpg/250px-Brisbane_Riverfire_2009_Bridge.jpg)](./File:Brisbane_Riverfire_2009_Bridge.jpg)

[Riverfire](./Brisbane_Festival "Brisbane Festival") at the [Story Bridge](./Story_Bridge "Story Bridge")

The Royal Queensland Exhibition (known locally as the [Ekka](./Ekka "Ekka")), an agricultural exhibition held each August at the [Brisbane Showgrounds](./Brisbane_Showgrounds "Brisbane Showgrounds") in [Bowen Hills](./Bowen_Hills "Bowen Hills"), is the longest-running major annual event held in Brisbane. A public holiday is held for each [local government area](./Local_government_area "Local government area") across Brisbane to enable widespread public attendance.

The [Brisbane Festival](./Brisbane_Festival "Brisbane Festival") is held each September at [South Bank Parklands](./South_Bank_Parklands "South Bank Parklands"), the [CBD](./Brisbane_central_business_district "Brisbane central business district") and surrounding areas. It includes [Riverfire](./Riverfire "Riverfire"), one of the Queensland's largest annual fireworks displays, which is attended by hundreds of thousands of residents.

The [Brisbane International Film Festival](./Brisbane_International_Film_Festival "Brisbane International Film Festival") (BIFF) is held in July/August each year in a variety of venues around Brisbane. BIFF features new films and retrospectives by domestic and international filmmakers along with seminars and awards.

The Brisbane Portrait Prize is an annual arts event held formerly at the [Brisbane Powerhouse](./Brisbane_Powerhouse "Brisbane Powerhouse") and from 2024, at the [State Library of Queensland](./State_Library_of_Queensland "State Library of Queensland").[[122]](./Brisbane#cite_note-127) Sitters for the portrait must have a connection to Brisbane city.[[123]](./Brisbane#cite_note-128)

The [Buddha Birth Day](./Buddha's_Birthday "Buddha's Birthday") festival at South Bank parklands attracts over 200,000 visitors each year,[[124]](./Brisbane#cite_note-129)[[125]](./Brisbane#cite_note-130) and is the largest event of its type in Australia.

There are also many smaller community events such as the [Paniyiri Greek Festival](./Paniyiri_Greek_Festival "Paniyiri Greek Festival") (held over two days in May), the Brisbane Medieval Fayre and Tournament (held each June), the [Bridge to Brisbane](./Bridge_to_Brisbane "Bridge to Brisbane") charity fun run, the [Anywhere Festival](./Anywhere_Festival "Anywhere Festival") and the [Caxton Street Seafood and Wine Festival](./Caxton_Street_Seafood_and_Wine_Festival "Caxton Street Seafood and Wine Festival").

Major events are often held at the 171 km2 (66 sq mi) [Brisbane Convention & Exhibition Centre](./Brisbane_Convention_&_Exhibition_Centre "Brisbane Convention & Exhibition Centre") in [South Brisbane](./South_Brisbane "South Brisbane").

Brisbane has hosted several major sporting events including the [1982 Commonwealth Games](./1982_Commonwealth_Games "1982 Commonwealth Games") and the [2001 Goodwill Games](./2001_Goodwill_Games "2001 Goodwill Games"), as well as events during the [1987 Rugby World Cup](./1987_Rugby_World_Cup "1987 Rugby World Cup"), [1992 Cricket World Cup](./1992_Cricket_World_Cup "1992 Cricket World Cup"), [2000 Sydney Olympics](./2000_Sydney_Olympics "2000 Sydney Olympics"), [2003 Rugby World Cup](./2003_Rugby_World_Cup "2003 Rugby World Cup"), [2008 Rugby League World Cup](./2008_Rugby_League_World_Cup "2008 Rugby League World Cup"), [2015 Asian Cup](./2015_Asian_Cup "2015 Asian Cup"), [2017 Rugby League World Cup](./2017_Rugby_League_World_Cup "2017 Rugby League World Cup"), [2018 Commonwealth Games](./2018_Commonwealth_Games "2018 Commonwealth Games") and the [2023 Women's World Cup](./2023_FIFA_Women's_World_Cup "2023 FIFA Women's World Cup").

It will host the [2032 Summer Olympics](./2032_Summer_Olympics "2032 Summer Olympics") and [2032 Summer Paralympics](./2032_Summer_Paralympics "2032 Summer Paralympics").[[126]](./Brisbane#cite_note-auto2-131)[[127]](./Brisbane#cite_note-auto3-132)[[128]](./Brisbane#cite_note-133) The city also bid for the [1992 Summer Olympics](./1992_Summer_Olympics "1992 Summer Olympics") but lost to [Barcelona](./Barcelona "Barcelona"). It holds the [Brisbane International](./Brisbane_International "Brisbane International") tennis competition every year.

Brisbane is represented by the [rugby league](./Rugby_league "Rugby league") teams the [Brisbane Broncos](./Brisbane_Broncos "Brisbane Broncos") and [Dolphins](./Dolphins_(NRL) "Dolphins (NRL)"), who play in the [National Rugby League](./National_Rugby_League "National Rugby League"), and is also home to the [Queensland Maroons](./Queensland_Maroons "Queensland Maroons"), who play in the [State of Origin series](./State_of_Origin_series "State of Origin series"). In [rugby union](./Rugby_union "Rugby union") the city hosts the [Queensland Reds](./Queensland_Reds "Queensland Reds") who play in the [Super Rugby](./Super_Rugby "Super Rugby") competition. Brisbane also hosts a professional [Australian rules football](./Australian_rules_football "Australian rules football") team, the [Brisbane Lions](./Brisbane_Lions "Brisbane Lions"), who play in the [Australian Football League](./Australian_Football_League "Australian Football League"); as well as an [A-League](./A-League "A-League") soccer team, the [Brisbane Roar FC](./Brisbane_Roar_FC "Brisbane Roar FC").

In [Cricket](./Cricket "Cricket") the city hosts the [Brisbane Heat](./Brisbane_Heat "Brisbane Heat") who play in the [Big Bash League](./Big_Bash_League "Big Bash League") and the [Queensland Bulls](./Queensland_Bulls "Queensland Bulls") who play in the [Sheffield Shield](./Sheffield_Shield "Sheffield Shield") and the [Ryobi One Day Cup](./Ryobi_One_Day_Cup "Ryobi One Day Cup"). Other Brisbane sports teams include a [basketball](./Basketball "Basketball") team, the [Brisbane Bullets](./Brisbane_Bullets "Brisbane Bullets"); a [baseball](./Baseball "Baseball") team, the [Brisbane Bandits](./Brisbane_Bandits "Brisbane Bandits"); a [netball](./Netball "Netball") team, the [Queensland Firebirds](./Queensland_Firebirds "Queensland Firebirds"); a [field hockey](./Field_hockey "Field hockey") team, the [Brisbane Blaze](./Brisbane_Blaze "Brisbane Blaze"); and water polo teams the [Brisbane Barracudas](./Brisbane_Barracudas "Brisbane Barracudas") and [Queensland Breakers](./Queensland_Breakers "Queensland Breakers").

The city's major stadiums and sporting venues include [the Gabba](./The_Gabba "The Gabba") (a 37,000 seat round stadium at [Woolloongabba](./Woolloongabba "Woolloongabba")), [Lang Park](./Lang_Park "Lang Park") (a 52,500 seat rectangular stadium at [Milton](./Milton,_Queensland "Milton, Queensland") also known by its corporate name Suncorp Stadium), [Ballymore Stadium](./Ballymore_Stadium "Ballymore Stadium"), the [Queensland Sport and Athletics Centre](./Queensland_Sport_and_Athletics_Centre "Queensland Sport and Athletics Centre"), the [Sleeman Centre](./Sleeman_Centre_(Brisbane) "Sleeman Centre (Brisbane)") (swimming), the [State Tennis Centre](./Tennyson_Tennis_Centre "Tennyson Tennis Centre"), the [Eagle Farm Racecourse](./Eagle_Farm_Racecourse "Eagle Farm Racecourse"), and the [Doomben Racecourse](./Doomben_Racecourse "Doomben Racecourse"). The city is also home to numerous golf courses, with the largest being the Indooroopilly Golf Club at [Indooroopilly, Queensland](./Indooroopilly,_Queensland "Indooroopilly, Queensland"), the [Brookwater Golf and Country Club](./Brookwater_Golf_and_Spa_Resort "Brookwater Golf and Spa Resort") at [Brookwater](./Brookwater "Brookwater"), Nudgee Golf Club at [Nudgee](./Nudgee,_Queensland "Nudgee, Queensland"), the Keperra Country Golf Club at [Keperra](./Keperra "Keperra"), and the [Royal Queensland Golf Club](./Royal_Queensland_Golf_Club "Royal Queensland Golf Club") at [Eagle Farm](./Eagle_Farm "Eagle Farm").

In addition to its flagship sport franchises, Brisbane and its regions and suburbs have numerous teams in secondary leagues including the [Intrust Super Cup](./Intrust_Super_Cup "Intrust Super Cup"), [National Rugby Championship](./National_Rugby_Championship "National Rugby Championship"), [Queensland Premier Rugby](./Queensland_Premier_Rugby "Queensland Premier Rugby"), [National Premier League Queensland](./National_Premier_League_Queensland "National Premier League Queensland"), [National Basketball League](./National_Basketball_League_(Australia) "National Basketball League (Australia)"), [ANZ Championship](./ANZ_Championship "ANZ Championship"), [Australian Baseball League](./Australian_Baseball_League "Australian Baseball League"), [Hockey One](./Hockey_One "Hockey One"), [National Water Polo League](./Australian_National_Water_Polo_League "Australian National Water Polo League"), and [F-League](./F-League "F-League").

Tourism and recreation
----------------------

Main article: [Tourism in Brisbane](./Tourism_in_Brisbane "Tourism in Brisbane")

Tourism plays a major role in Brisbane's economy, being the third-most popular destination for international tourists after Sydney and Melbourne.[[129]](./Brisbane#cite_note-134) Popular tourist and recreation areas near inner city Brisbane include the [South Bank Parklands](./South_Bank_Parklands "South Bank Parklands") (including the [Wheel of Brisbane](./Wheel_of_Brisbane "Wheel of Brisbane")), the [City Botanic Gardens](./City_Botanic_Gardens "City Botanic Gardens"), [Roma Street Parkland](./Roma_Street_Parkland "Roma Street Parkland"), [New Farm Park](./New_Farm_Park "New Farm Park"), the [Howard Smith Wharves](./Howard_Smith_Wharves "Howard Smith Wharves"), [Queens Wharf](./Queen's_Wharf,_Brisbane "Queen's Wharf, Brisbane") & Casino, the [Teneriffe woolstores precinct](./Teneriffe,_Queensland "Teneriffe, Queensland"), [Fortitude Valley](./Fortitude_Valley "Fortitude Valley") (including [James Street](./Fortitude_Valley,_Queensland#Commercial_area "Fortitude Valley, Queensland") and [Chinatown](./Chinatown,_Brisbane "Chinatown, Brisbane")), [West End](./West_End,_Queensland "West End, Queensland"), [City Hall](./Brisbane_City_Hall "Brisbane City Hall") (including the [Museum of Brisbane](./Museum_of_Brisbane "Museum of Brisbane")), the [Parliament of Queensland](./Parliament_of_Queensland "Parliament of Queensland"), the [Story Bridge](./Story_Bridge "Story Bridge") and bridge climb; [St John's Cathedral](./St_John's_Cathedral_(Brisbane) "St John's Cathedral (Brisbane)"), [ANZAC Square](./ANZAC_Square,_Brisbane "ANZAC Square, Brisbane") and the [Queensland Cultural Centre](./Queensland_Cultural_Centre "Queensland Cultural Centre") (including the [Queensland Museum](./Queensland_Museum "Queensland Museum"), [Queensland Performing Arts Centre](./Queensland_Performing_Arts_Centre "Queensland Performing Arts Centre"), [Queensland Art Gallery](./Queensland_Art_Gallery "Queensland Art Gallery"), the [Gallery of Modern Art](./Gallery_of_Modern_Art,_Brisbane "Gallery of Modern Art, Brisbane") and the [State Library of Queensland](./State_Library_of_Queensland "State Library of Queensland")), the [Kangaroo Point Cliffs](./Kangaroo_Point_Cliffs "Kangaroo Point Cliffs") and park, and the [Queensland Maritime Museum](./Queensland_Maritime_Museum "Queensland Maritime Museum").

Away from the inner city, Brisbane has a number of tourist attractions and destinations such as the, [University of Queensland](./University_of_Queensland "University of Queensland") in St Lucia, Sirromet Winery at [Mount Cotton](./Mount_Cotton "Mount Cotton"), [Tangalooma](./Tangalooma "Tangalooma") on Moreton Island, [Lone Pine Koala Sanctuary](./Lone_Pine_Koala_Sanctuary "Lone Pine Koala Sanctuary") in Fig Tree Pocket, Eat Street (food night markets) at Northshore Hamilton, [Fort Lytton](./Fort_Lytton "Fort Lytton"), and [Mount Coot-tha](./Mount_Coot-tha "Mount Coot-tha") (including the [Mount Coot-tha Reserve](./Mount_Coot-tha_Forest "Mount Coot-tha Forest"), [Mount Coot-tha Lookout](./Mount_Coot-tha_Lookout "Mount Coot-tha Lookout"), the [Mount Coot-tha Botanic Gardens](./Mount_Coot-tha_Botanic_Gardens "Mount Coot-tha Botanic Gardens") and the [Sir Thomas Brisbane Planetarium](./Sir_Thomas_Brisbane_Planetarium "Sir Thomas Brisbane Planetarium")) is a popular recreational attraction for hiking and bushwalking.

Brisbane is notable for its [Brisbane Riverwalk](./Brisbane_Riverwalk "Brisbane Riverwalk") network, which runs along much of the [Brisbane River](./Brisbane_River "Brisbane River") foreshore throughout the inner-city area, with the longest span running between [Newstead](./Newstead,_Queensland "Newstead, Queensland") and [Toowong](./Toowong "Toowong"). Another popular stretch runs beneath the [Kangaroo Point Cliffs](./Kangaroo_Point_Cliffs "Kangaroo Point Cliffs") between [South Brisbane](./South_Brisbane "South Brisbane") and [Kangaroo Point](./Kangaroo_Point,_Queensland "Kangaroo Point, Queensland"). Several spans of the Riverwalk are built out over the Brisbane River. Brisbane also has over 27 km (17 mi) of bicycle pathways, mostly surrounding the [Brisbane River](./Brisbane_River "Brisbane River") and city centre. Other popular recreation activities include the [Story Bridge](./Story_Bridge "Story Bridge") adventure climb and rock climbing at the [Kangaroo Point Cliffs](./Kangaroo_Point_Cliffs "Kangaroo Point Cliffs").

[Moreton Bay](./Moreton_Bay "Moreton Bay") and its [marine park](./Moreton_Bay_Marine_Park "Moreton Bay Marine Park") is also a major attraction, and its three primary islands [Moreton Island](./Moreton_Island "Moreton Island"), [North Stradbroke Island](./North_Stradbroke_Island "North Stradbroke Island") and [Bribie Island](./Bribie_Island "Bribie Island"), accessible by ferry, contain popular surf beaches and resorts. [Tangalooma](./Tangalooma "Tangalooma") resort on Moreton Island is popular for its nightly wild dolphin feeding attraction, and for operating Australia's longest running whale watching cruises. The [Fort Lytton National Park](./Fort_Lytton_National_Park "Fort Lytton National Park") including a [colonial defence fort](./Fort_Lytton_Historic_Military_Precinct "Fort Lytton Historic Military Precinct") and museum is also a historical bayside attraction. Beachside suburbs such as those on the [Redcliffe Peninsula](./Redcliffe_Peninsula "Redcliffe Peninsula"), as well as [Shorncliffe](./Shorncliffe,_Queensland "Shorncliffe, Queensland"), [Sandgate](./Sandgate,_Queensland "Sandgate, Queensland"), [Wynnum](./Wynnum "Wynnum"), [Manly](./Manly,_Queensland "Manly, Queensland") and [Wellington Point](./Wellington_Point "Wellington Point") are also popular attractions for their bayside beaches, piers, and infrastructure for boating, sailing, fishing and [kitesurfing](./Kitesurfing "Kitesurfing").

There are many [national parks](./National_park "National park") surrounding the Brisbane metropolitan area which are popular recreational attractions for hiking and bushwalking. The [D'Aguilar National Park](./D'Aguilar_National_Park "D'Aguilar National Park") runs along the northwest of the metropolitan area in the [D'Aguilar Range](./D'Aguilar_Range "D'Aguilar Range"), and contains popular bushwalking and hiking peaks at [Mount Nebo](./Mount_Nebo_(Queensland) "Mount Nebo (Queensland)"), [Camp Mountain](./Camp_Mountain "Camp Mountain"), [Mount Pleasant](./Mount_Pleasant,_Queensland_(Moreton_Bay) "Mount Pleasant, Queensland (Moreton Bay)"), [Mount Glorious](./Mount_Glorious "Mount Glorious"), [Mount Samson](./Mount_Samson "Mount Samson") and [Mount Mee](./Mount_Mee "Mount Mee"). The [Glass House Mountains National Park](./Glass_House_Mountains_National_Park "Glass House Mountains National Park") is located to the north of the metropolitan area in the [Glass House Mountains](./Glass_House_Mountains,_Queensland "Glass House Mountains, Queensland") between it and that of the [Sunshine Coast](./Sunshine_Coast,_Queensland "Sunshine Coast, Queensland"). The [Tamborine National Park](./Tamborine_National_Park "Tamborine National Park") at [Tamborine Mountain](./Tamborine_Mountain "Tamborine Mountain") is located in the [Gold Coast hinterland](./Gold_Coast_hinterland "Gold Coast hinterland") to the south of the metropolitan area. [Moreton](./Moreton_Island "Moreton Island"), [North Stradbroke](./North_Stradbroke_Island "North Stradbroke Island") and [Bribie](./Bribie_Island "Bribie Island") islands are substantially covered by the [Moreton Island National Park](./Moreton_Island_National_Park "Moreton Island National Park"), [Naree Budjong Djara National Park](./Naree_Budjong_Djara_National_Park "Naree Budjong Djara National Park") and the [Bribie Island National Park](./Bribie_Island_National_Park "Bribie Island National Park") respectively. The [Boondall Wetlands](./Boondall_Wetlands "Boondall Wetlands") in the suburb of [Boondall](./Boondall "Boondall") are protected [mangrove](./Australian_mangroves "Australian mangroves") wetlands with floating walking trails.

Immediately to the south and north of Brisbane are the [Gold Coast](./Gold_Coast,_Queensland "Gold Coast, Queensland") and [Sunshine Coast](./Sunshine_Coast,_Queensland "Sunshine Coast, Queensland") respectively, which are home to several of Australia's most popular swimming and surfing beaches, and are popular day and weekend destinations for Brisbanites.

In 2015, a competition by travel guidebook *[Rough Guides](./Rough_Guides "Rough Guides")* saw Brisbane elected as one of the top ten most beautiful cities in the world, citing reasons such as "its winning combination of high-rise modern architecture, lush green spaces and the enormous Brisbane River that snakes its way through the centre before emptying itself into the azure Moreton Bay".[[130]](./Brisbane#cite_note-135)

Governance
----------

Main articles: [City of Brisbane](./City_of_Brisbane "City of Brisbane"), [Logan City](./Logan_City "Logan City"), [City of Moreton Bay](./City_of_Moreton_Bay "City of Moreton Bay"), [City of Ipswich](./City_of_Ipswich "City of Ipswich"), [Redland City](./Redland_City "Redland City"), [Scenic Rim Region](./Scenic_Rim_Region "Scenic Rim Region"), and [Government of Queensland](./Government_of_Queensland "Government of Queensland")

[City of Brisbane coat of arms](./Coat_of_arms_of_Brisbane "Coat of arms of Brisbane")

[City of Brisbane flag](./Flag_of_Brisbane "Flag of Brisbane")

Unlike other Australian capital cities, a large portion of the greater metropolitan area, or Greater Capital City Statistical Area (GCCSA) of Brisbane is controlled by a single [local government area](./Local_government_in_Australia "Local government in Australia"), the [City of Brisbane](./City_of_Brisbane "City of Brisbane"), which is the largest local government area (in terms of population and budget) in Australia, serving more than 40% of the GCCSA's population. It was formed by the merger of twenty smaller LGAs in 1925, and covers an area of 1,367 km2 (528 sq mi). The remainder of the metropolitan area falls into the LGAs of [Logan City](./Logan_City "Logan City") to the south, [City of Moreton Bay](./City_of_Moreton_Bay "City of Moreton Bay") in the northern suburbs, the [City of Ipswich](./City_of_Ipswich "City of Ipswich") to the south west, [Redland City](./Redland_City "Redland City") to the south east, and into the [Somerset](./Somerset_Region "Somerset Region"), [Scenic Rim](./Scenic_Rim_Region "Scenic Rim Region") and [Lockyer Valley](./Lockyer_Valley_Region "Lockyer Valley Region") regions on the urban periphery. Several of these are also among the nation's most populous LGAs.

Each LGA is governed under a similar structure, including a directly elected mayor (including the [Lord Mayor of Brisbane](./Lord_Mayor_of_Brisbane "Lord Mayor of Brisbane")), as well as a council composed of councillors representing geographical wards. [Brisbane City Hall](./Brisbane_City_Hall "Brisbane City Hall") is the seat of the [Brisbane City Council](./Brisbane_City_Council "Brisbane City Council"), the governing corporation of the City of Brisbane LGA, and the bulk of its executive offices are located at the [Brisbane Square](./Brisbane_Square "Brisbane Square") skyscraper.
