[Government House, Brisbane](./Government_House,_Brisbane "Government House, Brisbane"), home to the [Governor of Queensland](./Governor_of_Queensland "Governor of Queensland") and [Parliament House](./Parliament_House,_Brisbane "Parliament House, Brisbane"), home of the [Parliament of Queensland](./Parliament_of_Queensland "Parliament of Queensland")

As the capital city of [Queensland](./Queensland "Queensland"), Brisbane is home to the [Parliament of Queensland](./Parliament_of_Queensland "Parliament of Queensland") at [Parliament House](./Parliament_House,_Brisbane "Parliament House, Brisbane") at [Gardens Point](./Gardens_Point "Gardens Point") in the [CBD](./Brisbane_central_business_district "Brisbane central business district"), adjacent to [Old Government House](./Old_Government_House,_Queensland "Old Government House, Queensland"). Queensland's current [Government House](./Government_House,_Brisbane "Government House, Brisbane") is located in [Paddington](./Paddington,_Queensland "Paddington, Queensland"). The bulk of the state government's executive offices are located at the [1 William Street](./1_William_Street,_Brisbane "1 William Street, Brisbane") skyscraper. The Queensland [Supreme](./Supreme_Court_of_Queensland "Supreme Court of Queensland") and [District](./District_Court_of_Queensland "District Court of Queensland") courts are located at the [Queen Elizabeth II Courts of Law](./Queen_Elizabeth_II_Courts_of_Law,_Brisbane "Queen Elizabeth II Courts of Law, Brisbane") in [George Street](./George_Street,_Brisbane "George Street, Brisbane"), while the [Magistrates](./Magistrates_Court_of_Queensland "Magistrates Court of Queensland") court is located at the adjacent [Brisbane Magistrates Court building](./Brisbane_Magistrates_Court_building "Brisbane Magistrates Court building"). The various federal courts are located at the [Commonwealth Law Courts](./Commonwealth_Law_Courts "Commonwealth Law Courts") building on [North Quay](./North_Quay,_Brisbane "North Quay, Brisbane").

The [Australian Army](./Australian_Army "Australian Army")'s [Enoggera Barracks](./Enoggera_Barracks "Enoggera Barracks") is located in [Enoggera](./Enoggera,_Queensland "Enoggera, Queensland"), while the historic [Victoria Barracks](./Victoria_Barracks,_Brisbane "Victoria Barracks, Brisbane") in [Petrie Terrace](./Petrie_Terrace "Petrie Terrace") now hosts a military museum. The [Royal Australian Navy](./Royal_Australian_Navy "Royal Australian Navy")'s [HMAS Moreton](./HMAS_Moreton "HMAS Moreton") base is located at [Bulimba](./Bulimba "Bulimba"). The [Royal Australian Air Force](./Royal_Australian_Air_Force "Royal Australian Air Force")'s [RAAF Base Amberley](./RAAF_Base_Amberley "RAAF Base Amberley") is located in [Amberley](./Amberley,_Queensland "Amberley, Queensland") in the outer south-west of the metropolitan area.

Brisbane's largest prisons and correctional facilities, the [Brisbane Correctional Centre](./Brisbane_Correctional_Centre "Brisbane Correctional Centre"), [Brisbane Women's Correctional Centre](./Brisbane_Women's_Correctional_Centre "Brisbane Women's Correctional Centre"), [Arthur Gorrie Correctional Centre](./Arthur_Gorrie_Correctional_Centre "Arthur Gorrie Correctional Centre") and [Wolston Correctional Centre](./Wolston_Correctional_Centre "Wolston Correctional Centre") are located at [Wacol](./Wacol "Wacol"), while the city's main historical prison, the [Boggo Road Gaol](./Boggo_Road_Gaol "Boggo Road Gaol"), is now a museum.

### Politics

Greater Brisbane is represented by five [local government areas](./Local_government_areas_of_Queensland "Local government areas of Queensland") (LGAs): the [City of Brisbane](./City_of_Brisbane "City of Brisbane"), the [City of Ipswich](./City_of_Ipswich "City of Ipswich"), [Logan City](./Logan_City "Logan City"), the [City of Moreton Bay](./City_of_Moreton_Bay "City of Moreton Bay") and [Redland City](./Redland_City "Redland City"). The City of Brisbane is by far the largest and the most populated of the four, and [Brisbane City Council](./Brisbane_City_Council "Brisbane City Council") has 27 members: 26 councillors elected from single-member [wards](./Ward_(electoral_subdivision) "Ward (electoral subdivision)") and one directly elected [Lord Mayor](./Lord_Mayor_of_Brisbane "Lord Mayor of Brisbane").

In the [Queensland Legislative Assembly](./Queensland_Legislative_Assembly "Queensland Legislative Assembly"), Brisbane is represented by 41 single-member [electoral districts](./Electoral_districts_of_Queensland "Electoral districts of Queensland"). In the [House of Representatives](./Australian_House_of_Representatives "Australian House of Representatives"), Brisbane is represented by 13 single-member [electoral divisions](./Divisions_of_the_Australian_House_of_Representatives "Divisions of the Australian House of Representatives").

Brisbane has a diverse political climate. On the federal level, the [centre-left](./Centre-left "Centre-left") [Labor Party](./Australian_Labor_Party "Australian Labor Party") holds 11 Brisbane-based seats, while the [centre-right](./Centre-right "Centre-right") [Liberal National Party](./Liberal_National_Party_of_Queensland "Liberal National Party of Queensland") (LNP) and the [left-wing](./Left-wing "Left-wing") [Greens](./Australian_Greens "Australian Greens") each hold one ([Bowman](./Division_of_Bowman "Division of Bowman") and [Ryan](./Division_of_Ryan "Division of Ryan"), respectively). On the state level, Labor holds the vast majority of Brisbane-based seats, while the LNP holds nine and the Greens hold one ([Maiwar](./Electoral_district_of_Maiwar "Electoral district of Maiwar")). On the local level, LNP hold the Lord Mayoralty of Brisbane (with [Adrian Schrinner](./Adrian_Schrinner "Adrian Schrinner") as Lord Mayor) and 18 of the 26 wards of the City of Brisbane, while Labor holds five, the Greens hold two and an independent hold one ([Tennyson Ward](./Tennyson_Ward "Tennyson Ward")).

Three major universities are headquartered in Brisbane, namely:

* [Queensland University of Technology](./Queensland_University_of_Technology "Queensland University of Technology") (QUT), with campuses in the central business district ([Gardens Point](./Gardens_Point "Gardens Point")) and [Kelvin Grove](./Kelvin_Grove,_Queensland "Kelvin Grove, Queensland")
* [Griffith University](./Griffith_University "Griffith University") (GU), with campuses in [Nathan](./Nathan,_Queensland "Nathan, Queensland"), [Mount Gravatt](./Mount_Gravatt "Mount Gravatt"), [South Bank](./South_Bank,_Queensland "South Bank, Queensland") and [Meadowbrook](./Meadowbrook,_Queensland "Meadowbrook, Queensland")

Two other major universities, which are not headquartered in Brisbane, have multiple campuses in the Brisbane metropolitan area, namely:

* The [University of Southern Queensland](./University_of_Southern_Queensland "University of Southern Queensland") (USQ), with campuses in [Springfield](./Springfield,_Queensland "Springfield, Queensland") and [Ipswich](./Ipswich,_Queensland "Ipswich, Queensland") and the central business district
* The [University of the Sunshine Coast](./University_of_the_Sunshine_Coast "University of the Sunshine Coast") (USC), with campuses in [Petrie](./Petrie,_Queensland "Petrie, Queensland") and [Caboolture](./Caboolture "Caboolture")

Other universities which have campuses in Brisbane include the [Australian Catholic University](./Australian_Catholic_University "Australian Catholic University"), [Central Queensland University](./Central_Queensland_University "Central Queensland University") and [James Cook University](./James_Cook_University "James Cook University").

Brisbane is a major destination for [international students](./International_students "International students"), who constitute a large proportion of enrolments in Brisbane's universities and are important to the city's economy and real estate market. In 2018, there were over 95,000 international students enrolled in universities and other tertiary education institutions in the central City of Brisbane [local government area](./Local_government_area "Local government area") alone.[[110]](./Brisbane#cite_note-choosebrisbane.com.au-115) The majority of Brisbane's international students originate from China, India and other countries in the [Asia-Pacific](./Asia-Pacific "Asia-Pacific") region.[[134]](./Brisbane#cite_note-139)

There are biotechnology and research facilities at several universities in Brisbane, including the [Institute for Molecular Bioscience](./Institute_for_Molecular_Bioscience "Institute for Molecular Bioscience") and [CSIRO](./CSIRO "CSIRO") at the [University of Queensland](./University_of_Queensland "University of Queensland") and the [Institute of Health and Biomedical Innovation](./Institute_of_Health_and_Biomedical_Innovation "Institute of Health and Biomedical Innovation") at [Queensland University of Technology](./Queensland_University_of_Technology "Queensland University of Technology").[[135]](./Brisbane#cite_note-140)

There are three major [TAFE](./TAFE "TAFE") colleges in Brisbane; the [Brisbane North Institute of TAFE](./Brisbane_North_Institute_of_TAFE "Brisbane North Institute of TAFE"), the [Metropolitan South Institute of TAFE](./Metropolitan_South_Institute_of_TAFE "Metropolitan South Institute of TAFE"), and the [Southbank Institute of TAFE](./Southbank_Institute "Southbank Institute").[[136]](./Brisbane#cite_note-141) Brisbane is also home to numerous other independent tertiary providers, including the [Australian College of Natural Medicine](./Australian_College_of_Natural_Medicine "Australian College of Natural Medicine"), the [Queensland Theological College](./Queensland_Theological_College "Queensland Theological College"), the [Brisbane College of Theology](./Brisbane_College_of_Theology "Brisbane College of Theology"), [SAE Institute](./SAE_Institute "SAE Institute"), [Jschool: Journalism Education & Training](./Jschool:_Journalism_Education_&_Training "Jschool: Journalism Education & Training"), [JMC Academy](./JMC_Academy "JMC Academy"), and [American College](./American_College_(Brisbane) "American College (Brisbane)"), and the [Aboriginal Centre for the Performing Arts](./Aboriginal_Centre_for_the_Performing_Arts "Aboriginal Centre for the Performing Arts").

Many of Brisbane's [pre-school](./Pre-school "Pre-school"), primary, and secondary schools are under the jurisdiction of Education Queensland, a department of the [Queensland Government](./Queensland_Government "Queensland Government").[[137]](./Brisbane#cite_note-142) Independent (private), [Roman Catholic](./Roman_Catholic "Roman Catholic") and other religious schools also constitute a large share of Brisbane's primary and secondary schooling sectors, with the oldest such independent schools composing the memberships of the [Great Public Schools Association of Queensland](./Great_Public_Schools_Association_of_Queensland "Great Public Schools Association of Queensland") (GPS) for boys schools and [Queensland Girls' Secondary Schools Sports Association](./Queensland_Girls'_Secondary_Schools_Sports_Association "Queensland Girls' Secondary Schools Sports Association") (QGSSSA) for girls schools.

### Transport

Brisbane has an extensive transport network within the city, as well as connections to regional centres, interstate and to overseas destinations. Like all Australian cities, the most popular mode of transport is private car.[[138]](./Brisbane#cite_note-143) Public transport is provided by rail, bus and ferry services and is coordinated by [Translink](./TransLink_(South_East_Queensland) "TransLink (South East Queensland)"), which provides a unified ticketing and electronic payment system (known as *[go card](./Go_card "Go card")*) for [South East Queensland](./South_East_Queensland "South East Queensland"). The region is divided into seven [fare zones](./Fare "Fare") radiating outwards from the [Brisbane central business district](./Brisbane_central_business_district "Brisbane central business district") (CBD), with Brisbane's built-up area falling within zones 1–3. Bus services are operated by public and private operators whereas trains and ferries are operated by public agencies. The CBD is the central hub for all public transport services with services focusing on [Roma Street](./Roma_Street_railway_station "Roma Street railway station"), [Central](./Central_railway_station,_Brisbane "Central railway station, Brisbane") and [Fortitude Valley](./Fortitude_Valley_railway_station "Fortitude Valley railway station") railway stations; [King George Square](./King_George_Square_busway_station "King George Square busway station"), [Queen Street](./Queen_Street_bus_station "Queen Street bus station") and [Roma Street](./Roma_Street_busway_station "Roma Street busway station") busway stations; and [North Quay](./North_Quay_ferry_wharf "North Quay ferry wharf"), [Riverside](./Riverside_ferry_wharf "Riverside ferry wharf") and [QUT Gardens Point](./QUT_Gardens_Point_ferry_wharf "QUT Gardens Point ferry wharf") ferry wharves.

#### Roads

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5f/Hornibrook_april_2011_%28181%29.jpg/250px-Hornibrook_april_2011_%28181%29.jpg)](./File:Hornibrook_april_2011_(181).jpg)

[Houghton Highway](./Houghton_Highway "Houghton Highway") and [Ted Smout Memorial Bridge](./Ted_Smout_Memorial_Bridge "Ted Smout Memorial Bridge") crossing [Bramble Bay](./Bramble_Bay "Bramble Bay"), Queensland's longest bridges

Brisbane is served by a large network of urban and inter-urban motorways. The [Pacific Motorway](./Pacific_Motorway_(Brisbane–Brunswick_Heads) "Pacific Motorway (Brisbane–Brunswick Heads)") (M3/M1) connects the inner-city with the southern suburbs, [Gold Coast](./Gold_Coast,_Queensland "Gold Coast, Queensland") and [New South Wales](./New_South_Wales "New South Wales"). The [Ipswich Motorway](./Ipswich_Motorway "Ipswich Motorway") (M7/M2) connects the inner-city with the outer south-western suburbs. The [Western Freeway](./Western_Freeway,_Brisbane "Western Freeway, Brisbane") and [Centenary Motorway](./Centenary_Motorway "Centenary Motorway") (M5) connect the city's inner-west and outer south-west. The [Bruce Highway](./Bruce_Highway "Bruce Highway") and [Gympie Arterial Road](./Gympie_Arterial_Road "Gympie Arterial Road") (M1/M3) connect the city's northern suburbs with the [Sunshine Coast](./Sunshine_Coast,_Queensland "Sunshine Coast, Queensland") and northern Queensland. The [Logan Motorway](./Logan_Motorway "Logan Motorway") (M2/M6) connects the southern and south-western suburbs. The [Gateway Motorway](./Gateway_Motorway "Gateway Motorway") is a [toll road](./Toll_road "Toll road") which connects the Gold and [Sunshine Coast](./Sunshine_Coast,_Queensland "Sunshine Coast, Queensland"). The [Port of Brisbane Motorway](./Port_of_Brisbane_Motorway "Port of Brisbane Motorway") links the Gateway Motorway to the [Port of Brisbane](./Port_of_Brisbane "Port of Brisbane"). The [Inner City Bypass](./Inner_City_Bypass,_Brisbane "Inner City Bypass, Brisbane") and [Riverside Expressway](./Riverside_Expressway "Riverside Expressway") serve as an inner ring freeway system to prevent motorists from travelling through the city's congested centre.[[139]](./Brisbane#cite_note-144)

Brisbane also has a large network of major road tunnels under the metropolitan area, known as the [TransApex](./TransApex "TransApex") network, which include the [Clem Jones Tunnel](./Clem_Jones_Tunnel "Clem Jones Tunnel") between the inner-north and inner-south, the [Airport Link tunnel](./Airport_Link,_Brisbane "Airport Link, Brisbane") in the north-east and the [Legacy Way tunnel](./Legacy_Way "Legacy Way") in the south-west. They are the three longest road tunnels in Australia.

#### Bridges

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/26/Story_Bridge_%28Explore%29_-_Flickr_-_Fishyone1.jpg/250px-Story_Bridge_%28Explore%29_-_Flickr_-_Fishyone1.jpg)](./File:Story_Bridge_(Explore)_-_Flickr_-_Fishyone1.jpg)

The 777-metre [Story Bridge](./Story_Bridge "Story Bridge"), completed in 1940

The Brisbane River creates a barrier to road transport routes. In total there are [eighteen bridges](./Bridges_over_the_Brisbane_River "Bridges over the Brisbane River") over the river, mostly concentrated in the inner city area. The road bridges (which usually also include provision for pedestrians and cyclists) by distance from the river mouth are the [Sir Leo Hielscher Bridges](./Sir_Leo_Hielscher_Bridges "Sir Leo Hielscher Bridges"), the [Story Bridge](./Story_Bridge "Story Bridge"), the [Captain Cook Bridge](./Captain_Cook_Bridge,_Brisbane "Captain Cook Bridge, Brisbane"), the [Victoria Bridge](./Victoria_Bridge,_Brisbane "Victoria Bridge, Brisbane"), the [William Jolly Bridge](./William_Jolly_Bridge "William Jolly Bridge"), the [Go Between Bridge](./Go_Between_Bridge "Go Between Bridge"), the [Eleanor Schonell Bridge](./Eleanor_Schonell_Bridge "Eleanor Schonell Bridge"), the [Walter Taylor Bridge](./Walter_Taylor_Bridge "Walter Taylor Bridge") the [Centenary Bridge](./Centenary_Bridge "Centenary Bridge"), and the [Colleges Crossing](./Colleges_Crossing "Colleges Crossing"). There are three railway bridges, namely the [Merivale Bridge](./Merivale_Bridge "Merivale Bridge"), the [Albert Bridge](./Albert_Bridge,_Brisbane "Albert Bridge, Brisbane") and the [Indooroopilly Railway Bridge](./Indooroopilly_Railway_Bridge "Indooroopilly Railway Bridge"). There are also five pedestrian only bridges: the [Kangaroo Point Bridge](./Kangaroo_Point_Green_Bridge "Kangaroo Point Green Bridge"), the [Goodwill Bridge](./Goodwill_Bridge "Goodwill Bridge"), the [Neville Bonner Bridge](./Neville_Bonner_Bridge "Neville Bonner Bridge"), the [Kurilpa Bridge](./Kurilpa_Bridge "Kurilpa Bridge") and the [Jack Pesch Bridge](./Jack_Pesch_Bridge "Jack Pesch Bridge").

The [Houghton Highway](./Houghton_Highway "Houghton Highway") (northbound) and [Ted Smout Memorial Bridge](./Ted_Smout_Memorial_Bridge "Ted Smout Memorial Bridge") (southbound) bridges, over [Bramble Bay](./Bramble_Bay "Bramble Bay") between [Brighton, Queensland](./Brighton,_Queensland "Brighton, Queensland") and the [Redcliffe Peninsula](./Redcliffe_Peninsula "Redcliffe Peninsula"), are the longest bridges in the state. The abutment arches of the original crossing The [Hornibrook Bridge](./Hornibrook_Bridge "Hornibrook Bridge") still remain in place.

#### Rail

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/94/Train_approaching_Roma_Street_railway_station%2C_Brisbane%2C_2021.jpg/250px-Train_approaching_Roma_Street_railway_station%2C_Brisbane%2C_2021.jpg)](./File:Train_approaching_Roma_Street_railway_station,_Brisbane,_2021.jpg)

A [Queensland Rail NGR](./New_Generation_Rollingstock "New Generation Rollingstock") train approaching [Roma Street station](./Roma_Street_railway_station "Roma Street railway station")

The [Queensland Rail City network](./Queensland_Rail_City_network "Queensland Rail City network") consists of 154 train stations along 13 suburban and interurban rail lines and across the metropolitan area, namely: the [Airport](./Airport_railway_line,_Brisbane "Airport railway line, Brisbane"), [Beenleigh](./Beenleigh_railway_line "Beenleigh railway line"), [Caboolture](./Caboolture_railway_line "Caboolture railway line"), [Cleveland](./Cleveland_railway_line "Cleveland railway line"), [Doomben](./Doomben_railway_line "Doomben railway line"), [Ferny Grove](./Ferny_Grove_railway_line "Ferny Grove railway line"), [Ipswich/Rosewood](./Ipswich_and_Rosewood_railway_line "Ipswich and Rosewood railway line"), [Redcliffe Peninsula](./Redcliffe_Peninsula_railway_line "Redcliffe Peninsula railway line"), [Shorncliffe](./Shorncliffe_railway_line "Shorncliffe railway line"), and [Springfield](./Springfield_railway_line "Springfield railway line") lines, as well as the [Exhibition line](./Exhibition_railway_line "Exhibition railway line") which is used only for events at the [Brisbane Showgrounds](./Brisbane_Showgrounds "Brisbane Showgrounds"), as well as an inner-city bypass for freight and a turnback for long-distance services. The network extends to the [Gold](./Gold_Coast,_Queensland "Gold Coast, Queensland") and [Sunshine](./Sunshine_Coast,_Queensland "Sunshine Coast, Queensland") coasts, which are fully integrated into the network on the [Gold Coast line](./Gold_Coast_line "Gold Coast line") and [Sunshine Coast line](./Sunshine_Coast_railway_line "Sunshine Coast railway line"). The [Airtrain](./Airport_railway_line,_Brisbane "Airport railway line, Brisbane") service which runs on the [Airport line](./Airport_railway_line,_Brisbane "Airport railway line, Brisbane") is jointly operated between [Queensland Rail](./Queensland_Rail "Queensland Rail") and [Airtrain Citylink](./Airtrain_Citylink "Airtrain Citylink").

55 million passenger trips were taken across the network in 2018–19.[[140]](./Brisbane#cite_note-145)

Construction of the network began in 1865[[141]](./Brisbane#cite_note-146) and has been progressively expanded in the subsequent centuries. [Electrification of the network](./Rail_electrification_in_Queensland "Rail electrification in Queensland") was completed between 1979 and 1988.

The [Cross River Rail](./Cross_River_Rail "Cross River Rail") project includes a twin rail tunnel (5.9 km (3.7 mi) long) which will pass under the Brisbane River to link two new railway stations at [Albert Street](./Albert_Street,_Brisbane "Albert Street, Brisbane") in the CBD and [Woolloongabba](./Woolloongabba "Woolloongabba"); it is under construction and scheduled to be completed in early 2025.[[142]](./Brisbane#cite_note-todo-147)

#### Bus

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/72/Translink_Bus_Queensland_Australia.jpg/250px-Translink_Bus_Queensland_Australia.jpg)](./File:Translink_Bus_Queensland_Australia.jpg)

Translink bus

[Brisbane's busway network](./Busways_in_Brisbane "Busways in Brisbane") is a large dedicated [bus rapid transit](./Bus_rapid_transit "Bus rapid transit") network. The network comprises the [South East Busway](./South_East_Busway "South East Busway"), the [Northern Busway](./Northern_Busway,_Brisbane "Northern Busway, Brisbane") and the [Eastern Busway](./Eastern_Busway,_Brisbane "Eastern Busway, Brisbane"). The main network hubs are the [King George Square](./King_George_Square_busway_station "King George Square busway station"), [Queen Street](./Queen_Street_bus_station "Queen Street bus station"), and [Roma Street](./Roma_Street_busway_station "Roma Street busway station") busway stations.

There are also numerous suburban bus routes operating throughout the metropolitan area, including the high-frequency blue and maroon [CityGlider](./CityGlider "CityGlider") routes which run between [Newstead](./Newstead,_Queensland "Newstead, Queensland") and [West End](./West_End,_Queensland "West End, Queensland") (blue), and [Ashgrove](./Ashgrove,_Queensland "Ashgrove, Queensland") and [Coorparoo](./Coorparoo "Coorparoo") (maroon) respectively.

[Brisbane Metro](./Brisbane_Metro "Brisbane Metro") is a [bus rapid transit](./Bus_rapid_transit "Bus rapid transit") (BRT) project which will initially consist of two routes (Metro 1 and 2) running between [Eight Mile Plains](./Eight_Mile_Plains_busway_station "Eight Mile Plains busway station") and [Roma Street](./Roma_Street_busway_station "Roma Street busway station"), and [UQ St Lucia (UQ Lakes)](./UQ_Lakes_busway_station "UQ Lakes busway station") and the [Royal Brisbane and Women's Hospital](./Royal_Brisbane_and_Women's_Hospital "Royal Brisbane and Women's Hospital") respectively. It is set to open in 2024.

The CityCat high-speed [catamaran](./Catamaran "Catamaran") ferry service, popular with tourists and commuters, operates services along the [Brisbane River](./Brisbane_River "Brisbane River") between the [University of Queensland](./University_of_Queensland "University of Queensland") and [Northshore Hamilton](./Northshore_Hamilton_ferry_wharf "Northshore Hamilton ferry wharf"), with wharves at [UQ St Lucia](./University_of_Queensland_ferry_wharf "University of Queensland ferry wharf"), [West End](./West_End_ferry_wharf "West End ferry wharf"), [Guyatt Park](./Guyatt_Park_ferry_wharf "Guyatt Park ferry wharf"), [Regatta](./Regatta_ferry_wharf "Regatta ferry wharf"), [Milton](./Milton_ferry_wharf "Milton ferry wharf"), [North Quay](./North_Quay_ferry_wharf "North Quay ferry wharf"), [South Bank](./South_Bank_ferry_wharf "South Bank ferry wharf"), [QUT Gardens Point](./QUT_Gardens_Point_ferry_wharf "QUT Gardens Point ferry wharf"), [Riverside](./Riverside_ferry_wharf "Riverside ferry wharf"), [Sydney Street](./Sydney_Street_ferry_wharf "Sydney Street ferry wharf"), [Mowbray Park](./Mowbray_Park_ferry_wharf "Mowbray Park ferry wharf"), [New Farm Park](./New_Farm_Park_ferry_wharf "New Farm Park ferry wharf"), [Hawthorne](./Hawthorne_ferry_wharf "Hawthorne ferry wharf"), [Bulimba](./Bulimba_ferry_wharf "Bulimba ferry wharf"), [Teneriffe](./Teneriffe_ferry_wharf "Teneriffe ferry wharf"), [Bretts Wharf](./Bretts_Wharf "Bretts Wharf"), [Apollo Road](./Apollo_Road_ferry_wharf "Apollo Road ferry wharf"), and [Northshore Hamilton](./Northshore_Hamilton_ferry_wharf "Northshore Hamilton ferry wharf").

The Cross River services operate smaller vessels for popular cross-river routes, namely: [Bulimba](./Bulimba_ferry_wharf "Bulimba ferry wharf")–[Teneriffe](./Teneriffe_ferry_wharf "Teneriffe ferry wharf") and [Holman Street](./Holman_Street_ferry_wharf "Holman Street ferry wharf")–[Riverside](./Riverside_ferry_wharf "Riverside ferry wharf").

The free CityHopper service operates smaller vessels along a route between [North Quay](./North_Quay_ferry_wharf "North Quay ferry wharf") and [Sydney Street](./Sydney_Street_ferry_wharf "Sydney Street ferry wharf"), stopping at [South Bank](./South_Bank_ferry_wharf "South Bank ferry wharf"), [Maritime Museum](./Maritime_Museum_ferry_wharf "Maritime Museum ferry wharf"), [Riverside](./Riverside_ferry_wharf "Riverside ferry wharf") and [Holman Street](./Holman_Street_ferry_wharf "Holman Street ferry wharf").

There are tourist passenger ferries that depart the Brisbane River at [Pinkenba](./Pinkenba "Pinkenba") to [Tangalooma](./Tangalooma "Tangalooma") on Moreton Island four times daily, and Micat 4WD car ferries that depart from the [Port of Brisbane](./Port_of_Brisbane "Port of Brisbane") daily.[[144]](./Brisbane#cite_note-149)

#### Pedestrian

An extensive network of pedestrian and cyclist pathways span the banks of the [Brisbane River](./Brisbane_River "Brisbane River") in the inner suburbs to form the [Riverwalk](./Brisbane_River#Brisbane_Riverwalk "Brisbane River") network.[[145]](./Brisbane#cite_note-150) In some segments, the Riverwalk is built over the river. The longest span of the Riverwalk connects [Newstead](./Newstead,_Queensland "Newstead, Queensland") in the east with [Toowong](./Toowong "Toowong") in the west.

#### Airports

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/97/Brisbane_Airport_domestic_terminal_Vabre.jpg/250px-Brisbane_Airport_domestic_terminal_Vabre.jpg)](./File:Brisbane_Airport_domestic_terminal_Vabre.jpg)

Domestic terminal at [Brisbane Airport](./Brisbane_Airport "Brisbane Airport")

[Brisbane Airport](./Brisbane_Airport "Brisbane Airport") ([IATA](./IATA_airport_code "IATA airport code"): **BNE**, [ICAO](./ICAO_airport_code "ICAO airport code"): **YBBN**) is the city's main airport, the [third busiest in Australia](./List_of_the_busiest_airports_in_Australia "List of the busiest airports in Australia") after [Sydney Airport](./Sydney_Airport "Sydney Airport") and [Melbourne Airport](./Melbourne_Airport "Melbourne Airport"). It is located north-east of the city centre on Moreton Bay and provides domestic and international passenger services. In 2017, Brisbane Airport handled over 23 million passengers.[[146]](./Brisbane#cite_note-AirportTraffic-151) The airport is the main [hub](./Airline_hub "Airline hub") for [Virgin Australia](./Virgin_Australia "Virgin Australia") as well as a number of minor and freight airlines, and a focus city for [Qantas](./Qantas "Qantas") and [Jetstar](./Jetstar "Jetstar"). The airport is served by the Airtrain service which runs on the [Airport line](./Airport_railway_line,_Brisbane "Airport railway line, Brisbane"), providing a direct service to the [CBD](./Brisbane_central_business_district "Brisbane central business district").

[Archerfield Airport](./Archerfield_Airport "Archerfield Airport") in Brisbane's southern suburbs, [Redcliffe Airport](./Redcliffe_Airport_(Queensland) "Redcliffe Airport (Queensland)") on the [Redcliffe Peninsula](./Redcliffe_Peninsula "Redcliffe Peninsula") and [Caboolture Airfield](./Caboolture_Airfield "Caboolture Airfield") in the far north of the metropolitan area serve Brisbane as [general aviation](./General_aviation "General aviation") airports.

Brisbane is also served by other major airports in [South East Queensland](./South_East_Queensland "South East Queensland"), including [Gold Coast Airport](./Gold_Coast_Airport "Gold Coast Airport") at [Coolangatta](./Coolangatta "Coolangatta"), [Sunshine Coast Airport](./Sunshine_Coast_Airport "Sunshine Coast Airport") at [Marcoola](./Marcoola "Marcoola"), and [Toowoomba Wellcamp Airport](./Toowoomba_Wellcamp_Airport "Toowoomba Wellcamp Airport") at [Wellcamp](./Wellcamp "Wellcamp").

#### Seaport

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/02/Brisbane_Docks_2004_-_panoramio.jpg/250px-Brisbane_Docks_2004_-_panoramio.jpg)](./File:Brisbane_Docks_2004_-_panoramio.jpg)

The [Port of Brisbane](./Port_of_Brisbane "Port of Brisbane"), Australia's third-busiest seaport

The [Port of Brisbane](./Port_of_Brisbane "Port of Brisbane") is located on the south side of the mouth of the Brisbane River on [Moreton Bay](./Moreton_Bay "Moreton Bay") and on the adjacent Fisherman's Island, an [artificial island](./Artificial_island "Artificial island") created by [land reclamation](./Land_reclamation "Land reclamation"). It is the third busiest port in Australia for value of goods.[[107]](./Brisbane#cite_note-Port_Technology-112) The port is the endpoint of the main shipping channel across Moreton Bay which extends 90 kilometres north near [Mooloolaba](./Mooloolaba "Mooloolaba"). The port has 29 operating berths including nine deep-water container [berths](./Berth_(moorings) "Berth (moorings)") and three deep-water bulk berths as well as 17 bulk and general cargo berths.

There are two [cruise ship](./Cruise_ship "Cruise ship") terminals in Brisbane. [Portside Wharf](./Portside_Wharf "Portside Wharf") on the north side of the river at [Hamilton](./Hamilton,_Queensland "Hamilton, Queensland") is an international standard facility for cruise liners. Due to the height of the [Gateway Bridge](./Gateway_Bridge "Gateway Bridge") which must be passed to reach the terminal, the wharf services small and medium-sized cruise ships. The [Brisbane International Cruise Terminal](./Brisbane_International_Cruise_Terminal "Brisbane International Cruise Terminal") at Luggage Point in [Pinkenba](./Pinkenba "Pinkenba") on the north side of the river opposite the Port of Brisbane is able to accommodate the largest cruise vessels in the world.[[147]](./Brisbane#cite_note-152)

### Healthcare

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4e/Queensland_Children%27s_Hospital_in_Brisbane%2C_November_2019.jpg/250px-Queensland_Children%27s_Hospital_in_Brisbane%2C_November_2019.jpg)](./File:Queensland_Children's_Hospital_in_Brisbane,_November_2019.jpg)

The [Queensland Children's Hospital](./Queensland_Children's_Hospital "Queensland Children's Hospital") at [South Brisbane](./South_Brisbane "South Brisbane")

Brisbane is covered by [Queensland Health's](./Queensland_Health "Queensland Health") Hospital and Health Services (divided in Metro North, Metro South and Children's Health Queensland).[[148]](./Brisbane#cite_note-153) Within the greater Brisbane area there are eight major [public hospitals](./Public_hospital "Public hospital"), four major [private hospitals](./Private_hospital "Private hospital"), and numerous smaller public and private facilities. The [Royal Brisbane and Women's Hospital](./Royal_Brisbane_and_Women's_Hospital "Royal Brisbane and Women's Hospital") and the [Princess Alexandra Hospital](./Princess_Alexandra_Hospital,_Brisbane "Princess Alexandra Hospital, Brisbane") are two of Queensland's three major trauma centres. Standing alone, they are the largest hospitals in Australia. The [Princess Alexandra Hospital](./Princess_Alexandra_Hospital,_Brisbane "Princess Alexandra Hospital, Brisbane") houses the [Translational Research Institute (Australia)](./Translational_Research_Institute_(Australia) "Translational Research Institute (Australia)") along with the state's renal and liver transplant services. The [Royal Brisbane and Women's Hospital](./Royal_Brisbane_and_Women's_Hospital "Royal Brisbane and Women's Hospital") includes a specialist burns unit.[[149]](./Brisbane#cite_note-154) [The Prince Charles Hospital](./The_Prince_Charles_Hospital "The Prince Charles Hospital") is the state's major cardiac transplant centre. Other major public hospitals include the [Queensland Children's Hospital](./Queensland_Children's_Hospital "Queensland Children's Hospital"), the [Queen Elizabeth II Jubilee Hospital](./Queen_Elizabeth_II_Jubilee_Hospital "Queen Elizabeth II Jubilee Hospital"), and the [Mater Hospital](./Mater_Group "Mater Group").

Specialist and [general medical practices](./General_practitioner "General practitioner") are located in the CBD, and most suburbs and localities.

Brisbane is also home to the headquarters of the [Queensland Ambulance Service](./Queensland_Ambulance_Service "Queensland Ambulance Service") central executive, located at the Emergency Services Complex Kedron Park, along with the headquarters of the [Queensland Fire and Emergency Services](./Queensland_Fire_and_Emergency_Services "Queensland Fire and Emergency Services") and the Queensland Emergency Operations Centre.

### Other utilities

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9a/Toowong_Cemetery_1a.jpg/250px-Toowong_Cemetery_1a.jpg)](./File:Toowong_Cemetery_1a.jpg)

[Toowong Cemetery](./Toowong_Cemetery "Toowong Cemetery"), opened in 1875, Queensland's largest cemetery

Water in Brisbane is managed by two [statutory authorities](./Statutory_authority "Statutory authority"): [Seqwater](./Seqwater "Seqwater") and [Urban Utilities](./Queensland_Urban_Utilities "Queensland Urban Utilities"). Bulk water storage, treatment and transportation for South East Queensland is managed by [Seqwater](./Seqwater "Seqwater"), with [Urban Utilities](./Queensland_Urban_Utilities "Queensland Urban Utilities") (previously Brisbane Water) responsible for distribution to the greater Brisbane area. Water for the area is stored in three major dams to the north-west of the metropolitan area: [Wivenhoe](./Wivenhoe_Dam "Wivenhoe Dam"), [Somerset](./Lake_Somerset "Lake Somerset") and [North Pine](./North_Pine_Dam "North Pine Dam").

The provision of electricity in Brisbane is managed by government and private bodies. Generators (some private and some owned by the Queensland government) sell energy into the wholesale market for eastern Australia known as the [National Electricity Market](./National_Electricity_Market "National Electricity Market"). Transmission and distribution of electricity is managed by the Queensland government owned corporations [Energex](./Energex "Energex") and [Powerlink Queensland](./Powerlink_Queensland "Powerlink Queensland") respectively. [Private retailers](./Electricity_retailing "Electricity retailing") then purchase electricity from the wholesale [market](./Electricity_market "Electricity market") and sell it to consumers, which have the ability to choose between different retailers in a partially de-regulated market.[[150]](./Brisbane#cite_note-155)

The supply of [gas](./Natural_gas "Natural gas") to users is more heavily privatised, with the private [APA Group](./APA_Group_(Australia) "APA Group (Australia)") distributing gas in Brisbane, which is then bought and sold by retailers (mainly [Origin Energy](./Origin_Energy "Origin Energy") and [AGL Energy](./AGL_Energy "AGL Energy")) in a partially de-regulated market.[[151]](./Brisbane#cite_note-156)

Metropolitan Brisbane is serviced by all major and most minor telecommunications companies and their networks, including [Telstra](./Telstra "Telstra"), [Optus](./Optus "Optus"), and [Vodafone Australia](./Vodafone_Australia "Vodafone Australia").

Brisbane is home to numerous [cemeteries](./Cemeteries "Cemeteries") including the following large 19th-century historical cemeteries: the 44-hectare [Toowong Cemetery](./Toowong_Cemetery "Toowong Cemetery") (the largest cemetery in Queensland, which is a popular destination for walkers and joggers), [Balmoral Cemetery](./Balmoral_Cemetery,_Brisbane "Balmoral Cemetery, Brisbane"), [Lutwyche Cemetery](./Lutwyche_Cemetery "Lutwyche Cemetery"), [Nudgee Cemetery](./Nudgee_Cemetery "Nudgee Cemetery"), [Nundah Cemetery](./Nundah_Cemetery "Nundah Cemetery"), and [South Brisbane Cemetery](./South_Brisbane_Cemetery "South Brisbane Cemetery").

Media
-----

### Print

The main local print newspapers of Brisbane are *[The Courier-Mail](./The_Courier-Mail "The Courier-Mail")* and its sibling *[The Sunday Mail](./The_Sunday_Mail_(Brisbane) "The Sunday Mail (Brisbane)")*, both owned by [News Corporation](./News_Corporation "News Corporation"). Brisbane also receives the national daily, *[The Australian](./The_Australian "The Australian")* and its sibling the *Weekend Australian.*

The *[Brisbane Times](./Brisbane_Times "Brisbane Times")* is Brisbane's second major local news source, owned by [Nine](./Nine_Entertainment_Co. "Nine Entertainment Co."), and is online only. Its sibling papers, *[The Sydney Morning Herald](./The_Sydney_Morning_Herald "The Sydney Morning Herald")* and Melbourne's *[The Age](./The_Age "The Age")* are sometimes sold in print in Brisbane in small numbers. The national broadsheet *[Australian Financial Review](./Australian_Financial_Review "Australian Financial Review")*, also owned by Nine, is sold in print in Brisbane.

There are community and suburban newspapers throughout the metropolitan area, including *Brisbane News* and *City News*, many of which are produced by [Quest Community Newspapers](./Quest_Community_Newspapers "Quest Community Newspapers").

### Television

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/30/OIC_river_view_of_toowong_and_mt_coot-tha.jpg/250px-OIC_river_view_of_toowong_and_mt_coot-tha.jpg)](./File:OIC_river_view_of_toowong_and_mt_coot-tha.jpg)

Television [transmission towers](./Transmission_tower "Transmission tower") atop [Mount Coot-tha](./Mount_Coot-tha "Mount Coot-tha")

Brisbane is served by all five major television networks in Australia, which broadcast from prominent [television transmission towers](./Transmission_tower "Transmission tower") on the summit of [Mount Coot-tha](./Mount_Coot-tha "Mount Coot-tha"). The three commercial stations, [Seven](./Seven_Network "Seven Network"), [Nine](./Nine_Network "Nine Network"), and [Ten](./Network_10 "Network 10"), are accompanied by two government networks, [ABC](./Australian_Broadcasting_Corporation "Australian Broadcasting Corporation") and [SBS](./Special_Broadcasting_Service "Special Broadcasting Service"). Channels provided by these networks include [10 HD](./10_HD "10 HD") (10 broadcast in HD), [10 Drama](./10_Drama "10 Drama"), [10 Comedy](./10_Comedy "10 Comedy"), [Nickelodeon](./Nickelodeon_(Australian_TV_channel) "Nickelodeon (Australian TV channel)"), [TVSN](./TVSN "TVSN"), [ABC TV HD](./ABC_HD_(Australian_TV_channel) "ABC HD (Australian TV channel)") (ABC TV broadcast in HD), [ABC Family](./ABC_Family_(Australian_TV_channel) "ABC Family (Australian TV channel)")/[ABC Kids](./ABC_Kids_(Australia) "ABC Kids (Australia)"), [ABC Entertains](./ABC_Entertains "ABC Entertains"), [ABC News](./ABC_News_(TV_channel) "ABC News (TV channel)"), [SBS HD](./SBS_HD "SBS HD") (SBS broadcast in HD), [SBS World Movies](./SBS_World_Movies "SBS World Movies"), [SBS Viceland HD](./SBS_Viceland_HD "SBS Viceland HD") (SBS Viceland broadcast in HD), [SBS Food](./SBS_Food "SBS Food"), [NITV](./NITV "NITV"), [SBS WorldWatch](./SBS_WorldWatch "SBS WorldWatch"), [7HD](./7HD "7HD") (Seven broadcast in HD), [7two](./7two "7two"), [7mate](./7mate "7mate"), [7flix](./7flix "7flix"), [7mate HD](./7mate_HD "7mate HD") (7mate broadcast in HD), [Racing.com](./Racing.com "Racing.com"), [9HD](./9HD "9HD") (Nine broadcast in HD), [9Gem](./9Gem "9Gem"), [9Go!](./9Go! "9Go!"), [9Life](./9Life "9Life"), [9Gem HD](./9Gem_HD "9Gem HD") (9Gem broadcast in HD) and [9Rush](./9Rush "9Rush"). [31 Digital](./31_Digital "31 Digital"), a community station, also broadcast in Brisbane until 2017. [Optus](./Optus "Optus") and [Foxtel](./Foxtel "Foxtel") operates Pay TV services in Brisbane, via [cable](./Cable_television "Cable television") and [satellite](./Satellite_television "Satellite television") means.

### Radio

Brisbane is serviced by five major public radio stations including major commercial radio stations, including [ABC Radio Brisbane](./ABC_Radio_Brisbane "ABC Radio Brisbane") (local news, current affairs and talk); [ABC Radio National](./ABC_Radio_National "ABC Radio National") (national news and current affairs); [ABC NewsRadio](./ABC_NewsRadio "ABC NewsRadio") (national news); [ABC Classic FM](./ABC_Classic_FM "ABC Classic FM") (classical music); [Triple J](./Triple_J "Triple J") (alternative music); and [SBS Radio](./SBS_Radio "SBS Radio") (multicultural broadcasting).

Brisbane is serviced by numerous major commercial and community radio stations including 4BC (local and national talk, news and current affairs); [SENQ](./4KQ "4KQ") (sport); [4BH](./4BH "4BH") (classic hits); [KIIS 97.3](./KIIS_97.3 "KIIS 97.3") (pop); [B105](./B105_FM "B105 FM") (pop); [Nova 106.9](./Nova_106.9 "Nova 106.9") (top 40); [Triple M](./Triple_M_Brisbane "Triple M Brisbane") (rock); [96five Family FM](./96five_Family_FM "96five Family FM") (Christian/pop); [Radio TAB](./Radio_TAB "Radio TAB") (betting); and [4MBS](./4MBS "4MBS") (classical).

Brisbane is also serviced by community radio stations such as VAC Radio ([Mandarin](./Standard_Chinese "Standard Chinese")); Radio Brisvaani ([Hindi](./Hindi "Hindi")); [Radio Arabic](./2ME_Radio_Arabic "2ME Radio Arabic") ([Arabic](./Arabic "Arabic")); [4EB](./4EB "4EB") (multiple languages); [98.9 FM](./98.9_FM_(Brisbane) "98.9 FM (Brisbane)") ([indigenous](./Indigenous_Australians "Indigenous Australians")); [4RPH](./4RPH "4RPH") (vision impaired); [Switch 1197](./Switch_1197 "Switch 1197") (youth broadcasting); [4ZZZ](./4ZZZ "4ZZZ") (community radio); and [Vision Christian Radio](./Vision_Christian_Radio "Vision Christian Radio") ([Christian](./Christianity "Christianity")).[[152]](./Brisbane#cite_note-157) Additional channels are also available via [DAB](./Digital_audio_broadcasting "Digital audio broadcasting") [digital radio](./Digital_radio "Digital radio").

"In 1843, [ [Ludwig Leichhardt](./Ludwig_Leichhardt "Ludwig Leichhardt") ] was given two names: *Makandschin* from an original Brisbane man and *Megandsin* from an original speaker from a different country... [Meston](./Archibald_Meston "Archibald Meston") listed *Magoo-jin* then *Magandjin*, based on *Magan*, the name of the tulipwood tree, from elderly [Goori](./Koori "Koori") [Aboriginal] speakers who asserted they were 'Brisbane natives'... From a Goori knowledge base the names based on the tulipwood tree fits best for the original Goori name. The suffix -djin indicates plural, e.g. people, district, river. The *Migan-dar-gu-n* (*Mi'andjan*) version describes the use of a sharp tool, possibly ground being dug up, likely the first convict garden, which the [Petrie](./Thomas_Petrie "Thomas Petrie") map shows multiplied across the whole of the promontory. Another explanation of this name is 'land shaped like a spike'. Both these are based on *Dugai* [European] activity and *Dugai* lens... *Magandjin* fits as the original word for an area of what is now called Brisbane. *Migandjan* refers to digging the ground—either gardens or buildings. However, the term *Migandjan* spread. As demonstrated, language repatriation is a work in progress."
