skating\\n\\nCulture\\n-------\\n\\n[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/25/Ostra_Aradalen1_Sweden.jpg/250px-Ostra_Aradalen1_Sweden.jpg)](./File:Ostra_Aradalen1_Sweden.jpg)\\n\\nTraditional summer houses, *buvåll* \"critter house\" in Jämtland. \\'Bu\\' is [cognate](./Cognate \"Cognate\") to the English word \"booth\" and \\'våll\\' to \"[weald](./Weald \"Weald\")\"\\n\\n[![Goats at Gräftåvallen, southern Jämtland](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/ad/Gr%C3%A4ft%C3%A5vallen.jpg/250px-Gr%C3%A4ft%C3%A5vallen.jpg)](./File:Gräftåvallen.jpg \"Goats at Gräftåvallen, southern Jämtland\")\\n\\nGoats at Gräftåvallen, southern Jämtland\\n\\n[![Jämthund](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/38/J%C3%A4mthund_drvd.png/250px-J%C3%A4mthund_drvd.png)](./File:Jämthund_drvd.png \"Jämthund\")\\n\\nJämthund\\n\\nThe culture of Jämtland has been greatly affected by the fact that Jämtland has never had an [upper class](./Upper_class \"Upper class\"), since the population have mostly consisted of free sovereign farmers with wide connections and a strong regional identity.[[26]](./Jämtland#cite_note-26) This has been the case for many generations. When [Christian IV of Denmark](./Christian_IV_of_Denmark \"Christian IV of Denmark\") punished the Jamts severely after having sworn the Swedish king their allegiance (see above) by turning them into [tenant farmers](./Tenant_farmer \"Tenant farmer\") and abolished their seal, he told them to stay put on their farms. They did not heed this call but instead sought help from their own organized advisors and \"the land\\'s defense\", an insolence that further outraged the Danish king. Jämtland started out free and remained autonomous during its time as a Norwegian [dependency](./Dependent_territory \"Dependent territory\"). Because of Jämtland\\'s historical background the local culture shows great similarities with the [Norwegian farm culture](./Norwegian_farm_culture \"Norwegian farm culture\").\\n\\nToday, the history of Jämtland is exhibited in the regional museum [Jamtli](./Jamtli \"Jamtli\") in [Östersund](./Östersund \"Östersund\"). The museum consists of an [open-air section](./Open-air_museum \"Open-air museum\") with historical buildings, as well as an indoor museum which houses exhibitions about the region\\'s cultural history, from the Stone Age until modern times. Local history has been very popular in Jämtland for over 100 years, due to the extensive cultural home ground movement that emerged in the late 19th and early 20th century. The movement founded Jamtli to preserve the cultural heritage.\\n\\n### Lifestyle\\n\\nThe culture in Jämtland has been marked by the stages in human development; the hunting-gathering stage, the semi-nomadic herding stage, the fully agricultural stage and the modern technological stage.\\n\\nRemnants from the hunter-gathering stage is first and foremost hunting itself. Jämtland\\'s population remained in this stage for a very long time due to the hunters ability to sustain the population. Today the moose hunt is regarded by many Jamts as the major holiday of the year. When the first humans came to Jämtland they brought dogs with them as helpers. The local dog, [Jämthund](./Jämthund \"Jämthund\"), is a canine breed eponymous to Jämtland. Even if it is not explicitly stated, popular perception holds that the dog depicted in the coat of arms is of that breed. The Jämthund is often described having a [wolf](./Wolf \"Wolf\")-like appearance.\\n\\nOne of the first things [Tacitus](./Tacitus \"Tacitus\") mentions in his work *[Germania](./Germania_(book) \"Germania (book)\")* is that the Germanic people treasure their animals above all else. Tacitus also concludes that the Germanic people found cultivation repulsive. Instead, he states, the Germanic people devote themselves to food and sleep and besides that they prefer to remain idle. All of this, to certain extents, applied to Jämtland. When the people of Jämtland settled down they relied mostly on [pastoralism](./Pastoralism \"Pastoralism\") ([transhumance](./Transhumance \"Transhumance\")). Their animals were the source of wealth and they were therefore loved by their owners. This love for the [livestock](./Livestock \"Livestock\") has manifested itself in the dialect, a male [nipple](./Nipple \"Nipple\") is called *bokkjen* (the [buck](./Goat#Etymology \"Goat\")) and a female nipple is known as *geita* (the [goat](./Goat \"Goat\")).\\n\\nIn Jämtland the Scandinavian inland transhumance, *buföring*, has always been more important than cultivation. In fact it was crucial to take care of the livestock and supply them with food, and rewarding. Every summer for several weeks, from May to September, *gjetaran* (herd boys) and *butøusan* (herd girls, *bu* is cognate to \"booth\") followed and guarded *kreka*, the critter, on their way to a [grazing land](./Grazing \"Grazing\") on higher altitudes where several critter houses had been raised. The common animals taken out on these journeys were *gjettran* (Jämtland goats) and *kynnan* (the fell cows) a white, brisk and headstrong cow race, lacking horns. It was a hard work and it depended on cooperation between males and females. This lifestyle lived on for thousand years and it was first in the 1950s it became obsolete. This tradition has however been resurrected as of late, mostly for touristic purposes.\\n\\nWhen the population settled down the society greatly changed, first coexisting with the older societies, later absorbing them. Trade became much more important, a political institution elected by the people came into existence, the very same institution whose successor is the current County Council. Jämtland got its name and a somewhat [hierarchical](./Hierarchy \"Hierarchy\") social structure emerged, though, as already pointed out, Jämtland never had an upper class. Strong families such as [Skanke](./Skanke \"Skanke\") and [Blix](./Blix_(noble_family)?action=edit&redlink=1 \"Blix (noble family)\") did exist though and on the countryside in Jämtland people still live in networks of relatives, *families*. Where they provide a second [social security](./Social_security \"Social security\") for many, in the rest of Sweden and in e.g. Östersund this has completely or almost entirely been replaced by [public welfare](./Public_welfare \"Public welfare\").\\n\\n### Cuisine\\n\\nSee also: [Cuisine of Norway](./Cuisine_of_Norway \"Cuisine of Norway\") and [Cuisine of Sweden](./Cuisine_of_Sweden \"Cuisine of Sweden\")\\n\\n[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b9/Messmor.jpg/250px-Messmor.jpg)](./File:Messmor.jpg)\\n\\n*Messmör*, soft whey butter, is a Jamtish product popular in Sweden\\n\\nMuch of Jämtland\\'s cuisine is remnant from the herding stage. Just like other Scandinavians, it is common among Jamts to drink [milk](./Milk \"Milk\") throughout their entire life. There are many different types of Jamtish [dairy products](./Dairy_products \"Dairy products\"), especially cheese, since it was by far the easiest way to conserve milk. [Mesost](./Brunost \"Brunost\") is particularly associated with Jämtland and also e.g. a local variant of [cottage cheese](./Cottage_cheese \"Cottage cheese\") called *grynost*. In Jämtland there are several small [dairies](./Dairy \"Dairy\") in the villages, most famous is the one in [Skärvången](./Skärvången?action=edit&redlink=1 \"Skärvången\"). Other products associated with Jämtland are the [soft whey butter](./Soft_whey_butter?action=edit&redlink=1 \"Soft whey butter\"), [long fil](./Long_fil?action=edit&redlink=1 \"Long fil\"), [kjesfil](./Kjesfil?action=edit&redlink=1 \"Kjesfil\"), *flautgröt* \"[cream](./Cream \"Cream\") [porridge](./Porridge \"Porridge\")\", [tunnbröd](./Tunnbröd \"Tunnbröd\"), a version of [palt](./Palt \"Palt\") called *kams*, klobb etc.\\n\\nThe ancient practice of brewing *Julöl* (yule beer) persists even today with the [microbrewery](./Microbrewery \"Microbrewery\") [Jämtlands Bryggeri](./Jämtlands_Bryggeri \"Jämtlands Bryggeri\") in [Pilgrimstad](./Pilgrimstad \"Pilgrimstad\").\\n\\nLocal projects such as the internet portal [Food of Jämtland](http://www.foodofjamtland.se/english) and the trading mark *[Smakriket Jämtland](https://www.smakriket.se)* (the \"taste realm\" Jämtland) are two major contributors in marketing, preserving and developing the cuisine of Jämtland.\\n\\nSome of the newest merchandises in Jämtland are a [sparkling wine](./Sparkling_wine \"Sparkling wine\") made of [birch](./Birch \"Birch\") [sap](./Sap \"Sap\") and a [sausage](./Sausage \"Sausage\") called *Jämtlandsfalu*, wilderness juice, the [snaps](./Snaps \"Snaps\") *kallsup* and tunnbröd [chips.](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/chips \"wikt:chips\")\\n\\n### Folklore\\n\\nSee also: [Scandinavian folklore](./Scandinavian_folklore \"Scandinavian folklore\")\\n\\n[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/36/PB190187.JPG/250px-PB190187.JPG)](./File:PB190187.JPG)\\n\\nLake Storsjön\\n\\nThe folklore of Jämtland mostly correspond to [Scandinavian folklore](./Scandinavian_folklore \"Scandinavian folklore\") as whole, although the folklore is seldom regarded as popular belief nowadays, with one major exception, [Storsjöodjuret](./Storsjöodjuret \"Storsjöodjuret\").\\n\\nAccording to legend it is believed that [Storsjön](./Storsjön \"Storsjön\") (literally *the Great Lake*) harbors a large lake creature, Storsjöodjuret. There are many witness reports but the creature\\'s existence remains to be established conclusively. Regardless of any proven existence, Storsjöodjuret was officially placed under the protection of a degree issued in 1986 by the [County Administrative Board](./County_Administrative_Boards_of_Sweden \"County Administrative Boards of Sweden\") to guarantee its safety from hunters and fortune seekers, the protection was lifted in November 2005.[[27]](./Jämtland#cite_note-27) The first description of Storsjöodjuret was made in this tale from 1635;\\n\\n[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1f/Draak_%C3%96stersund_22jul2006.jpg/250px-Draak_%C3%96stersund_22jul2006.jpg)](./File:Draak_Östersund_22jul2006.jpg)\\n\\nStorsjöodjuret is commonly represented by this figure.\\n\\n\\n> A long, long time ago two trolls, Jata and Kata, stood on the shores of the Great Lake brewing a concoction in their cauldrons. They brewed and mixed and added to the liquid for days and weeks and years. They knew not what would result from their brew but they wondered about it a great deal. One evening there was heard a strange sound from one of their cauldrons. There was a wailing, a groaning and a crying, then suddenly came a loud bang. A strange animal with a black serpentine body and a cat-like head jumped out of the cauldron and disappeared into the lake. The monster enjoyed living in the lake, grew unbelievably larger and awakened terror among the people whenever it appeared. Finally, it extended all the way round the island of Frösön, and could even bite its own tail. Ketil Runske bound the mighty monster with a strong spell which was carved on a stone and raised on the island of Frösön. The serpent was pictured on the stone. Thus was the spell to be tied till the day someone came who could read and understand the inscription on the stone.\\n\\n*[Puken](./Puken?action=edit&redlink=1 \"Puken\")* is a magical ball of [yarn](./Yarn \"Yarn\") summoned by a witch to draw objects to her. It often steals milk to the witch by milking [cows](./Cow \"Cow\").[[28]](./Jämtland#cite_note-28)\\n\\nJust like in the rest of the world [dragons](./Dragon \"Dragon\") have been known for a long time. In Jämtland they resemble [brooms](./Broom \"Broom\"), that flies quickly and strikes down where [treasuries](./Treasury \"Treasury\") are buried.[[29]](./Jämtland#cite_note-29)\\n\\n*[Sjörå](./Sjörå \"Sjörå\")* is a keeper of freshwater, that master fish, [aas](./River \"River\") and lakes. It is similar to the Jamtish *[skogskjæringa](./Hulder \"Hulder\")* \"wife of the forest\". A being that, at day, takes the appearance of a *[rauvtjuksa](./Siberian_jay \"Siberian jay\")* \"red tail\", a bird seen as ominous in Jamtish folklore. When in physical form her tail is always apparent. She tries to lure men to have [sexual intercourse](./Sexual_intercourse \"Sexual intercourse\") with her. The *skogsrå* is not the same creature as skogskjæringa in Jamtish folklore, it is the keeper of the forest and master all the animals in it. It takes on the shape of a moose during hunting season, and grows larger and larger if hit by bullets and eventually forces the hunters out. It can however, be slain with a silver bullet.[[30]](./Jämtland#cite_note-30)\\n\\n[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/ca/Johan_Tirens_naecken.jpg/250px-Johan_Tirens_naecken.jpg)](./File:Johan_Tirens_naecken.jpg)\\n\\nLocal artist [Johan Tirén](./Johan_Tirén \"Johan Tirén\")\\'s painting *Jämtlandssägen* (Jämtland\\'s tale) with a young fiddler wearing traditional Great Jamtish clothes, whilst listening to the Nix play.\\n\\n[Tomten](./Tomte \"Tomte\") is a common creature, it is quite tall and has an eye in the middle of his forehead. It is the keeper of [barns](./Barn \"Barn\") and a very capricious being, though he usually brings luck.[[31]](./Jämtland#cite_note-p_98-31)\\n\\nThe [Nix](./Neck_(water_spirit) \"Neck (water spirit)\"), *Näkkjen*, is a common mythical creature, in Jämtland it refers to a male water spirit whose music was dangerous to women. Each year in the town of [Hackås](./Hackås \"Hackås\") in southern Jämtland an annual [traditional music](./Traditional_Nordic_dance_music \"Traditional Nordic dance music\") contest *[Årets Näck](./Årets_Näck \"Årets Näck\")* is held where each contestant impersonates the Nix.\\n\\nIn Jämtland the [vættir](./Vættir \"Vættir\")/[dwarves](./Dwarf_(mythology) \"Dwarf (mythology)\") goes by the name *jolbyggar* \"earth builders\". They herd large white goats and cows and live underground, they are considered innocuous though sometimes they exchange an unbaptized child for a so-called *bytningsbarn*. They are commonly associated with the grazing lands.[[31]](./Jämtland#cite_note-p_98-31) They also go by the names *småruskan*, *smågubban* and *småtussan*.\\n\\n### Folk costumes\\n\\nJämtland has several different types of folk costumes or *[bunads](./Bunad \"Bunad\")*. Unlike certain regions in Scandinavia a unitary bunad did not exist in Jämtland\\'s parishes, with the exception of [Hammerdal parish](./Hammerdal_parish?action=edit&redlink=1 \"Hammerdal parish\") with its [brown](./Brown \"Brown\")-striped clothing.\\n\\nUsually Jämtland is divided into three different clothing parts, the North Jamtish ([Hammerdal](./Hammerdal_Court_District \"Hammerdal Court District\")), the East Jamtish ([Ragunda](./Ragunda_Court_District \"Ragunda Court District\")) and the Great Jamtish area, covering the rest and the majority of Jämtland.\\n\\nThe North Jamtish clothing part is typically influenced by the folk costumes of northern Ångermanland and to a lesser degree Lapland, with the exception of [Frostviken parish](./Frostviken_parish?action=edit&redlink=1 \"Frostviken parish\") settled by [Trønders](./Trøndersk \"Trøndersk\") in the 18th century. The East Jamtish part is the least old-fashioned of the three with many changes done to the costumes through time, making them closer to the kind used at the Swedish coast, rather than the others in Jämtland. The Great Jamtish part has typically old-fashioned and conservative homogeneous bunads with blue socks, red knitted caps among the males, dark bounded caps for ladies and coloured for girls. The skirts are usually of a single colour and the men have blue or black [hodden](./Hodden \"Hodden\") [coats](./Coat_(clothing) \"Coat (clothing)\"), with yellow [chamois leather](./Chamois_leather \"Chamois leather\") pants made from moose skin.\\n\\n### Dialects\\n\\nThe genuine dialect of Jämtland is [Jamtish](./Jamtish \"Jamtish\"). The speakers of the dialect refer to it as *Jamska* ([ˈjamskɐ]), which is a definite form that translates to English as \"the Jamtish\". However, due to the lack of a well-established English name of the dialect both Jamtish and Jamtlandic are used.\\n\\nJamtish is in fact a group of dialects and there are distinctive dialects in every parish. Though they are usually classified in four groups; *framlänningsmålet* \"the Central Jamtish tongue\", *opplänningsmålet* (spoken in Western Jämtland), Southwest Jamtish and Northern Jamtish. The dialects in eastern Jämtland are sometimes considered as a fifth group of Jamtish, but also as dialects more related to the Swedish dialects spoken in [Ångermanland](./Ångermanland \"Ångermanland\"). In the very north of Jämtland *lidmål*, a version of [Trøndersk](./Trøndersk \"Trøndersk\"), is spoken. Jamtish is spoken by 50 000 people at most living in Jämtland and in other areas of Sweden, particularly the capital [Stockholm](./Stockholm \"Stockholm\").\\n\\n|  |  |\\n| --- | --- |\\n| *Veit vår gräse ahllten e, brano grönt*  *å grönar tre, veit vår all får væ i fre?*  *Veit vår ingenting e svårst*  *å e öft, e huskut kort*  *om nättran er e lagom mårt?*  *De e västa nola værln*  *å åsta sönna hagan*  *nola västa sjön*  *å sönna åsta dagom*  - From [Triakel](./Triakel \"Triakel\")\\'s song **Veit**[[32]](./Jämtland#cite_note-32) | *Where d\\'you find a life of ease, green grass*   *and greener trees, gently waving in the breeze?*  *Where d\\'you think the bugs don\\'t bite*  *And the work, as quick and light?*  *Where\\'s it hardly dark at night?*  *It\\'s to the east of the waning moon*  *And to the west of the wide horizon,*  *North of where the sun goes down*  *And south of where it\\'s rising.*   English version of the same song, though not a literal translation. |\\n\\n### Language\\n\\nEven if the Jamtish official status is a dialect many Jamtish people see it as an own language. There are multiple activists that are trying to make the Swedish government recognise Jamtish as a minority language just as [Yiddish](./Yiddish \"Yiddish\") or [Sami](./Sami_people \"Sami people\") have become one. The claimers say to look at the different words and pronunciations of them. Whether or not it is its own language has been widely debated since the early 20th century.\\n\\n### Provincial character\\n\\nHistorically each province in Sweden has been known for a specific provincial character or *[volksgeist](./Volksgeist \"Volksgeist\")*. This was a field of intense research in Sweden earlier but is viewed somewhat unmodern and considered prejudice today.\\n\\nThe provincial character of Jämtland was often portrayed as cheerful and the population have historically been known for their hospitality. Before the dawn of the railway it was common among farmers to leave their doors unlocked when the annual summer journey to the critter houses was due, often with the table set with food for travelers.\\n\\n[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8b/Ostersund.JPG/250px-Ostersund.JPG)](./File:Ostersund.JPG)\\n\\nÖstersund was founded to stop the faring traditions in Jämtland. This happened first after the railroad was established and the city is now the trading center of Jämtland.\\n\\nThe faring traditions of Jämtland are also very characteristic. The Jamts were known to neglect the agriculture and instead take on long trading journeys all over Scandinavia to various [markets](./Market_(place) \"Market (place)\") such as the ancients ones in [Levanger](./Levanger_(town) \"Levanger (town)\") and [Gregorius market](./Gregorius_market?action=edit&redlink=1 \"Gregorius market\") on Frösön. This was regarded as sheer pleasure in itself and not as something they were obligated to do. In the middle of the 18th century Jämtland\\'s population was roughly 20 000 and it was common that over 1 000 Jamts were present during *Marsimartnan* in Levanger, it is also claimed that the city was built solely on spikes from Jämtland before the fire in the 19th century. The journeys took place during the winters when the landscape was more accessible (when [swamps](./Swamp \"Swamp\"), lakes and [tarns](./Tarn_(lake) \"Tarn (lake)\") froze to ice) and was conducted by males, which left the females in complete charge of the [household](./Household \"Household\") and the [property](./Property \"Property\"). The journeys were well-organized [expeditions](./Exploration \"Exploration\") and no one traveled alone. These traditions has awarded the Jamt with traits such as enterprising and energetic. The Jamts\\' attempts to avoid tariffs were very successful which greatly angered Swedish officials through time. These journeys eventually stopped once the railway came, though it has recently been renewed by locals. Some say that the heritage from this age lives on, given the high number of enterprises per capita.\\n\\n### Republic of Jamtland\\n\\nMain article: [Republic of Jamtland](./Republic_of_Jamtland \"Republic of Jamtland\")\\n\\n[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/09/Unofficial_Flag_of_Jamtland.svg/250px-Unofficial_Flag_of_Jamtland.svg.png)](./File:Unofficial_Flag_of_Jamtland.svg)\\n\\n[Flag of the Republic of Jamtland](./Flag_of_the_Republic_of_Jamtland \"Flag of the Republic of Jamtland\")\\n\\nIn the 1960s, an [independence movement](./Independence_movement \"Independence movement\") calling itself the \"Republic of Jamtland\" was created by humorist/actor/director [Yngve Gamlin](./Yngve_Gamlin \"Yngve Gamlin\"). Motivated on paper as an attempt to return the province to Jamtlandic control, the republic was given some form of recognition in 1967 when Mr. Gamlin was invited to an event for visiting statesmen hosted by Swedish prime minister [Tage Erlander](./Tage_Erlander \"Tage Erlander\"). Described in some sources as a form of criticism against [centralized](./Centralized \"Centralized\") Swedish government and in others as a [marketing](./Marketing \"Marketing\") ploy, it is likely that both played some part in its foundation (Republic officials typically describe it as \"51 percent serious\"). The republic has a self-styled [flag](./Flag_of_the_Republic_of_Jamtland \"Flag of the Republic of Jamtland\") and national anthem ([Jämtlandssången](./Jämtlandssången \"Jämtlandssången\")) and the independence movement hosts the annual [Storsjöyran](./Storsjöyran \"Storsjöyran\") event in the capital, [Östersund](./Östersund \"Östersund\").\\n\\n### Sports\\n\\nFootball in the province is administered by [Jämtland-Härjedalens Fotbollförbund](./Jämtland-Härjedalens_Fotbollförbund \"Jämtland-Härjedalens Fotbollförbund\"). | |\\n| Website | [qld.gov.au](http://qld.gov.au) |\\n\\n**Queensland** (locally [/ˈkwiːnzlænd/](./Help:IPA/English \"Help:IPA/English\") [*KWEENZ-land*](./Help:Pronunciation_respelling_key \"Help:Pronunciation respelling key\"),[[note 1]](./Queensland#cite_note-9) commonly abbreviated as **QLD**) is a [state](./States_and_territories_of_Australia \"States and territories of Australia\") in northeastern [Australia](./Australia \"Australia\"), the second-largest and third-most populous state in Australia. It is bordered by the [Northern Territory](./Northern_Territory \"Northern Territory\"), [South Australia](./South_Australia \"South Australia\") and [New South Wales](./New_South_Wales \"New South Wales\") to the west, south-west and south, respectively. To the east, Queensland is bordered by the [Coral Sea](./Coral_Sea \"Coral Sea\") and the [Pacific Ocean](./Pacific_Ocean \"Pacific Ocean\"); to the state\\'s north is the [Torres Strait](./Torres_Strait \"Torres Strait\"), separating the Australian mainland from [Papua New Guinea](./Papua_New_Guinea \"Papua New Guinea\"), and the [Gulf of Carpentaria](./Gulf_of_Carpentaria \"Gulf of Carpentaria\") to the north-west. With an area of 1,723,030 square kilometres (665,270\\xa0sq\\xa0mi), Queensland is the world\\'s [sixth-largest subdivision](./List_of_country_subdivisions_by_area \"List of country subdivisions by area\") of any country on earth; it [is larger than all but 16 countries](./List_of_countries_and_dependencies_by_area \"List of countries and dependencies by area\"). Due to its size, Queensland\\'s geographical features and climates are diverse, and include [tropical rainforests](./Tropical_rainforest \"Tropical rainforest\"), [rivers](./River \"River\"), [coral reefs](./Coral_reef \"Coral reef\"), [mountain ranges](./Mountain_range \"Mountain range\") and white sandy beaches in its [tropical](./Tropical_climate \"Tropical climate\") and [sub-tropical](./Humid_subtropical_climate \"Humid subtropical climate\") coastal regions, as well as [deserts](./Desert \"Desert\") and [savanna](./Savanna \"Savanna\") in the [semi-arid](./Semi-arid_climate \"Semi-arid climate\") and [desert](./Desert_climate \"Desert climate\") climatic regions of its [interior](./Outback \"Outback\").\\n\\nQueensland has a population of over 5.5 million,[[9]](./Queensland#cite_note-ABSPop-10) concentrated in [South East Queensland](./South_East_Queensland \"South East Queensland\"), where nearly three in four reside. The capital and largest city in the state is [Brisbane](./Brisbane \"Brisbane\"), Australia\\'s [third-largest city](./List_of_cities_in_Australia_by_population \"List of cities in Australia by population\") and comprising fully half of the state\\'s population. Ten of Australia\\'s thirty largest cities are located in Queensland, the largest outside Brisbane being the [Gold Coast](./Gold_Coast,_Queensland \"Gold Coast, Queensland\"), the [Sunshine Coast](./Sunshine_Coast,_Queensland \"Sunshine Coast, Queensland\"), [Townsville](./Townsville \"Townsville\"), [Cairns](./Cairns \"Cairns\"), [Ipswich](./Ipswich,_Queensland \"Ipswich, Queensland\"), and [Toowoomba](./Toowoomba \"Toowoomba\"). 24.2% of the state\\'s population were [born overseas](./Immigration_to_Australia \"Immigration to Australia\").[[10]](./Queensland#cite_note-11) The state has the highest inter-state net migration in Australia.[[11]](./Queensland#cite_note-12)\\n\\nQueensland was first inhabited by [Aboriginal Australians](./Aboriginal_Australians \"Aboriginal Australians\"), with the [Torres Strait Islands](./Torres_Strait_Islands \"Torres Strait Islands\") inhabited by [Torres Strait Islanders](./Torres_Strait_Islanders \"Torres Strait Islanders\").[[12]](./Queensland#cite_note-13) Dutch navigator [Willem Janszoon](./Willem_Janszoon \"Willem Janszoon\"), the first European to land in Australia, explored the west coast of the [Cape York Peninsula](./Cape_York_Peninsula \"Cape York Peninsula\") in 1606. In 1770, [James Cook](./James_Cook \"James Cook\") claimed the east coast of Australia for the [Kingdom of Great Britain](./Kingdom_of_Great_Britain \"Kingdom of Great Britain\"). In 1788, [Arthur Phillip](./Arthur_Phillip \"Arthur Phillip\") founded the colony of New South Wales, which included all of what is now Queensland. Queensland was explored in subsequent decades, and the [Moreton Bay Penal Settlement](./Moreton_Bay_Penal_Settlement \"Moreton Bay Penal Settlement\") was established at Brisbane in 1824 by [John Oxley](./John_Oxley \"John Oxley\"). During the [Australian frontier wars](./Australian_frontier_wars \"Australian frontier wars\") of the 19th century, colonists killed tens of thousands of Aboriginal people in Queensland while consolidating their control over the territory.\\n\\nOn 6 June 1859 (now commemorated as [Queensland Day](./Queensland_Day \"Queensland Day\")), [Queen Victoria](./Queen_Victoria \"Queen Victoria\") signed the letters patent to establish the colony of Queensland, [separating it from New South Wales](./Separation_of_Queensland \"Separation of Queensland\") and thereby establishing Queensland as a [self-governing](./Self-governing_colony \"Self-governing colony\") [Crown colony](./Crown_colony \"Crown colony\") with [responsible government](./Responsible_government \"Responsible government\"). A large part of colonial Queensland\\'s economy relied on [blackbirded](./Blackbirding \"Blackbirding\") South Sea Islander slavery.[*[citation needed](./Wikipedia:Citation_needed \"Wikipedia:Citation needed\")*]\\n\\nQueensland was among the six colonies which became the founding states of Australia with [Federation](./Federation_of_Australia \"Federation of Australia\") on 1 January 1901. Since the [Bjelke-Petersen](./Joh_Bjelke-Petersen \"Joh Bjelke-Petersen\") era of the late 20th century, Queensland has received a high level of internal migration from the other states and territories of Australia and remains a popular destination for interstate migration.\\n\\nQueensland has the [third-largest economy](./List_of_Australian_states_and_territories_by_gross_state_product \"List of Australian states and territories by gross state product\") among Australian states, with strengths in mining, agriculture, transportation, [international education](./International_student \"International student\"), insurance, and banking. Nicknamed the *Sunshine State* for its tropical and sub-tropical climates, [Great Barrier Reef](./Great_Barrier_Reef \"Great Barrier Reef\"), and numerous beaches, tourism is also important to the state\\'s economy.\\n\\nHistory\\n-------\\n\\nMain article: [History of Queensland](./History_of_Queensland \"History of Queensland\")\\n\\n### Pre-European contact\\n\\nMain article: [History of Indigenous Australians](./History_of_Indigenous_Australians \"History of Indigenous Australians\")\\n\\nQueensland was one of the largest regions of pre-colonial Aboriginal population in Australia.[[13]](./Queensland#cite_note-FOOTNOTEØrsted-Jensen201110–11-14) The Aboriginal ownership of Queensland is thought to predate 50,000\\xa0BC, and early migrants are believed to have arrived via boat or land bridge across [Torres Strait](./Torres_Strait \"Torres Strait\"). Through time, their descendants developed into more than 90 different language and cultural groups.\\n\\nDuring the last [ice age](./Ice_age \"Ice age\"), Queensland\\'s landscape became more arid and largely desolate, making food and other supplies scarce. The people developed the world\\'s first seed-grinding technology.[[14]](./Queensland#cite_note-15) The end of the [glacial period](./Glacial_period \"Glacial period\") brought about a warming climate, making the land more hospitable. It brought high rainfall along the eastern coast, stimulating the growth of the state\\'s tropical rainforests.[[15]](./Queensland#cite_note-r-evans-hoq-16)\\n\\nThe [Torres Strait Islands](./Torres_Strait_Islands \"Torres Strait Islands\") is home to the [Torres Strait Islander peoples](./Torres_Strait_Islanders \"Torres Strait Islanders\"). Torres Strait Islanders are ethnically and culturally distinct from mainland Aboriginal peoples. They have a long history of interaction with both Aboriginal peoples of what is now Australia and the peoples of [New Guinea](./New_Guinea \"New Guinea\").\\n\\n### European colonisation\\n\\n[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/ca/Captain_Cook_at_Possession_Island.jpg/330px-Captain_Cook_at_Possession_Island.jpg)](./File:Captain_Cook_at_Possession_Island.jpg)\\n\\nCaptain [James Cook](./James_Cook \"James Cook\") claims the [east coast of Australia](./Eastern_states_of_Australia \"Eastern states of Australia\") for the [Kingdom of Great Britain](./Kingdom_of_Great_Britain \"Kingdom of Great Britain\") at [Possession Island](./Possession_Island_(Queensland) \"Possession Island (Queensland)\") in 1770\\n\\n[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9a/SeventeenSeventyNov082024_01.jpg/330px-SeventeenSeventyNov082024_01.jpg)](./File:SeventeenSeventyNov082024_01.jpg)\\n\\nThe peninsula of [Seventeen Seventy, Queensland](./Seventeen_Seventy,_Queensland \"Seventeen Seventy, Queensland\"), where Captain Cook landed in 1770\\n\\n[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/98/Bulla_Queensland_1861.jpg/330px-Bulla_Queensland_1861.jpg)](./File:Bulla_Queensland_1861.jpg)\\n\\nFighting between [Burke and Wills](./Burke_and_Wills_expedition \"Burke and Wills expedition\")\\'s supply party and Aboriginal Australians at Bulla in 1861\\n\\nIn February 1606, Dutch navigator [Willem Janszoon](./Willem_Janszoon \"Willem Janszoon\") landed near the site of what is now [Weipa](./Weipa,_Queensland \"Weipa, Queensland\"), on the western shore of [Cape York](./Cape_York_Peninsula \"Cape York Peninsula\"). This was the first recorded landing of a European in [Australia](./Australia \"Australia\"), and it also marked the first reported contact between Europeans and the [Aboriginal people of Australia](./Aboriginal_people_of_Australia \"Aboriginal people of Australia\").[[15]](./Queensland#cite_note-r-evans-hoq-16) The region was also explored by French and Spanish explorers (commanded by [Louis Antoine de Bougainville](./Louis_Antoine_de_Bougainville \"Louis Antoine de Bougainville\") and [Luís Vaez de Torres](./Luís_Vaez_de_Torres \"Luís Vaez de Torres\"), respectively) before the arrival of Lieutenant [James Cook](./James_Cook \"James Cook\") in 1770. Cook claimed the east coast under instruction from [King George III](./King_George_III \"King George III\") of the [Kingdom of Great Britain](./Kingdom_of_Great_Britain \"Kingdom of Great Britain\") on 22 August 1770 at [Possession Island](./Possession_Island_(Queensland) \"Possession Island (Queensland)\"), naming eastern Australia, including Queensland, *New South Wales*.[[16]](./Queensland#cite_note-17)\\n\\nThe Aboriginal population declined significantly after a [smallpox epidemic](./History_of_smallpox#Pacific_epidemics \"History of smallpox\") during the late 18th century and massacres by the European settlers.[[17]](./Queensland#cite_note-18)[*[page\\xa0needed](./Wikipedia:Citing_sources \"Wikipedia:Citing sources\")*]\\n\\nIn 1823, [John Oxley](./John_Oxley \"John Oxley\"), a British explorer, sailed north from what is now [Sydney](./Sydney \"Sydney\") to scout possible penal colony sites in [Gladstone](./Gladstone,_Queensland \"Gladstone, Queensland\") (then [Port Curtis](./Port_Curtis \"Port Curtis\")) and [Moreton Bay](./Moreton_Bay \"Moreton Bay\"). At Moreton Bay, he found the [Brisbane River](./Brisbane_River \"Brisbane River\"). He returned in 1824 and established a penal settlement at what is now [Redcliffe](./Redcliffe_Peninsula \"Redcliffe Peninsula\"). The settlement, initially known as [Edenglassie](./Edenglassie \"Edenglassie\"), was then transferred to the current location of the [Brisbane city centre](./Brisbane_central_business_district \"Brisbane central business district\"). [Edmund Lockyer](./Edmund_Lockyer \"Edmund Lockyer\") discovered outcrops of coal along the banks of the upper Brisbane River in 1825.[[18]](./Queensland#cite_note-19) In 1839 transportation of convicts was ceased, culminating in the closure of the Brisbane penal settlement. In 1842 free settlement, which had already commenced, was officially permitted. In 1847, the [Port of Maryborough](./Port_of_Maryborough \"Port of Maryborough\") was opened as a wool port. While most early immigrants came from New South Wales, the first free immigrant ship to arrive in Moreton Bay from Europe was the [*Artemisia*](./Artemisia_(ship) \"Artemisia (ship)\"), in 1848.\\n\\nEarlier than this immigrant ship was the arrival of the Irish famine orphan girls to Queensland. Devised by the then British Secretary of State for the Colonies, The Earl Grey Scheme established a special emigration scheme which was designed to resettle destitute girls from the workhouses of Ireland during the Great Famine. The first ship, the \"Earl Grey\", departed Ireland for a 124-day sail to Sydney. After controversy developed upon their arrival in Australia, a small group of 37 young orphans, sometimes referred to as The Belfast Girls or the Feisty Colleens, never set foot on Sydney soil, and instead sailed up to Brisbane (then Moreton Bay) on 21 October 1848 on board the *Ann Mary*. This scheme continued until 1852.[[19]](./Queensland#cite_note-20)\\n\\nIn 1857, Queensland\\'s first lighthouse was built at [Cape Moreton](./Cape_Moreton \"Cape Moreton\").[[20]](./Queensland#cite_note-21)\\n\\n### Frontier wars and massacres\\n\\nFurther information: [Australian frontier wars §\\xa0Queensland](./Australian_frontier_wars#Queensland \"Australian frontier wars\"), and [List of massacres of Indigenous Australians §\\xa0Queensland](./List_of_massacres_of_Indigenous_Australians#Queensland \"List of massacres of Indigenous Australians\")\\n\\nThe frontier wars fought between European settlers and Aboriginal tribes in Queensland were the bloodiest and most brutal in colonial Australia.[[21]](./Queensland#cite_note-22) Many of these conflicts are now seen as acts of genocide.[[22]](./Queensland#cite_note-23)[[23]](./Queensland#cite_note-24)[[24]](./Queensland#cite_note-queteen-25)[[25]](./Queensland#cite_note-26)\\n\\nThe wars featured the most frequent massacres of First Nations people, the three deadliest massacres on white settlers, the most disreputable frontier police force, and the highest number of white victims to frontier violence on record in any Australian colony.[[26]](./Queensland#cite_note-FOOTNOTEØrsted-Jensen2011-27) Across at least 644 collisions at least 66,680 were killed — with Aboriginal fatalities alone comprising no less than 65,180.[[27]](./Queensland#cite_note-ReferenceA-28) Of these deaths, around 24,000 Aboriginal men, women and children were killed by the Native Police between 1859 and 1897.[[28]](./Queensland#cite_note-29)\\n\\nThe military force of the Queensland Government in this war was the [Native Police](./Australian_native_police \"Australian native police\"), who operated from 1849 to the 1920s. The Native Police was a body of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander troopers that operated under the command of white officers. The Native Police were often recruited forcefully from far-away communities.[[29]](./Queensland#cite_note-30)[[30]](./Queensland#cite_note-31)\\n\\n[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/02/Wills_Tragedy_1861.jpg/250px-Wills_Tragedy_1861.jpg)](./File:Wills_Tragedy_1861.jpg)\\n\\nAftermath of the 1861 [Cullin-La-Ringo massacre](./Cullin-La-Ringo_massacre \"Cullin-La-Ringo massacre\") in which 19 settlers were killed by Aboriginal people, the deadliest attack on settlers in the frontier wars\\n\\nConflict spread quickly with free settlement in 1838, with settlement rapidly expanding in a great rush to take up the surrounding land in the [Darling Downs](./Darling_Downs \"Darling Downs\"), Logan and Brisbane Valley and South Burnett onwards from 1840, in many cases leading to widespread fighting and heavy loss of life. The conflict later spread north to the [Wide Bay](./Wide_Bay–Burnett \"Wide Bay–Burnett\") and [Burnett River](./Burnett_River \"Burnett River\") and [Hervey Bay](./Hervey_Bay \"Hervey Bay\") region, and at one stage the settlement of [Maryborough](./Maryborough,_Queensland \"Maryborough, Queensland\") was virtually under siege.[[31]](./Queensland#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBroome1988102-32)\\n\\nThe largest reasonably well-documented massacres in southeast Queensland were the [Kilcoy](./Kilcoy,_Queensland \"Kilcoy, Queensland\") and [Whiteside](./Whiteside,_Queensland \"Whiteside, Queensland\") poisonings, each of which was said to have taken up to 70 Aboriginal lives by use of a gift of flour laced with [strychnine](./Strychnine \"Strychnine\"). At the [Battle of One Tree Hill](./Battle_of_One_Tree_Hill \"Battle of One Tree Hill\") in September 1843, [Multuggerah](./Multuggerah \"Multuggerah\") and his group of warriors ambushed one group of settlers, routing them and subsequently others in the skirmishes which followed, starting in retaliation for the Kilcoy poisoning.[[32]](./Queensland#cite_note-kerkhove-33)[[33]](./Queensland#cite_note-marr-34)\\n\\nCentral Queensland was particularly hard hit during the 1860s and 1870s, several contemporary writers mention the Skull Hole, Bladensburg, or Mistake Creek massacre[[a]](./Queensland#cite_note-35) on [Bladensburg Station](./Bladensburg_Station \"Bladensburg Station\") near [Winton](./Winton,_Queensland \"Winton, Queensland\"), which in 1901 was said to have taken up to 200 Aboriginal lives.[[34]](./Queensland#cite_note-36) First Nations warriors killed 19 settlers during the [Cullin-La-Ringo massacre](./Cullin-La-Ringo_massacre \"Cullin-La-Ringo massacre\") on 17 October 1861.[[35]](./Queensland#cite_note-FOOTNOTEConnor2008220-37) In the weeks afterwards, police, native police and civilians killed up to 370 members of the [Gayiri](./Gayiri \"Gayiri\") Aboriginal people in response.[[36]](./Queensland#cite_note-Jackson-38)\\n\\nFrontier violence peaked on the northern mining frontier during the 1870s, most notably in Cook district and on the [Palmer](./Palmer_River_(Queensland) \"Palmer River (Queensland)\") and Hodgkinson River goldfields, with heavy loss of Aboriginal lives and several well-known massacres.[[37]](./Queensland#cite_note-39) Raids conducted by the [Kalkadoon](./Kalkatungu \"Kalkatungu\") held settlers out of Western Queensland for ten years until September 1884 when they attacked a force of settlers and native police at Battle Mountain near modern [Cloncurry](./Cloncurry,_Queensland \"Cloncurry, Queensland\"). The subsequent battle of Battle Mountain ended in disaster for the Kalkadoon, who suffered heavy losses.[[38]](./Queensland#cite_note-FOOTNOTECoulthard-Clark200151–52-40) Fighting continued in [North Queensland](./North_Queensland \"North Queensland\"), however, with First Nations raiders attacking sheep and cattle while Native Police mounted heavy retaliatory massacres.[[39]](./Queensland#cite_note-FOOTNOTEConnor2008221-41)[[40]](./Queensland#cite_note-42)\\n\\n### Blackbirding\\n\\nFurther information: [Blackbirding §\\xa0Queensland](./Blackbirding#Queensland \"Blackbirding\")\\n\\n[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/13/Groupe_de_Kanakas_dans_une_exploitation_de_canne_%C3%A0_sucre_du_Queensland.jpg/250px-Groupe_de_Kanakas_dans_une_exploitation_de_canne_%C3%A0_sucre_du_Queensland.jpg)](./File:Groupe_de_Kanakas_dans_une_exploitation_de_canne_à_sucre_du_Queensland.jpg)\\n\\n[Kanaka workers](./Kanaka_(Pacific_Island_worker) \"Kanaka (Pacific Island worker)\") in a sugar cane plantation, late 19th century\\n\\nTens of thousands of [South Sea Islanders](./South_Sea_Islanders \"South Sea Islanders\") were forced, deceived or coerced into [indentured servitude](./Indentured_servitude \"Indentured servitude\") and slavery on Australia\\'s agricultural plantations, despite slavery being outlawed in Australia and other parts of the [British Empire](./British_Empire \"British Empire\") by the [Slavery Abolition Act 1833](./Slavery_Abolition_Act_1833 \"Slavery Abolition Act 1833\"). This process was known as blackbirding.[[41]](./Queensland#cite_note-Mortensen_2000-43)[[42]](./Queensland#cite_note-McDonald_2023-44)[[43]](./Queensland#cite_note-45) This trade in what were then known as [Kanakas](./Kanaka_(Pacific_Island_worker) \"Kanaka (Pacific Island worker)\") was in operation from 1863 to 1908, a period of 45 years. Some 55,000 to 62,500 were brought to Australia, most being recruited or blackbirded from islands in [Melanesia](./Melanesia \"Melanesia\"), such as the [New Hebrides](./New_Hebrides \"New Hebrides\") (now [Vanuatu](./Vanuatu \"Vanuatu\")), the [Solomon Islands](./Solomon_Islands \"Solomon Islands\") and the islands around [New Guinea](./New_Guinea \"New Guinea\").[[44]](./Queensland#cite_note-AHRC-46)\\n\\n[![South Sea Islander men standing in front of a row of sugarcane.](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f9/Australian_South_Sea_Islander_cane_cutters_on_a_sugar_cane_plantation_in_Queensland_%289205204184%29.jpg/250px-Australian_South_Sea_Islander_cane_cutters_on_a_sugar_cane_plantation_in_Queensland_%289205204184%29.jpg)](./File:Australian_South_Sea_Islander_cane_cutters_on_a_sugar_cane_plantation_in_Queensland_(9205204184).jpg)\\n\\nBlackbirded South Sea Islanders on a [Sugarcane](./Sugarcane \"Sugarcane\") plantation in Queensland\\n\\nThe majority of those taken were male and around one quarter were under the age of sixteen.[[45]](./Queensland#cite_note-47) In total, approximately 15,000 South Sea Islanders (30%) died while labouring in Queensland – excluding those who died in transit or were killed in the recruitment process – mostly during three-year contracts.[[46]](./Queensland#cite_note-48) This is similar to the estimated 33% death rate among enslaved Africans in the first three years of arriving in America,[[47]](./Queensland#cite_note-49) Brazil, and the Caribbean; the conditions were often comparable to those of the [Atlantic slave trade](./Atlantic_slave_trade \"Atlantic slave trade\").[[42]](./Queensland#cite_note-McDonald_2023-44)[[41]](./Queensland#cite_note-Mortensen_2000-43)\\n\\nThe trade was legally sanctioned and regulated under Queensland law, and prominent men such as Robert Towns made massive fortunes through blackbirding, helping to establish some of the major cities in Queensland today.[[48]](./Queensland#cite_note-50) Towns\\' agent claimed that blackbirded labourers were \"savages who did not know the use of money\" and therefore did not deserve cash wages.[[49]](./Queensland#cite_note-51)\\n\\nFollowing Federation in 1901, the [White Australia policy](./White_Australia_policy \"White Australia policy\") came into effect, which saw most foreign workers in Australia deported under the *[Pacific Island Labourers Act 1901](./Pacific_Island_Labourers_Act_1901 \"Pacific Island Labourers Act 1901\")*, which saw the Pacific Islander population of the state decrease rapidly.[[50]](./Queensland#cite_note-52)\\n\\n### Independent governance\\n\\nFurther information: [Colony of Queensland](./Colony_of_Queensland \"Colony of Queensland\")\\n\\n[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/27/StateLibQld_1_14202_Shearers_and_farm_hands_at_Jondaryan_Woolshed%2C_ca._1872.jpg/250px-StateLibQld_1_14202_Shearers_and_farm_hands_at_Jondaryan_Woolshed%2C_ca._1872.jpg)](./File:StateLibQld_1_14202_Shearers_and_farm_hands_at_Jondaryan_Woolshed,_ca._1872.jpg)\\n\\n[Sheep of troops in Brisbane, prior to departure for the [Boer War](./Second_Boer_War \"Second Boer War\") in South Africa\\n\\nA public meeting was held in 1851 to consider the proposed [separation of Queensland](./Separation_of_Queensland \"Separation of Queensland\") from New South Wales. On 6 June 1859, Queen Victoria signed letters patent[[51]](./Queensland#cite_note-53) to form the separate colony of Queensland as a [self-governing](./Self-governing_colony \"Self-governing colony\") [Crown colony](./Crown_colony \"Crown colony\") with [responsible government](./Responsible_government \"Responsible government\"). [Brisbane](./Brisbane \"Brisbane\") was selected as the capital city. On 10 December 1859, a proclamation was read by [George Bowen](./George_Bowen \"George Bowen\"), the first [Governor of Queensland](./Governor_of_Queensland \"Governor of Queensland\"), formally establishing Queensland as a separate colony from New South Wales.[[52]](./Queensland#cite_note-q150-54) On 22 May 1860 the first Queensland election was held and [Robert Herbert](./Robert_Herbert \"Robert Herbert\"), Bowen\\'s private secretary, was appointed as the first [Premier of Queensland](./Premier_of_Queensland \"Premier of Queensland\").\\n\\nIn 1865, the first rail line in the state opened between [Ipswich](./Ipswich,_Queensland \"Ipswich, Queensland\") and [Grandchester](./Grandchester \"Grandchester\"). Queensland\\'s economy expanded rapidly in 1867 after James Nash discovered gold on the [Mary River](./Mary_River_(Queensland) \"Mary River (Queensland)\") near the town of [Gympie](./Gympie \"Gympie\"), sparking a gold rush and saving the Colony of Queensland from near economic collapse. While still significant, they were on a much smaller scale than the gold rushes of Victoria and New South Wales.\\n\\nImmigration to Australia and Queensland, in particular, began in the 1850s to support the state economy. During the period from the 1860s until the early 20th century, many labourers, known at the time as [Kanakas](./Kanakas \"Kanakas\"), were brought to Queensland from neighbouring Pacific Island nations to work in the state\\'s sugar cane fields. Some of these people had been kidnapped under a process known as [blackbirding](./Blackbirding \"Blackbirding\") or press-ganging, and their employment conditions constituted an allegedly exploitative form of indentured labour. [Italian immigrants](./Italian_Australians \"Italian Australians\") entered the sugar cane industry from the 1890s.[[53]](./Queensland#cite_note-55)\\n\\nDuring the 1890s, the six Australian colonies, including Queensland, held a series of referendums which culminated in the [Federation of Australia](./Federation_of_Australia \"Federation of Australia\") on 1 January 1901. During this time, Queensland had a population of half a million people. Since then, Queensland has remained a [federated state](./Federated_state \"Federated state\") within Australia, and its population has significantly grown.\\n\\n### 20th century\\n\\n[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/fb/StateLibQld_1_114168_Returned_World_War_Two_soldiers_march_in_Queen_Street%2C_Brisbane%2C_1944.jpg/250px-StateLibQld_1_114168_Returned_World_War_Two_soldiers_march_in_Queen_Street%2C_Brisbane%2C_1944.jpg)](./File:StateLibQld_1_114168_Returned_World_War_Two_soldiers_march_in_Queen_Street,_Brisbane,_1944.jpg)\\n\\nReturned World War II soldiers march in Queen Street, Brisbane, 1944\\n\\nIn 1905 women voted in state elections for the first time. The state\\'s first university, the [University of Queensland](./University_of_Queensland \"University of Queensland\"), was established in Brisbane in 1909. In 1911, the first alternative treatments for polio were pioneered in Queensland and remain in use across the world today.[[54]](./Queensland#cite_note-56)\\n\\n[World War I](./World_War_I \"World War I\") had a [major impact on Queensland](./Queensland_in_World_War_I \"Queensland in World War I\"). Over 58,000 Queenslanders fought in World War I and over 10,000 of them died.[[55]](./Queensland#cite_note-57)\\n\\nAustralia\\'s first major airline, [Qantas](./Qantas \"Qantas\") (originally standing for \"Queensland and Northern Territory Aerial Services\"), was founded in [Winton](./Winton,_Queensland \"Winton, Queensland\") in 1920 to serve outback Queensland.\\n\\nIn 1922 Queensland abolished the [Queensland Legislative Council](./Queensland_Legislative_Council \"Queensland Legislative Council\"), becoming the only Australian state with a [unicameral](./Unicameral_legislature \"Unicameral legislature\") [parliament](./Parliaments_of_the_Australian_states_and_territories \"Parliaments of the Australian states and territories\").\\n\\nIn 1935 [cane toads](./Cane_toads_in_Australia \"Cane toads in Australia\") were deliberately introduced to Queensland from Hawaii in an unsuccessful attempt to reduce the number of French\\'s cane and greyback [cane beetles](./Cane_beetle \"Cane beetle\") that were destroying the roots of sugar cane plants, which are integral to Queensland\\'s economy. The toads have remained an environmental pest since that time. In 1962, the first commercial production of oil in Queensland and Australia began at [Moonie](./Moonie,_Queensland \"Moonie, Queensland\").\\n\\nDuring [World War II](./World_War_II \"World War II\") Brisbane became central to the [Allied](./Allies_of_World_War_II \"Allies of World War II\") campaign when the AMP Building (now called [MacArthur Central](./MacArthur_Central \"MacArthur Central\")) was used as the [South West Pacific headquarters](./South_West_Pacific_Area_(command)#Command \"South West Pacific Area (command)\") for [General Douglas MacArthur](./Douglas_MacArthur \"Douglas MacArthur\"), chief of the Allied Pacific forces, until his headquarters were moved to [Hollandia](./Jayapura \"Jayapura\") in August 1944.[[56]](./Queensland#cite_note-58) In 1942, during the war, Brisbane was the site of a violent clash between visiting US military personnel and Australian servicemen and civilians, which resulted in one death and hundreds of injuries. This incident became known colloquially as the [Battle of Brisbane](./Battle_of_Brisbane \"Battle of Brisbane\").[[57]](./Queensland#cite_note-59)\\n\\n[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2e/ITM436209_Dept_No_404_%2851763920364%29.jpg/250px-ITM436209_Dept_No_404_%2851763920364%29.jpg)](./File:ITM436209_Dept_No_404_(51763920364).jpg)\\n\\n[Queen Elizabeth II](./Queen_Elizabeth_II \"Queen Elizabeth II\") visited Brisbane in October 1982 for the [Commonwealth Games](./1982_Commonwealth_Games \"1982 Commonwealth Games\")\\n\\nThe end of World War II saw a [wave of immigration](./Post-war_immigration_to_Australia \"Post-war immigration to Australia\") from across Europe, with many more immigrants coming from [southern](./Southern_Europe \"Southern Europe\") and [eastern](./Eastern_Europe \"Eastern Europe\") Europe than in previous decades.\\n\\nIn the later decades of the 20th century, the [humid subtropical climate](./Subtropical_climate \"Subtropical climate\")—regulated by the availability of air conditioning—saw Queensland become a popular destination for migrants from interstate.[[58]](./Queensland#cite_note-60) Since that time, Queensland has continuously seen high levels of migration from the other states and territories of Australia.\\n\\nIn 1966, [Lyndon B. Johnson](./Lyndon_B._Johnson \"Lyndon B. Johnson\") became the first U.S. president to visit Queensland. During his visit, he met with Australia prime minister [Harold Holt](./Harold_Holt \"Harold Holt\").[*[citation needed](./Wikipedia:Citation_needed \"Wikipedia:Citation needed\")*]\\n\\nThe end of the [White Australia policy](./White_Australia_policy \"White Australia policy\") in 1973 saw the beginning of a wave of immigration from around the world, and most prominently from Asia, which continues to the present.\\n\\nIn 1981 the [Great Barrier Reef](./Great_Barrier_Reef \"Great Barrier Reef\") off Queensland\\'s northeast coast, one of the world\\'s largest coral reef systems, was declared a [UNESCO World Heritage Site](./UNESCO_World_Heritage_Site \"UNESCO World Heritage Site\").\\n\\n### 21st century\\n\\nIn 2003 Queensland adopted [maroon](./Maroon \"Maroon\") as the state\\'s official colour. The announcement was made as a result of an informal tradition to use maroon to represent the state in association with sporting events.[[6]](./Queensland#cite_note-state-colour-6)\\n\\nAfter three decades of record population growth, Queensland was impacted by major [floods between late 2010 and early 2011](./2010–2011_Queensland_floods \"2010–2011 Queensland floods\"), causing extensive damage and disruption across the state.[[59]](./Queensland#cite_note-Berry-61)[[60]](./Queensland#cite_note-62)\\n\\nIn 2020, Queensland was impacted by the [COVID-19 pandemic](./COVID-19_pandemic \"COVID-19 pandemic\"). (Fraser Island)](./K\\'gari_(Fraser_Island) \"K\\'gari (Fraser Island)\")\\n\\nWith a total area of 1,729,742 square kilometres (715,309 square miles), Queensland is an expansive state with a highly diverse range of climates and geographical features. If Queensland were an independent nation, it would be the world\\'s 16th largest in terms of area.\\n\\nQueensland\\'s eastern coastline borders the [Coral Sea](./Coral_Sea \"Coral Sea\"), an arm of the Pacific Ocean. The state is bordered by the [Torres Strait](./Torres_Strait \"Torres Strait\") to the north, with [Boigu Island](./Boigu_Island_(Queensland) \"Boigu Island (Queensland)\") off the coast of [New Guinea](./New_Guinea \"New Guinea\") representing the northern extreme of its territory. The triangular [Cape York Peninsula](./Cape_York_Peninsula \"Cape York Peninsula\"), which points toward New Guinea, is the northernmost part of the state\\'s mainland. West of the peninsula\\'s tip, northern Queensland is bordered by the [Gulf of Carpentaria](./Gulf_of_Carpentaria \"Gulf of Carpentaria\"). To the west, Queensland is bordered by the [Northern Territory](./Northern_Territory \"Northern Territory\"), at the [138th meridian east](./138th_meridian_east \"138th meridian east\"), and to the southwest by northeastern [South Australia](./South_Australia \"South Australia\"). The state\\'s southern border with New South Wales is constituted in the east by the [watershed](./Drainage_divide \"Drainage divide\") from [Point Danger](./Point_Danger_(Tweed_Heads) \"Point Danger (Tweed Heads)\") to the [Dumaresq River](./Dumaresq_River \"Dumaresq River\"), and the Dumaresq, [Macintyre](./Macintyre_River \"Macintyre River\") and [Barwon](./Barwon_River_(New_South_Wales) \"Barwon River (New South Wales)\") rivers. The west of the southern border is defined by the [29th parallel south](./29th_parallel_south \"29th parallel south\") (including some minor [historical encroachments](./Queensland_and_New_South_Wales_boundary_encroachments \"Queensland and New South Wales boundary encroachments\")) until it reaches South Australia.\\n\\nLike much of eastern Australia, the [Great Dividing Range](./Great_Dividing_Range \"Great Dividing Range\") runs roughly parallel with, and inland from, the coast, and areas west of the range are more arid than the humid coastal regions. The [Great Barrier Reef](./Great_Barrier_Reef \"Great Barrier Reef\"), which is the world\\'s largest [coral reef](./Coral_reef \"Coral reef\") system, runs parallel to the state\\'s [Coral Sea](./Coral_Sea \"Coral Sea\") coast between the [Torres Strait](./Torres_Strait \"Torres Strait\") and [K\\'gari (Fraser Island)](./K\\'gari_(Fraser_Island) \"K\\'gari (Fraser Island)\"). Queensland\\'s coastline includes the world\\'s three largest sand islands: [K\\'gari (Fraser Island)](./K\\'gari_(Fraser_Island) \"K\\'gari (Fraser Island)\"), [Moreton](./Moreton_Island \"Moreton Island\"), and [North Stradbroke](./North_Stradbroke_Island \"North Stradbroke Island\").\\n\\nThe state contains six [World Heritage](./World_Heritage_Site \"World Heritage Site\")-listed preservation areas: the Great Barrier Reef along the Coral Sea coast, K\\'gari (Fraser Island) on the [Wide Bay–Burnett](./Wide_Bay–Burnett \"Wide Bay–Burnett\") region\\'s coastline, the [wet tropics](./Wet_Tropics_of_Queensland \"Wet Tropics of Queensland\") in [Far North Queensland](./Far_North_Queensland \"Far North Queensland\") including the [Daintree Rainforest](./Daintree_Rainforest \"Daintree Rainforest\"), [Lamington National Park](./Lamington_National_Park \"Lamington National Park\") in [South East Queensland](./South_East_Queensland \"South East Queensland\"), the [Riversleigh fossil sites](./Australian_Fossil_Mammal_Sites_(Riversleigh) \"Australian Fossil Mammal Sites (Riversleigh)\") in [North West Queensland](./Gulf_Country \"Gulf Country\"), and the [Gondwana Rainforests](./Gondwana_Rainforests \"Gondwana Rainforests\") in South East Queensland.\\n\\nThe state is divided into several [unofficial regions](./Regions_of_Queensland \"Regions of Queensland\") which are commonly used to refer to large areas of the state\\'s vast geography. These include:\\n\\n* **[South East Queensland](./South_East_Queensland \"South East Queensland\")** in the state\\'s coastal extreme south-eastern corner, an urban region which includes the state\\'s three largest cities: capital city Brisbane and popular coastal tourist destinations the [Gold Coast](./Gold_Coast,_Queensland \"Gold Coast, Queensland\") and [Sunshine Coast](./Sunshine_Coast,_Queensland \"Sunshine Coast, Queensland\"). In some definitions, it also includes the city of [Toowoomba](./Toowoomba,_Queensland \"Toowoomba, Queensland\"). South East Queensland accounts for more than 70% of the state\\'s population.\\n* The **[Darling Downs](./Darling_Downs \"Darling Downs\")** in the state\\'s inland southeast, which consists of fertile agricultural (particularly cattle grazing) land and in some definitions includes the city of Toowoomba. The region also includes the mountainous [Granite Belt](./Granite_Belt \"Granite Belt\"), the state\\'s coldest region which occasionally experiences snow.\\n* **[Wide Bay–Burnett](./Wide_Bay–Burnett \"Wide Bay–Burnett\")** in the state\\'s coastal southeast, to the north of the South East Queensland region. It is rich in [sugar cane](./Sugar_cane \"Sugar cane\") farms and includes the cities of [Bundaberg](./Bundaberg \"Bundaberg\"), [Hervey Bay](./Hervey_Bay \"Hervey Bay\") as well as [K\\'gari (Fraser Island)](./K\\'gari_(Fraser_Island) \"K\\'gari (Fraser Island)\"), the world\\'s largest sand island.\\n* **[Central Queensland](./Central_Queensland \"Central Queensland\")** on the state\\'s central coastline, which is dominated by cattle farmland and coal mining. It contains the [Capricorn Coast](./Capricorn_Coast \"Capricorn Coast\") and [Whitsunday Islands](./Whitsunday_Islands \"Whitsunday Islands\") tourist regions, as well as the cities of [Rockhampton](./Rockhampton \"Rockhampton\") and [Mackay](./Mackay,_Queensland \"Mackay, Queensland\").\\n* **[North Queensland](./North_Queensland \"North Queensland\")** on the state\\'s northern coastline, which is dominated by cattle farmland and mining and which includes the city of [Townsville](./Townsville \"Townsville\").\\n* **[Far North Queensland](./Far_North_Queensland \"Far North Queensland\")** on the state\\'s extreme northern coastline along the [Cape York Peninsula](./Cape_York_Peninsula \"Cape York Peninsula\"), which includes [tropical rainforest](./Tropical_rainforest Climate\\n\\n[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/12/Queensland_K%C3%B6ppen.svg/250px-Queensland_K%C3%B6ppen.svg.png)](./File:Queensland_Köppen.svg)\\n\\n[Köppen climate types](./Köppen_climate_classification \"Köppen climate classification\") in Queensland\\n\\nBecause of its size, there is significant variation in climate across the state. There is ample rainfall along the coastline, with a [monsoonal](./Monsoon \"Monsoon\") wet season in the [tropical](./Tropical_climate \"Tropical climate\") north, and [humid sub-tropical](./Humid_subtropical_climate \"Humid subtropical climate\") conditions along the southern coastline. Low rainfall and hot humid summers are typical for the inland and west. Elevated areas in the south-eastern inland can experience temperatures well below freezing in mid-winter providing [frost](./Frost \"Frost\") and, rarely, [snowfall](./Snowfall \"Snowfall\"). The climate of the coastal regions is influenced by warm ocean waters, keeping the region free from extremes of temperature and providing moisture for rainfall.[[61]](./Queensland#cite_note-63)\\n\\nThere are six predominant climatic zones in Queensland,[[62]](./Queensland#cite_note-64) based on temperature and humidity:\\n\\n* Hot humid summer, warm humid winter (far north and coastal): [Cairns](./Cairns \"Cairns\"), [Innisfail](./Innisfail,_Queensland \"Innisfail, Queensland\")\\n* Hot humid summer, warm dry winter (north and coastal): [Townsville](./Townsville \"Townsville\"), [Mackay](./Mackay,_Queensland \"Mackay, Queensland\")\\n* Hot humid summer, mild dry winter (coastal elevated areas and coastal south-east): Isa](./Mt_Isa \"Mt Isa\"), [Emerald](./Emerald,_Queensland \"Emerald, Queensland\"), [Longreach](./Longreach \"Longreach\")\\n* Hot dry summer, cool dry winter (southern inland): The most northerly snow ever recorded in Australia occurred near [Mackay](./Mackay,_Queensland \"Mackay, Queensland\"); however, this was exceptional.[[69]](./Queensland#cite_note-71)\\n\\nNatural disasters are often a threat in Queensland: severe [tropical cyclones](./Tropical_cyclone \"Tropical cyclone\") can impact the central and northern coastlines and cause severe damage,[[70]](./Queensland#cite_note-72) with recent examples including [Larry](./Cyclone_Larry \"Cyclone Larry\"), [Yasi](./Cyclone_Yasi \"Cyclone Yasi\"), [Ita](./Cyclone_Ita \"Cyclone Ita\") and [Debbie](./Cyclone_Debbie \"Cyclone Debbie\"). Flooding from rain-bearing systems can also be severe and can occur anywhere in Queensland. One of the deadliest and most damaging floods in the history of the state occurred in [early 2011](./2010-11_Queensland_floods \"2010-11 Queensland floods\").[[71]](./Queensland#cite_note-73) Severe springtime [thunderstorms](./Thunderstorm \"Thunderstorm\") generally affect the south-east and inland of the state and can bring damaging winds, torrential rain, large [hail](./Hail \"Hail\") and even [tornadoes](./Tornado \"Tornado\").[[72]](./Queensland#cite_note-74) The [strongest tornado](./Bucca_tornado \"Bucca tornado\") ever recorded in Australia occurred in Queensland near [Bundaberg](./Bundaberg \"Bundaberg\") in November 1992.[[73]](./Queensland#cite_note-75) Droughts and [bushfires](./Bushfires_in_Australia \"Bushfires in Australia\") can also occur; however, the latter are generally less severe than those that occur in southern states.\\n\\nThe highest official maximum temperature recorded in the state was 49.5\\xa0°C (121.1\\xa0°F) at Birdsville Police Education\\n\\n[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/28/University_of_Queensland.jpg/250px-University_of_Queensland.jpg)](./File:University_of_Queensland.jpg)\\n\\nThe Great Court at the [University of Queensland](./University_of_Queensland \"University of Queensland\") in Brisbane, Queensland\\'s oldest university\\n\\nQueensland is home to numerous universities. The state\\'s oldest university, the [University of Queensland](./University_of_Queensland \"University of Queensland\"), was established in 1909 and frequently [ranks among the world\\'s top 50](./College_and_university_rankings \"College and university rankings\").[[92]](./Queensland#cite_note-100)[[93]](./Queensland#cite_note-101)[[94]](./Queensland#cite_note-102) Other major universities include [Queensland University of Technology](./Queensland_University_of_Technology \"Queensland University of Technology\"), [Griffith University](./Griffith_University \"Griffith University\"), the [University of Southern Queensland](./University_of_Southern_Queensland \"University of Southern Queensland\"), the [University of the Sunshine Coast](./University_of_the_Sunshine_Coast \"University of the Sunshine Coast\"), [James Cook University](./James_Cook_University \"James Cook University\") (which was the state\\'s first university outside of [South East Queensland](./South_East_Queensland \"South East Queensland\")), [Central Queensland University](./Central_Queensland_University \"Central Queensland University\") and [Bond University](./Bond_University \"Bond University\") (which was Australia\\'s first private university).\\n\\n[International education](./International_student \"International student\") is an important industry, with 134,312 [international students enrolled in the state](./International_students_in_Australia \"International students in Australia\") in 2018, largely focused on Brisbane. Most of the state\\'s international students are from Asia.[[95]](./Queensland#cite_note-IntlStudying-103)\\n\\nAt the primary and secondary levels, Queensland is home to numerous [state](./Queensland_state_schools \"Queensland state schools\") and private schools.\\n\\nQueensland has a [public library system](./List_of_libraries_in_Queensland#Public_libraries \"List of libraries in Queensland\") which is managed by the State Library of Queensland.[[96]](./Queensland#cite_note-104) Some university libraries are also open to the public.\\n\\nEconomy\\n-------\\n\\nMain article: [Economy of Queensland](./Economy_of_Queensland \"Economy of Queensland\")\\n\\nSee also: [Economy of Australia](./Economy_of_Australia \"Economy of Australia\")\\n\\n[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e0/Brisbane_City_Skyline.jpg/250px-Brisbane_City_Skyline.jpg)](./File:Brisbane_City_Skyline.jpg)\\n\\nSkyline of the [Brisbane central business district](./Brisbane_central_business_district \"Brisbane central business district\"). Since the 1980s, a sizeable influx of interstate and overseas migrants, large amounts of federal government investment, increased mining of vast mineral deposits and an expanding aerospace sector have contributed to the state\\'s economic growth.[[98]](./Queensland#cite_note-aus-106)\\n\\n[Primary industries](./Primary_sector_of_industry \"Primary sector of industry\") include bananas, [pineapples](./Pineapple \"Pineapple\"), peanuts, a wide variety of other tropical and temperate fruit and vegetables, grain crops, [wineries](./Winery \"Winery\"), cattle raising, cotton, [sugarcane](./Sugarcane \"Sugarcane\"), and [wool](./Wool \"Wool\"). The mining industry includes [bauxite](./Bauxite \"Bauxite\"), coal, silver, lead, [zinc](./Zinc \"Zinc\"), gold and copper.[[99]](./Queensland#cite_note-107)[[100]](./Queensland#cite_note-108)\\n\\n[Secondary industries](./Secondary_sector_of_the_economy \"Secondary sector of the economy\") are mostly further processing of the above-mentioned primary produce. For example, bauxite is shipped by sea from [Weipa](./Weipa,_Queensland \"Weipa, Queensland\") and converted to alumina at [Gladstone](./Gladstone,_Queensland \"Gladstone, Queensland\").[[101]](./Queensland#cite_note-rta-109) There is also copper refining and the refining of sugar cane to sugar at a number of mills along the eastern coastline.\\n\\nMajor [tertiary industries](./Tertiary_sector_of_the_economy \"Tertiary sector of the economy\") are retail, tourism, and [international education](./International_student \"International student\").
