[D\\'Aguilar Range](./D\\'Aguilar_Range \"D\\'Aguilar Range\") and [National Park](./D\\'Aguilar_National_Park \"D\\'Aguilar National Park\"), as well as [Moreton Bay](./Moreton_Bay \"Moreton Bay\") (including [Moreton](./Moreton_Island \"Moreton Island\"), [North Stradbroke](./North_Stradbroke_Island \"North Stradbroke Island\") and [Bribie](./Bribie_Island \"Bribie Island\") islands, and coastal suburbs such as [Shorncliffe](./Shorncliffe,_Queensland \"Shorncliffe, Queensland\"), [Wynnum](./Wynnum,_Queensland \"Wynnum, Queensland\") and those on the [Redcliffe Peninsula](./Redcliffe_Peninsula \"Redcliffe Peninsula\")).[[110]](./Queensland#cite_note-118)[[111]](./Queensland#cite_note-119)[[112]](./Queensland#cite_note-120)\\n\\nThe [Gold Coast](./Gold_Coast,_Queensland \"Gold Coast, Queensland\") is home to numerous popular surf beaches such as those at [Surfers Paradise](./Surfers_Paradise,_Queensland \"Surfers Paradise, Queensland\") and [Burleigh Heads](./Burleigh_Heads,_Queensland \"Burleigh Heads, Queensland\"). It also includes the largest concentration of [amusement parks](./Amusement_park \"Amusement park\") in Australia, including [Dreamworld](./Dreamworld_(Australian_theme_park) \"Dreamworld (Australian theme park)\"), [Movie World](./Warner_Bros._Movie_World \"Warner Bros. Movie World\"), [Sea World](./Sea_World_(Australia) \"Sea World (Australia)\"), [Wet \\'n\\' Wild](./Wet\\'n\\'Wild_Water_World \"Wet\\'n\\'Wild Water World\") and [WhiteWater World](./WhiteWater_World \"WhiteWater World\"), as well as the [Currumbin Wildlife Sanctuary](./Currumbin_Wildlife_Sanctuary \"Currumbin Wildlife Sanctuary\"). The Gold Coast\\'s hinterland includes [Lamington National Park](./Lamington_National_Park \"Lamington National Park\") in the [McPherson Range](./McPherson_Range \"McPherson Range\").[*[citation needed](./Wikipedia:Citation_needed \"Wikipedia:Citation needed\")*]\\n\\nThe [Sunshine Coast](./Sunshine_Coast,_Queensland \"Sunshine Coast, Queensland\") includes popular surfing and beach destinations including [Noosa Heads](./Noosa_Heads,_Queensland \"Noosa Heads, Queensland\") and [Mooloolaba](./Mooloolaba \"Mooloolaba\"). It is also home to [UnderWater World](./UnderWater_World,_Queensland \"UnderWater World, Queensland\") and [Steve Irwin](./Steve_Irwin \"Steve Irwin\")\\'s [Australia Zoo](./Australia_Zoo \"Australia Zoo\"). Its hinterland includes the [Glass House Mountains National Park](./Glass_House_Mountains_National_Park \"Glass House Mountains National Park\").[[113]](./Queensland#cite_note-121)\\n\\n[Cairns](./Cairns \"Cairns\") is renowned as the gateway to the [Great Barrier Reef](./Great_Barrier_Reef \"Great Barrier Reef\"), [Far North Queensland](./Far_North_Queensland \"Far North Queensland\") (including [Port Douglas](./Port_Douglas,_Queensland \"Port Douglas, Queensland\")) and the [Daintree Rainforest](./Daintree_Rainforest \"Daintree Rainforest\"). The [Whitsunday Islands](./Whitsunday_Islands \"Whitsunday Islands\") off the coast of [North Queensland](./North_Queensland \"North Queensland\") are a popular tourist destinations for their [resort](./Resort \"Resort\") facilities and access to the Great Barrier Reef.[[114]](./Queensland#cite_note-122)\\n\\nPolitics and government\\n-----------------------\\n\\nMain article: [Politics of Queensland](./Politics_of_Queensland \"Politics of Queensland\")\\n\\nOne of the six founding [states of Australia](./States_and_territories_of_Australia \"States and territories of Australia\"), Queensland has been a [federated state](./Federated_state \"Federated state\") subject to the [Australian Constitution](./Constitution_of_Australia \"Constitution of Australia\") since 1 January 1901. It may legislate on all matters not [ceded in the Australian Constitution to the federal government](./Section_51_of_the_Constitution_of_Australia \"Section 51 of the Constitution of Australia\"). It is a [parliamentary](./Parliamentary_system \"Parliamentary system\") [constitutional monarchy](./Constitutional_monarchy \"Constitutional monarchy\"). The [Constitution of Queensland](./Constitution_of_Queensland \"Constitution of Queensland\") sets out the operation of the state\\'s government. The state\\'s constitution contains several [entrenched provisions](./Entrenched_clause \"Entrenched clause\") which cannot be changed in the absence of a [referendum](./Referendum \"Referendum\"). There is also a [statutory](./Statutory_law \"Statutory law\") [charter of rights](./Charter_of_rights \"Charter of rights\"), the *Queensland Human Rights Act 2019*. Queensland\\'s system of government is influenced by the [Westminster system](./Westminster_system \"Westminster system\") and [Australia\\'s federal system of government](./Politics_of_Australia \"Politics of Australia\").\\n\\nThe government power [can be divided](./Separation_of_powers_in_Australia \"Separation of powers in Australia\") into three groups:\\n\\n* Legislature: the [unicameral](./Unicameralism \"Unicameralism\") [Parliament of Queensland](./Parliament_of_Queensland \"Parliament of Queensland\"), comprising the [Legislative Assembly](./Legislative_Assembly_of_Queensland \"Legislative Assembly of Queensland\") and the [Monarch](./Monarchy_of_Australia \"Monarchy of Australia\") (represented by the [Governor](./Governor_of_Queensland \"Governor of Queensland\"));\\n* Executive: the [Queensland Government](./Queensland_Government \"Queensland Government\"), which consists of the [Executive Council of Queensland](./Executive_Council_of_Queensland \"Executive Council of Queensland\"), which formalises decisions of the [Cabinet of Queensland](./Cabinet_of_Queensland \"Cabinet of Queensland\"), which is composed of the [Premier](./Premier_of_Queensland \"Premier of Queensland\") and other ministers of state appointed by the Governor on the advice of the premier;\\n* Judiciary: the [Supreme Court](./Supreme_Court_of_Queensland \"Supreme Court of Queensland\") and other state courts, whose judges are appointed by the Governor on the advice of Parliament.\\n\\n[Executive authority](./Executive_(government) \"Executive (government)\") is nominally vested in the [Governor of Queensland](./Governor_of_Queensland \"Governor of Queensland\") (currently [Jeannette Young](./Jeannette_Young \"Jeannette Young\")) who represents and is appointed by the [Monarch](./Monarchy_of_Australia \"Monarchy of Australia\") (currently [Charles III](./Charles_III \"Charles III\")) on the advice of the [Premier of Queensland](./Premier_of_Queensland \"Premier of Queensland\"). The Premier, who is the state\\'s [Head of government](./Head_of_government \"Head of government\"), along with the [Cabinet of Queensland](./Cabinet_of_Queensland \"Cabinet of Queensland\") (whose decisions are formalised by the [Executive Council](./Executive_Council_of_Queensland \"Executive Council of Queensland\")), exercise executive authority in practice. The Premier is appointed by the Governor and [must have support](./Responsible_government \"Responsible government\") of the [Legislative Assembly of Queensland](./Legislative_Assembly_of_Queensland \"Legislative Assembly of Queensland\"). The Premier is in practice a leading member of the Legislative Assembly and parliamentary leader of his or her political party, or coalition of parties, and members of the Cabinet will be drawn from the same party or coalition. The current Premier and [Deputy Premier](./Deputy_Premier_of_Queensland \"Deputy Premier of Queensland\") are [David Crisafulli](./David_Crisafulli \"David Crisafulli\") and [Jarrod Bleijie](./Jarrod_Bleijie \"Jarrod Bleijie\") of the [Liberal National Party](./Liberal_National_Party_of_Queensland \"Liberal National Party of Queensland\") respectively. [Government House](./Government_House,_Brisbane \"Government House, Brisbane\") at [Paddington](./Paddington,_Queensland \"Paddington, Queensland\") in Brisbane is the seat of the Governor, having replaced [Old Government House](./Old_Government_House,_Queensland \"Old Government House, Queensland\") at [Gardens Point](./Gardens_Point,_Brisbane \"Gardens Point, Brisbane\") in Brisbane\\'s [CBD](./Brisbane_central_business_district \"Brisbane central business district\") in the early 20th century. The executive branch is simply referred to as the [Queensland Government](./Queensland_Government \"Queensland Government\").\\n\\n[Legislative authority](./Legislature \"Legislature\") is exercised by the [Queensland Parliament](./Parliament_of_Queensland \"Parliament of Queensland\") which uniquely for Australian states is [unicameral](./Unicameralism \"Unicameralism\"), containing only one house, the Legislative Assembly. The Parliament was [bicameral](./Bicameral_legislature \"Bicameral legislature\") until 1922 when the [Legislative Council](./Queensland_Legislative_Council \"Queensland Legislative Council\") was abolished by the Labor \"suicide squad\", so called because they were appointed for the purpose of voting to abolish their own offices.[[115]](./Queensland#cite_note-apg-123) [Bills](./Bill_(law) \"Bill (law)\") receive [royal assent](./Royal_assent \"Royal assent\") from the [Governor](./Governor_of_Queensland \"Governor of Queensland\") before being passed into law. The Parliament\\'s seat is at [Parliament House](./Parliament_House,_Brisbane \"Parliament House, Brisbane\") at [Gardens Point](./Gardens_Point,_Brisbane \"Gardens Point, Brisbane\") in Brisbane\\'s CBD. Members of the Legislative Assembly represent [93 electoral districts](./Electoral_districts_of_Queensland \"Electoral districts of Queensland\"). Elections in Queensland are held at the end of each fixed four-year parliamentary term and are determined by full [preferential voting](./Instant-runoff_voting \"Instant-runoff voting\").\\n\\nThe state\\'s [judiciary](./Judiciary \"Judiciary\") consists of the [Supreme Court of Queensland](./Supreme_Court_of_Queensland \"Supreme Court of Queensland\") and the [District Court of Queensland](./District_Court_of_Queensland \"District Court of Queensland\"), established by the Queensland Constitution, as well as the [Magistrates Court of Queensland](./Magistrates_Court_of_Queensland \"Magistrates Court of Queensland\") and other courts and tribunals established by legislation. Cases may be appealed to the [High Court of Australia](./High_Court_of_Australia \"High Court of Australia\"). As with all Australian states and territories, Queensland has a [common law](./Common_law \"Common law\") legal system. The Supreme and District courts are headquartered at the [Queen Elizabeth II Courts of Law](./Queen_Elizabeth_II_Courts_of_Law,_Brisbane \"Queen Elizabeth II Courts of Law, Brisbane\") in Brisbane\\'s CBD.\\n\\nThe state\\'s politics are traditionally regarded as being [conservative](./Conservatism_in_Australia \"Conservatism in Australia\") relative to other states.[[116]](./Queensland#cite_note-Daly,_Leffman,_Dehne_2003_p397-124)[[117]](./Queensland#cite_note-Penrith,_Seal_2008_p478-125)[[118]](./Queensland#cite_note-126)[[119]](./Queensland#cite_note-127)[[120]](./Queensland#cite_note-128) Historically, the lack of an [upper house](./Upper_house \"Upper house\"), the \"[Bjelkemander](./Bjelkemander \"Bjelkemander\")\" (a [malapportion](./Malapportionment \"Malapportionment\") favouring rural electoral districts) has meant that Queensland had a long tradition of domination by strong-willed, [populist](./Populism \"Populism\") premiers, often accused of authoritarian tendencies, holding office for long periods. This tendency was exemplified by the government of the state\\'s longest-serving Premier [Joh Bjelke-Petersen](./Joh_Bjelke-Petersen \"Joh Bjelke-Petersen\").\\n\\n* [![Parliament House, seat of the Queensland](./Local_government_in_Queensland \"Local government in Queensland\")\\n\\nLocal government is the mechanism by which [local government areas](./Local_government_areas_of_Queensland \"Local government areas of Queensland\") can manage their own affairs to the extent permitted by the Local Government Act 2009. Queensland is divided into 77 local government areas, which are created by the state government under the legislation.[[121]](./Queensland#cite_note-129) Each local government area has a council responsible for providing a range of local services and utilities. \"Ekka\")) is held each August at the Brisbane Showgrounds.\\n\\nQueensland is home to major art galleries including the [Queensland Art Gallery](./Queensland_Art_Gallery \"Queensland Art Gallery\") and the [Queensland Gallery of Modern Art](./Queensland_Gallery_of_Modern_Art \"Queensland Gallery of Modern Art\") as well as cultural institutions such as the [Queensland Ballet](./Queensland_Ballet \"Queensland Ballet\"), [Opera Queensland](./Opera_Queensland \"Opera Queensland\"), [Queensland Theatre Company](./Queensland_Theatre_Company \"Queensland Theatre Company\"), and [Queensland Symphony Orchestra](./Queensland_Symphony_Orchestra \"Queensland Symphony Orchestra\"), all based at the [Queensland Cultural Centre](./Queensland_Cultural_Centre \"Queensland Cultural Centre\") in Brisbane. The state is the origin of musicians such as the [Bee Gees](./Bee_Gees \"Bee Gees\"), [the Go-Betweens](./The_Go-Betweens \"The Go-Betweens\"), [the Veronicas](./The_Veronicas \"The Veronicas\"), [the Saints](./The_Saints_(Australian_band) \"The Saints (Australian band)\"), [Savage Garden](./Savage_Garden \"Savage Garden\"), and [Sheppard](./Sheppard_(band) \"Sheppard (band)\") as well as writers such as [David Malouf](./David_Malouf \"David Malouf\"), [Nick Earls](./Nick_Earls \"Nick Earls\") and [Li Cunxin](./Li_Cunxin \"Li Cunxin\").\\n\\nMajor annual cultural events include the [Royal Queensland Exhibition](./Ekka \"Ekka\") (known locally as the Ekka), an agricultural exhibition held each August at the [Brisbane Showgrounds](./Brisbane_Showgrounds \"Brisbane Showgrounds\") as well as the [Brisbane Festival](./Brisbane_Festival \"Brisbane Festival\"), which includes one of the nation\\'s largest annual fireworks displays called \\'Riverfire\\', and which is held each September.\\n\\n### Sport\\n\\nMain article: [Sport in Queensland](./Sport_in_Queensland \"Sport in Queensland\")\\n\\n[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/98/The_Gabba_Panorama.jpg/250px-The_Gabba_Panorama.jpg)](./File:The_Gabba_Panorama.jpg)\\n\\n[Cricket](./Cricket \"Cricket\") game at [The Gabba](./The_Gabba \"The Gabba\"), a 42,000-seat round stadium in [Brisbane](./Brisbane \"Brisbane\")\\n\\nThe state of Queensland is represented in all of Australia\\'s national sporting competitions and it is also host to a number of domestic and international sporting events. The most popular winter and summer team sports are [rugby league](./Rugby_league \"Rugby league\") and [cricket](./Cricket \"Cricket\"), respectively.\\n\\nIn the [National Rugby League](./National_Rugby_League \"National Rugby League\"), the [Brisbane Broncos](./Brisbane_Broncos \"Brisbane Broncos\"), [North Queensland Cowboys](./North_Queensland_Cowboys \"North Queensland Cowboys\"), [The Dolphins](./Dolphins_(NRL) \"Dolphins (NRL)\") and [Gold Coast Titans](./Gold_Coast_Titans \"Gold Coast Titans\") are based in the state. Rugby league\\'s annual [State of Origin series](./State_of_Origin_series \"State of Origin series\") is a major event in the Queensland sporting calendar, with the [Queensland Maroons](./Queensland_rugby_league_team \"Queensland rugby league team\") representing the state.\\n\\nIn cricket, the [Queensland Bulls](./Queensland_Bulls \"Queensland Bulls\") represent the state in the [Sheffield Shield](./Sheffield_Shield \"Sheffield Shield\") and the [Ryobi One Day Cup](./Ryobi_One_Day_Cup \"Ryobi One Day Cup\"), while the [Brisbane Heat](./Brisbane_Heat \"Brisbane Heat\") compete in the [Big Bash League](./Big_Bash_League \"Big Bash League\").\\n\\nQueensland is also home to the [Brisbane Lions](./Brisbane_Lions \"Brisbane Lions\") and the [Gold Coast Suns](./Gold_Coast_Suns \"Gold Coast Suns\") in the [Australian Football League](./Australian_Football_League \"Australian Football League\") ([Australian rules football](./Australian_rules_football \"Australian rules football\")), and the [Brisbane Roar FC](./Brisbane_Roar_FC \"Brisbane Roar FC\") in the [A-League](./A-League \"A-League\") (soccer). In netball, the [Queensland Firebirds](./Queensland_Firebirds \"Queensland Firebirds\") went undefeated in the 2011 season as they went on to win the Grand Final. Other sports teams are the [Brisbane Bullets](./Brisbane_Bullets \"Brisbane Bullets\") and the [Cairns Taipans](./Cairns_Taipans \"Cairns Taipans\"), who compete in the [National Basketball League](./National_Basketball_League_(Australia) \"National Basketball League (Australia)\").\\n\\nThe state is represented by the [Queensland Reds](./Queensland_Reds \"Queensland Reds\") in the [Super Rugby](./Super_Rugby \"Super Rugby\") (rugby union).\\n\\nSwimming is also a popular sport in Queensland, with many Australian team members and international medalists hailing from the state.\\n\\nBrisbane will host the [2032 Summer Olympics](./2032_Summer_Olympics \"2032 Summer Olympics\"), marking the third time Australia hosted the Olympic Games following [Melbourne 1956](./1956_Summer_Olympics \"1956 Summer Olympics\") and [Sydney 2000](./2000_Summer_Olympics \"2000 Summer Olympics\").[[124]](./Queensland#cite_note-134) Major recurring sporting events hosted in Queensland include: the [Gold Coast 600](./Gold_Coast_600 \"Gold Coast 600\") (motorsport; since 1994), the [Gold Coast Marathon](./Gold_Coast_Marathon \"Gold Coast Marathon\") (athletics; since 1979), the [NRL All Stars Game](./NRL_All_Stars_Game \"NRL All Stars Game\") (rugby league; since 2010), the [Townsville 400](./Townsville_400 \"Townsville 400\") (motorsport; since 2009), the [Quicksilver Pro and Roxy Pro](./World_championship_tour_(WCT)_surfing \"World championship tour (WCT) surfing\") (surfing) and [Australian PGA Championship](./Australian_PGA_Championship \"Australian PGA Championship\") (golf; since 2000).\\n\\n### Symbols and emblems\\n\\nMain article: [Symbols of Queensland](./Symbols_of_Queensland \"Symbols of Queensland\")\\n\\nThe official state emblems of Queensland are prescribed in the Emblems of Queensland Act 2005.\\n\\n[Queen Victoria](./Queen_Victoria \"Queen Victoria\") granted the Queensland Coat of Arms to the Colony of Queensland in 1893, making it the oldest State Arms in Australia.[[125]](./Queensland#cite_note-:0-135) It depicts Queensland\\'s primary industries in the 19th century with a sheaf of wheat, the heads of a bull and a ram, and a column of gold rising from a heap of quartz. Two stalks of sugar cane which surround the state badge at the top, and below is Queensland\\'s state motto, *Audax at Fidelis*, which means \"Bold but Faithful\". In 1977, [Queen Elizabeth II](./Elizabeth_II \"Elizabeth II\") granted the supporting animals, the [brolga](./Brolga \"Brolga\") and the [red deer](./Red_deer \"Red deer\").[[125]](./Queensland#cite_note-:0-135)[[126]](./Queensland#cite_note-:1-136)\\n\\nIn November 2003 [maroon](./Maroon \"Maroon\") was officially named Queensland\\'s state colour, after many years of association with Queensland sporting teams. In 2025, Queensland Government branding changed to blue, with not yet an impact on the official state colour.[[127]](./Queensland#cite_note-137)\\n\\nThe [koala](./Koala \"Koala\") was officially named the animal or faunal, emblem of Queensland in 1971 after a newspaper poll showed strong public support. The Queensland Government introduced the poll due to a proposal by state tourism ministers for all states to adopt a faunal emblem.[[125]](./Queensland#cite_note-:0-135) In January 1986, the brolga was announced as the official bird emblem of Queensland, after many years on the Coat of Arms.[[126]](./Queensland#cite_note-:1-136)\\n\\nThe [Cooktown orchid](./Dendrobium_bigibbum \"Dendrobium bigibbum\") became known as Queensland\\'s floral emblem in 1959, during celebrations to mark the state\\'s centenary,[[128]](./Queensland#cite_note-138)[[129]](./Queensland#cite_note-139) and the [Barrier Reef Anemone Fish](./Amphiprion_akindynos \"Amphiprion akindynos\") was officially named as Queensland\\'s aquatic emblem in March 2005.[[130]](./Queensland#cite_note-140)\\n\\nThe [sapphire](./Sapphire \"Sapphire\") was named the official state gem for Queensland in August 1985.[[131]](./Queensland#cite_note-141)[[132]](./Queensland#cite_note-142)\\n\\nInfrastructure\\n--------------\\n\\nSee also: [Transportation in Australia](./Transportation_in_Australia \"Transportation in Australia\"), [Transport in Brisbane](./Transport_in_Brisbane \"Transport in Brisbane\"), [TransLink (South East Queensland)](./TransLink_(South_East_Queensland) \"TransLink (South East Queensland)\"), and [Queensland Rail City network](./Queensland_Rail_City_network \"Queensland Rail City network\")\\n\\n|  |  |\\n| --- | --- |\\n| [icon](./File:Question_book-new.svg) | This section **needs additional citations for [verification](./Wikipedia:Verifiability \"Wikipedia:Verifiability\")**. Unsourced material may be challenged and removed. *(June 2019)* *([Learn how and when to remove this message](./Help:Maintenance_template_removal \"Help:Maintenance template removal\"))* |\\n\\n### Transport\\n\\nQueensland is served by several [National Highways](./National_Highway_(Australia) \"National Highway (Australia)\") and, particularly in South East Queensland, a network of freeways such as the [M1](./M1_(Queensland) \"M1 (Queensland)\"). The [Department of Transport & Main Roads](./Department_of_Transport_and_Main_Roads \"Department of Transport and Main Roads\") oversees the development and operation of main roads and public transport, including taxis and local aviation.\\n\\n[Principal rail services](./Rail_transport_in_Queensland \"Rail transport in Queensland\") are provided by [Queensland Rail](./Queensland_Rail \"Queensland Rail\"), predominantly between the major centres east of the Great Dividing Range. Freight rail services in Queensland have been provided mostly by [Aurizon](./Aurizon \"Aurizon\") and [Pacific National](./Pacific_National \"Pacific National\"), with interstate intermodal services provided by Pacific National and [SCT Logistics](./SCT_Logistics \"SCT Logistics\"). Major seaports include the [Port of Brisbane](./Port_of_Brisbane \"Port of Brisbane\"), Australia\\'s third busiest by value of goods, as well as those at [Gladstone](./Gladstone,_Queensland \"Gladstone, Queensland\"), [Townsville](./Townsville \"Townsville\"), and [Bundaberg](./Bundaberg \"Bundaberg\"). There are large coal export facilities at [Hay Point](./Hay_Point,_Queensland \"Hay Point, Queensland\"), Gladstone, and [Abbot Point](./Abbot_Point \"Abbot Point\"). Major sugar export facilities are located at [Lucinda](./Lucinda,_Queensland \"Lucinda, Queensland\") and [Mackay](./Mackay,_Queensland \"Mackay, Queensland\").\\n\\n[Brisbane Airport](./Brisbane_Airport \"Brisbane Airport\") is the main international and domestic gateway serving the state, and is the [third busiest in Australia](./List_of_the_busiest_airports_in_Australia \"List of the busiest airports in Australia\"). Other international airports include the [Gold Coast Airport](./Gold_Coast_Airport \"Gold Coast Airport\"), [Cairns International Airport](./Cairns_International_Airport \"Cairns International Airport\"), and [Townsville Airport](./Townsville_Airport \"Townsville Airport\"). Regional airports with scheduled domestic flights include [Toowoomba Wellcamp Airport](./Toowoomba_Wellcamp_Airport \"Toowoomba Wellcamp Airport\"), [Great Barrier Reef Airport](./Great_Barrier_Reef_Airport \"Great Barrier Reef Airport\"), [Hervey Bay Airport](./Hervey_Bay_Airport \"Hervey Bay Airport\"), [Bundaberg Airport](./Bundaberg_Airport \"Bundaberg Airport\"), [Mackay Airport](./Mackay_Airport \"Mackay Airport\"), [Mount Isa Airport](./Mount_Isa_Airport \"Mount Isa Airport\"), [Proserpine / Whitsunday Coast Airport](./Whitsunday_Coast_Airport \"Whitsunday Coast Airport\"), [Rockhampton Airport](./Rockhampton_Airport \"Rockhampton Airport\"), and [Sunshine Coast Airport](./Sunshine_Coast_Airport \"Sunshine Coast Airport\").\\n\\n[South East Queensland](./South_East_Queensland \"South East Queensland\") has an integrated public transport system operated by [Translink](./TransLink_(South_East_Queensland) \"TransLink (South East Queensland)\"), which provides services [bus](./Bus_transport_in_Queensland \"Bus transport in Queensland\"), [rail](./Queensland_Rail_City_network \"Queensland Rail City network\"), [light rail](./G:link \"G:link\") and [Brisbane\\'s ferry services](./RiverCity_Ferries \"RiverCity Ferries\") through Queensland Rail and contracted operators. The region is divided into seven [Fare](./Fare \"Fare\") zones radiating outwards from the [Brisbane central business district](./Brisbane_central_business_district \"Brisbane central business district\"), which is the central hub for the system. The [Queensland Rail City network](./Queensland_Rail_City_network \"Queensland Rail City network\") consists of 152 train stations along 13 suburban rail lines and across the region, and predominantly within Brisbane\\'s metropolitan area. There is also a large bus network including Brisbane\\'s large dedicated [bus rapid transit](./Bus_rapid_transit \"Bus rapid transit\") network, the [Brisbane busway network](./Busways_in_Brisbane \"Busways in Brisbane\"). Brisbane\\'s popular [ferry services](./RiverCity_Ferries \"RiverCity Ferries\") include the CityCat, Cross River, and CityHopper services which have dedicated wharves along the [Brisbane River](./Brisbane_River \"Brisbane River\"). The [G:link](./G:link \"G:link\"), Queensland\\'s only [light rail](./Light_rail \"Light rail\") network, operates on the Gold Coast.[[133]](./Queensland#cite_note-143)\\n\\nThe new Queensland [Cross River Rail](./Cross_River_Rail \"Cross River Rail\") is a metro network that is currently under development within [Brisbane](./Brisbane \"Brisbane\") and is part of infrastructure to prepare the city for the [2032 Olympic games](./2032_Olympic_Games \"2032 Olympic Games\").[[134]](./Queensland#cite_note-144)\\n\\n* [![Passenger train at Oxley railway station on the Ipswich/Rosewood line within the Queensland Rail City network](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3a/NGR722_approaching_Oxley_railway_station%2C_Brisbane.jpg/250px-NGR722_approaching_Oxley_railway_station%2C_Brisbane.jpg)](./File:NGR722_approaching_Oxley_railway_station,_Brisbane.jpg \"Passenger train at Oxley railway station on the Ipswich/Rosewood line within the Queensland Rail City network\")\\n\\n  Passenger train at [Oxley railway station](./Oxley_railway_station \"Oxley railway station\") on the [Ipswich/Rosewood line](./Ipswich_and_Rosewood_railway_line \"Ipswich and Rosewood railway line\") within the [Queensland Rail City network](./Queensland_Rail_City_network \"Queensland Rail City network\")\\n* [![Cargo ships at the Port of Gladstone, Queensland\\'s largest commodity seaport](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/bb/Port_of_Gladstone_1.jpg/250px-Port_of_Gladstone_1.jpg)](./File:Port_of_Gladstone_1.jpg \"Cargo ships at the Port of Gladstone, Queensland\\'s largest commodity seaport\")\\n\\n  Cargo ships at the [Port of Gladstone](./Port_of_Gladstone \"Port of Gladstone\"), Queensland\\'s largest [commodity](./Commodity \"Commodity\") [seaport](./Seaport \"Seaport\")\\n\\n### Other utilities\\n\\n[Queensland Health](./Queensland_Health \"Queensland Health\") operates and administers the state\\'s [public health](./Public_health \"Public health\") system. There are sixteen regional Health and Hospital Services corresponding to geographical regions which are responsible for delivering public health services within their regions. Major public hospitals include the [Royal Brisbane and Women\\'s Hospital](./Royal_Brisbane_and_Women\\'s_Hospital \"Royal Brisbane and Women\\'s Hospital\"), [Princess Alexandra Hospital](./Princess_Alexandra_Hospital,_Brisbane \"Princess Alexandra Hospital, Brisbane\"), the [Mater Hospital](./Mater_Group \"Mater Group\"), the [Queen Elizabeth II Jubilee Hospital](./Queen_Elizabeth_II_Jubilee_Hospital \"Queen Elizabeth II Jubilee Hospital\"), and the [Queensland Children\\'s Hospital](./Queensland_Children\\'s_Hospital \"Queensland Children\\'s Hospital\") in Brisbane, as well as the [Townsville University Hospital](./Townsville_University_Hospital \"Townsville University Hospital\"), [Cairns Hospital](./Cairns_Hospital \"Cairns Hospital\"), [Gold Coast Hospital](./Gold_Coast_Hospital \"Gold Coast Hospital\") and [Gold Coast University Hospital](./Gold_Coast_University_Hospital \"Gold Coast University Hospital\") in the regional cities. There are smaller public hospitals, as well as private hospitals, around the state.\\n\\nSee also\\n--------\\n\\n* ![flag](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/04/Flag_of_Queensland.svg/40px-Flag_of_Queensland.svg.png)[Queensland portal](./Portal:Queensland \"Portal:Queensland\")\\n* ![flag](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/b/b9/Flag_of_Australia.svg/40px-Flag_of_Australia.svg.png)[Australia portal](./Portal:Australia \"Portal:Australia\")\\n* [![icon](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7b/%E5%A4%A7%E6%B4%8B.png/40px-%E5%A4%A7%E6%B4%8B.png)](./File:大洋.png)[Oceania portal](./Portal:Oceania \"Portal:Oceania\")\\n* ![icon](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f5/Terra.png/40px-Terra.png)[Geography portal](./Portal:Geography \"Portal:Geography\")\\n\\n* [Outline of Australia](./Outline_of_Australia \"Outline of Australia\")\\n* [State of North Queensland](./State_of_North_Queensland \"State of North Queensland\") (Proposed state)\\n\\nNotes\\n-----\\n\\n1. (39.8\\xa0in) |\\n\\n**Brisbane** ([/ˈbrɪzbən/](./Help:IPA/English \"Help:IPA/English\") [ⓘ](/wiki/File:En-au-Brisbane.oga \"File:En-au-Brisbane.oga\") [*BRIZ-bən*](./Help:Pronunciation_respelling_key \"Help:Pronunciation respelling key\");[[10]](./Brisbane#cite_note-10) [Turrbal/Yagara](./Turrbal_language \"Turrbal language\"): *Meanjin, Meaanjin, Maganjin or Magandjin*[[N 1]](./Brisbane#cite_note-IndigenousSpelling-11)) is the [capital](./List_of_Australian_capital_cities \"List of Australian capital cities\") and largest city of the [state](./States_and_territories_of_Australia \"States and territories of Australia\") of [Queensland](./Queensland \"Queensland\")[[11]](./Brisbane#cite_note-qpn-12) and the [third-most populous city](./List_of_cities_in_Australia_by_population \"List of cities in Australia by population\") in [Australia](./Australia \"Australia\"), with a population of approximately 2.8\\xa0million.[[9]](./Brisbane#cite_note-abs.gov.au-9) Brisbane lies at the centre of [South East Queensland](./South_East_Queensland \"South East Queensland\") urban region with an estimated population of 4.1 million in 2024.[[12]](./Brisbane#cite_note-ABS-SEQ-2024-13) The [central business district](./Brisbane_central_business_district \"Brisbane central business district\") is situated within a peninsula of the [Brisbane River](./Brisbane_River \"Brisbane River\") about 15\\xa0km (9\\xa0mi) from its mouth at [Moreton Bay](./Moreton_Bay \"Moreton Bay\").[[13]](./Brisbane#cite_note-14) Greater Brisbane sprawls over the hilly [floodplain](./Floodplain \"Floodplain\") of the Brisbane River Valley between [Pacific Ocean](./Pacific_Ocean \"Pacific Ocean\") and the [Taylor](./Taylor_Range \"Taylor Range\") and [D\\'Aguilar](./D\\'Aguilar_Range \"D\\'Aguilar Range\") [mountain ranges](./Mountain_range \"Mountain range\"),[[14]](./Brisbane#cite_note-15)[[15]](./Brisbane#cite_note-16) encompassing several [local government areas](./Local_government_in_Australia \"Local government in Australia\"), most centrally the [City of Brisbane](./City_of_Brisbane \"City of Brisbane\"), the most populous local government area in Australia. The [demonym](./Demonym \"Demonym\") of Brisbane is *Brisbanite*.[[16]](./Brisbane#cite_note-17)[[17]](./Brisbane#cite_note-18)\\n\\nThe [Moreton Bay penal settlement](./Moreton_Bay_penal_settlement \"Moreton Bay penal settlement\") was founded in 1824 at [Redcliffe](./Redcliffe,_Queensland \"Redcliffe, Queensland\") as a place for secondary offenders from the [Sydney colony](./Sydney \"Sydney\"), but in May 1825 moved to [North Quay](./North_Quay,_Brisbane \"North Quay, Brisbane\") on the banks of the Brisbane River, so named for the [Governor of New South Wales](./Governor_of_New_South_Wales \"Governor of New South Wales\") Sir [Thomas Brisbane](./Thomas_Brisbane \"Thomas Brisbane\"). [German Lutherans](./Lutheranism \"Lutheranism\") established the first free settlement of [Zion Hill](./Zion_Hill_Mission \"Zion Hill Mission\") at [Nundah](./Nundah \"Nundah\") in 1838, and in 1859 Brisbane was chosen as Queensland\\'s capital when [the state separated](./Separation_of_Queensland \"Separation of Queensland\") from [New South Wales](./New_South_Wales \"New South Wales\"). During [World War II](./World_War_II \"World War II\"), the [Allied](./Allies_of_World_War_II \"Allies of World War II\") command in the [South West Pacific](./South_West_Pacific_Area_(command) \"South West Pacific Area (command)\") was based in the city, along with the [headquarters](./MacArthur_Chambers \"MacArthur Chambers\") for General [Douglas MacArthur](./Douglas_MacArthur \"Douglas MacArthur\") of the United States Army.[[18]](./Brisbane#cite_note-19)\\n\\nBrisbane is a global centre for research and innovation[[19]](./Brisbane#cite_note-20)[[20]](./Brisbane#cite_note-21) and is a transportation hub, being served by large [rail](./Queensland_Rail_City_network \"Queensland Rail City network\"), [bus](./Busways_in_Brisbane \"Busways in Brisbane\") and [ferry](./RiverCity_Ferries \"RiverCity Ferries\") networks, as well as [Brisbane Airport](./Brisbane_Airport \"Brisbane Airport\") and the [Port of Brisbane](./Port_of_Brisbane \"Port of Brisbane\"), Australia\\'s third-busiest airport and seaport. A diverse city with over 36% of its metropolitan population being foreign-born, Brisbane is frequently ranked highly in lists of the [most liveable cities](./Most_liveable_cities \"Most liveable cities\").[[21]](./Brisbane#cite_note-22)[[22]](./Brisbane#cite_note-23) Brisbane has hosted major events including the [1982 Commonwealth Games](./1982_Commonwealth_Games \"1982 Commonwealth Games\"), [World Expo 88](./World_Expo_88 \"World Expo 88\") and the [2014 G20 summit](./2014_G20_summit \"2014 G20 summit\"), and will host the [2032 Summer Olympics](./2032_Summer_Olympics \"2032 Summer Olympics\").[[23]](./Brisbane#cite_note-24)\\n\\nBrisbane is one of Australia\\'s most [popular tourist destinations](./Tourism_in_Brisbane \"Tourism in Brisbane\") and is Australia\\'s most [biodiverse](./Biodiverse \"Biodiverse\") and [greenest city](./Sustainable_city \"Sustainable city\").[[24]](./Brisbane#cite_note-25) The city is known for its [cultural heritage](./Culture_of_Brisbane \"Culture of Brisbane\"), [architecture](./Queenslander_(architecture) \"Queenslander (architecture)\"), [museums and galleries](./List_of_museums_in_Brisbane \"List of museums in Brisbane\"), [festivals](./List_of_festivals_in_Brisbane \"List of festivals in Brisbane\") and [public art](./List_of_public_art_in_Brisbane \"List of public art in Brisbane\"), [food](./Cuisine_of_Brisbane \"Cuisine of Brisbane\"), [music](./Brisbane_punk_rock \"Brisbane punk rock\"), [sports and active lifestyle](./Sport_in_Brisbane \"Sport in Brisbane\"), and its numerous [parks and gardens](./Parks_and_gardens_of_Brisbane \"Parks and gardens of Brisbane\"). [South Bank](./South_Bank,_Queensland \"South Bank, Queensland\") and its [extensive parklands](./South_Bank_Parklands \"South Bank Parklands\"), is Queensland\\'s most visited place attracting over 16 million visitors annually.[[25]](./Brisbane#cite_note-26)\\n\\nThe surrounding region includes the [Gondwana Rainforests](./Gondwana_Rainforests \"Gondwana Rainforests\"); (including [Main Range](./Main_Range_National_Park \"Main Range National Park\"), [Lamington](./Lamington_National_Park \"Lamington National Park\"), and [Springbrook](./Springbrook_National_Park \"Springbrook National Park\")) as part of the [UNESCO World Heritage Site](./World_Heritage_Site \"World Heritage Site\"), the [Bunya Mountains National Park](./Bunya_Mountains_National_Park \"Bunya Mountains National Park\"), the [Glass House Mountains](./Glass_House_Mountains \"Glass House Mountains\"), and [Moreton Bay](./Moreton_Bay \"Moreton Bay\") alongside the islands of [Moreton](./Moreton_Island \"Moreton Island\"), [Bribie](./Bribie_Island \"Bribie Island\") and [North Stradbroke Island](./North_Stradbroke_Island \"North Stradbroke Island\"), and the historic islands of [Peel](./Peel_Island_(Queensland) \"Peel Island (Queensland)\") and [St Helena Island National Park](./St_Helena_Island_National_Park \"St Helena Island National Park\").\\n\\nToponymy\\n--------\\n\\nBrisbane is named after the [Brisbane River](./Brisbane_River \"Brisbane River\"), which in turn was named after [Thomas Brisbane](./Sir_Thomas_Brisbane \"Sir Thomas Brisbane\"), the British-born [governor of New South Wales](./Governor_of_New_South_Wales \"Governor of New South Wales\") from 1821 to 1825.[[26]](./Brisbane#cite_note-27)[[27]](./Brisbane#cite_note-28)[[28]](./Brisbane#cite_note-29) The surname is possibly derived from the [Scottish Gaelic](./Scottish_Gaelic \"Scottish Gaelic\") *bris*, meaning \\'to break or smash\\' and the [Old English](./Old_English \"Old English\") word *ban* meaning \\'[bone](./Bone \"Bone\")\\'*.*[[29]](./Brisbane#cite_note-30)[[30]](./Brisbane#cite_note-31) Alternatively, the surname could be derived from either \"Braesbane\" indicating white hills or \"Braesburn\" meaning a small rivulet from the hillside.[[31]](./Brisbane#cite_note-32) Popular nicknames for Brisbane include *Brissie* (pronounced \"Brizzie\"), *Brisvegas*, and *the* *River City*.[[32]](./Brisbane#cite_note-33)[[33]](./Brisbane#cite_note-trove-34)\\n\\nBrisbane is also known as *Meanjin*, *Magandjin* and other spellings,[[N 1]](./Brisbane#cite_note-IndigenousSpelling-11) the Indigenous name likely originally for [Gardens Point](./Gardens_Point,_Brisbane \"Gardens Point, Brisbane\").[[40]](./Brisbane#cite_note-:0-41) There is a difference of opinion between local traditional owners over the spelling, provenance and pronunciation of indigenous names for Brisbane.[[41]](./Brisbane#cite_note-42) The daughter of early colonist [Tom Petrie](./Tom_Petrie \"Tom Petrie\") recorded that the name \"*Mi-an-jin*\" or \"*Me-an-jin*\" referred to the area that Brisbane CBD now straddles.[[42]](./Brisbane#cite_note-43) Some sources state that the name means \\'place shaped as a spike\\' or \\'the spearhead\\' referencing the shape of the [Brisbane River](./Brisbane_River \"Brisbane River\") along the area of the Brisbane CBD.[[43]](./Brisbane#cite_note-44)[[35]](./Brisbane#cite_note-SharedVision-36) A contemporary Turrbal organisation has also suggested it means \\'the place of the blue water lilies\\'.[[38]](./Brisbane#cite_note-:5-39) Local Elder Gaja Kerry Charlton posits that *Meanjin* is based on a European understanding of \\'spike\\', and that the phonetically similar [Yagara](./Yagara_language \"Yagara language\") name *Magandjin* — after the native [tulipwood trees](./Harpullia_pendula \"Harpullia pendula\") (*magan*) at [Gardens Point](./Gardens_Point \"Gardens Point\") — is a more accurate and appropriate Aboriginal name for Brisbane.[[44]](./Brisbane#cite_note-magandjin-45)\\n\\nHistory\\n-------\\n\\nMain article: [History of Brisbane](./History_of_Brisbane \"History of Brisbane\")\\n\\nFor a chronological guide, see [Timeline of Brisbane](./Timeline_of_Brisbane \"Timeline of Brisbane\").\\n\\n[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/97/Portrait_of_Major-General_Sir_Thomas_Brisbane%2C_1842.jpg/250px-Portrait_of_Major-General_Sir_Thomas_Brisbane%2C_1842.jpg)](./File:Portrait_of_Major-General_Sir_Thomas_Brisbane,_1842.jpg)\\n\\nPortrait of [Major-General Sir Thomas Brisbane](./Thomas_Brisbane \"Thomas Brisbane\"), after whom the city and river were named.\\n\\n### Indigenous prehistory\\n\\nMain article: [Prehistory of Australia](./Prehistory_of_Australia \"Prehistory of Australia\")\\n\\nThe Brisbane region has been inhabited for more than 22,000 years by the [Yagara (Yuggera)](./Yagara_people \"Yagara people\"), [Turrbal](./Turrbal \"Turrbal\") and [Quandamooka](./Quandamooka \"Quandamooka\") peoples.[[45]](./Brisbane#cite_note-46)\\n\\nThe [Brisbane River](./Brisbane_River \"Brisbane River\") (*Maiwar*) formed the heart of cultural, economic and ceremonial life, with major camps at *Barambin* ([York\\'s Hollow](./York\\'s_Hollow \"York\\'s Hollow\")), *Woolloon-cappem* ([Kurilpa](./West_End,_Queensland \"West End, Queensland\")) and [Musgrave Park](./Musgrave_Park,_Brisbane \"Musgrave Park, Brisbane\").\\nThe central city peninsula was traditionally known as *Meeanjin*.\\n\\n### 18th and 19th centuries\\n\\nMain articles: [European maritime exploration of Australia](./European_maritime_exploration_of_Australia \"European maritime exploration of Australia\"), [Moreton Bay Penal Settlement](./Moreton_Bay_Penal_Settlement \"Moreton Bay Penal Settlement\"), and [Early Streets of Brisbane](./Early_Streets_of_Brisbane \"Early Streets of Brisbane\")\\n\\n[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/72/StateLibQld_2_148511_Early_drawing_of_a_section_of_the_town_of_Brisbane%2C_Queensland_including_the_Convict_Hospital%2C_1835.jpg/250px-StateLibQld_2_148511_Early_drawing_of_a_section_of_the_town_of_Brisbane%2C_Queensland_including_the_Convict_Hospital%2C_1835.jpg)](./File:StateLibQld_2_148511_Early_drawing_of_a_section_of_the_town_of_Brisbane,_Queensland_including_the_Convict_Hospital,_1835.jpg)\\n\\nEarly drawing of the Moreton Bay settlement, with [Old Tower Mill](./The_Old_Windmill,_Brisbane \"The Old Windmill, Brisbane\") c.1835\\n\\n[Matthew Flinders](./Matthew_Flinders \"Matthew Flinders\") charted parts of [Moreton Bay](./Moreton_Bay \"Moreton Bay\") in 1799, followed by [John Oxley](./John_Oxley \"John Oxley\") in 1823, who located the Brisbane River with the help of castaways and recommended the area for a [penal settlement](./Moreton_Bay_penal_settlement \"Moreton Bay penal settlement\").\\nThe first outpost was founded at [Redcliffe](./Redcliffe,_Queensland \"Redcliffe, Queensland\") in 1824 before relocating to [North Quay](./North_Quay,_Brisbane \"North Quay, Brisbane\") in 1825.\\nUnder [Captain Patrick Logan](./Patrick_Logan \"Patrick Logan\"), the penal station gained a reputation as one of the harshest in New South Wales. The 1820s and 1830s saw the settlement experience recurrent conflict with neighbouring Indigenous tribes, including organised [maize-field raids](./Corn_Field_Raids_of_1827–1828 \"Corn Field Raids of 1827–1828\") and the wider [Moreton Bay Islands conflict](./Moreton_Bay_conflict_(1832–1833) \"Moreton Bay conflict (1832–1833)\").\\nThe settlement closed in 1842, opening the district to free colonisation.\\n\\n[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3f/Drawing_of_Captain_Towns%27_%22Townsvale%22_Cotton_Plantation%2C_Veresdale%2C_Queensland.jpg/250px-Drawing_of_Captain_Towns%27_%22Townsvale%22_Cotton_Plantation%2C_Veresdale%2C_Queensland.jpg)](./File:Drawing_of_Captain_Towns\\'_\"Townsvale\"_Cotton_Plantation,_Veresdale,_Queensland.jpg)\\n\\nDrawing of indentured [South Sea Islanders](./South_Sea_Islanders \"South Sea Islanders\") on a [Logan River](./Logan_River \"Logan River\") plantation, c.1865\\n\\nFree settlement and pastoralists expanded along the river and surrounding valleys throughout the mid-19th century.\\n\\nThe Brisbane district became a major front of the [War of Southern Queensland](./War_of_Southern_Queensland \"War of Southern Queensland\") (1843–1855), involving coordinated resistance from [Yuggera](./Jagera_people \"Jagera people\") and [Turrbal](./Turrbal \"Turrbal\") groups, with support from neighbouring [Ningy Ningy](./Undanbi \"Undanbi\") people, under leaders such as [Dundalli](./Dundalli \"Dundalli\"), [Yilbung](./Yilbung \"Yilbung\") and the Duke of York. Raids and ambushes were carried out across the developing settlement, including at [Breakfast Creek](./Breakfast_Creek \"Breakfast Creek\"), [South Brisbane](./South_Brisbane,_Queensland \"South Brisbane, Queensland\"), the [Sandgate](./Sandgate,_Queensland \"Sandgate, Queensland\") district and the [Pine Rivers](./Pine_River_(Queensland) \"Pine River (Queensland)\").[[46]](./Brisbane#cite_note-47) In response, British forces, including detachments of the [99th](./99th_(Lanarkshire)_Regiment_of_Foot \"99th (Lanarkshire) Regiment of Foot\") and later [11th regiment](./Devonshire_Regiment \"Devonshire Regiment\") launched several armed operations through [York\\'s Hollow](./Victoria_Park,_Brisbane \"Victoria Park, Brisbane\") between 1846 and 1848.[[47]](./Brisbane#cite_note-48)\\n\\nBrisbane grew as a river port serving pastoral districts and the [Moreton Bay](./Moreton_Bay \"Moreton Bay\") islands, while German and Scottish migrants established early agricultural settlements, notably the [Zion Hill Mission](./Zion_Hill_Mission \"Zion Hill Mission\") at [Nundah](./Nundah,_Queensland \"Nundah, Queensland\") in 1838 and [Fortitude Valley](./Fortitude_Valley,_Queensland \"Fortitude Valley, Queensland\") named after the [Fortitude](./Fortitude_(1842_ship) \"Fortitude (1842 ship)\").\\nBrisbane became the capital of the newly separated [Colony of Queensland](./Colony_of_Queensland \"Colony of Queensland\") in 1859. Civic development followed, including the construction of [Parliament House](./Parliament_House,_Brisbane \"Parliament House, Brisbane\") and the [Treasury Building](./Treasury_Building,_Brisbane \"Treasury Building, Brisbane\"), expanding wharves and new rail connections linking the town to surrounding pastoral districts.\\n\\n[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/55/Parliamentary_Buildings_%26_Govt._Imperial_guard%2C_Brisbane%2C_March%2C_1869.jpg/250px-Parliamentary_Buildings_%26_Govt._Imperial_guard%2C_Brisbane%2C_March%2C_1869.jpg)](./File:Parliamentary_Buildings_&_Govt._Imperial_guard,_Brisbane,_March,_1869.jpg)\\n\\n[Queensland Parliament](./Parliament_House,_Brisbane \"Parliament House, Brisbane\") under guard, [George street](./George_Street,_Brisbane \"George Street, Brisbane\") c.1869\\n\\nFrom the 1860s, Brisbane became a key [Western Pacific](./Pacific_Ocean \"Pacific Ocean\") port in the trade of [blackbirded](./Blackbirding \"Blackbirding\") labour, serving as a major point of transit for [South Sea Islander](./South_Sea_Islander \"South Sea Islander\") indentured labourers transported to plantation districts across Queensland, linking the city to the wider plantation economy of the colony. Although administered as an indenture system, many historians regard the trade as a form of slavery or slavery-like coercion, citing deceptive recruitment practices, restrictions on movement and widespread exploitation.\\n\\nIn the late 19th century, Brisbane had become unusually cosmopolitan for its size, as its Pacific-facing port and persistent labour shortages encouraged earlier and more varied migration streams than most other Australian colonial cities, including German farming families, substantial Scottish and Irish communities, a Chinese quarter at [Frog\\'s Hollow](./Frog\\'s_Hollow \"Frog\\'s Hollow\"), a Jewish congregation, and one of Australia\\'s earliest Russian migrant groups.”[[48]](./Brisbane#cite_note-49)[[49]](./Brisbane#cite_note-50)[[50]](./Brisbane#cite_note-51)[[51]](./Brisbane#cite_note-52)\\n\\nBrisbane\\'s late 19th century development was repeatedly shaped by major natural disasters. The city suffered [two destructive fires](./Great_fire_of_Brisbane \"Great fire of Brisbane\") in 1864, which destroyed much of the early commercial centre and led to new building regulations favouring brick over timber construction. Economic hardship in 1866 sparked the “Bread or Blood” protests outside [Government House](./Old_Government_House,_Brisbane \"Old Government House, Brisbane\"), reflecting wider tensions during the [financial crisis](./Panic_of_1866 \"Panic of 1866\") of the mid-1860s. Vulnerability to natural hazards continued into the 1890s, when the [Great Flood of 1893](./Great_Flood_of_1893 \"Great Flood of 1893\") inundated large areas of Brisbane, swept away the first [Victoria Bridge](./Victoria_Bridge,_Brisbane \"Victoria Bridge, Brisbane\") and became one of the most significant floods in the city\\'s history. Following the destruction of the Victoria Bridge, a temporary ferry service was introduced, but it was later involved in the 1896 [Pearl ferry disaster](./Capsize_of_the_ferry_Pearl \"Capsize of the ferry Pearl\"), in which an estimated 80–100 people lost their lives.[[52]](./Brisbane#cite_note-53)\\n\\n### 20th century\\n\\n[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6a/Queensland_State_Archives_161_Queen_Street_Brisbane_looking_south_west_from_Creek_Street_c_1932.png/250px-Queensland_State_Archives_161_Queen_Street_Brisbane_looking_south_west_from_Creek_Street_c_1932.png)](./File:Queensland_State_Archives_161_Queen_Street_Brisbane_looking_south_west_from_Creek_Street_c_1932.png)\\n\\nCorner of [Queen](./Queen_Street,_Brisbane \"Queen Street, Brisbane\") and [Creek street](./Creek_Street,_Brisbane \"Creek Street, Brisbane\"), c.1932\\n\\nFollowing [Federation](./Federation_of_Australia \"Federation of Australia\") in 1901, Brisbane entered the new century as the capital of Queensland, marked by civic celebrations and the laying of the foundation stone for [St John\\'s Cathedral](./St_John\\'s_Cathedral_(Brisbane) \"St John\\'s Cathedral (Brisbane)\").\\n\\nThe early decades of the century were shaped by labour unrest, including the [1912 Brisbane general strike](./1912_Brisbane_general_strike \"1912 Brisbane general strike\"), and by political tensions during the [First World War](./First_World_War \"First World War\"), such as the 1917 [raid on the Queensland Government Printing Office](./Raid_on_the_Queensland_Government_Printing_Office \"Raid on the Queensland Government Printing Office\"), and the [Red Flag riots](./Red_Flag_riots \"Red Flag riots\") of 1918–19.\\nIn 1925 the creation of the [City of Brisbane](./City_of_Brisbane \"City of Brisbane\") formed Australia\\'s largest municipal authority, followed in 1930 by the opening of [Brisbane City Hall](./Brisbane_City_Hall \"Brisbane City Hall\"), one of the city\\'s most significant public buildings, and later in 1940 with the opening of the [Story Bridge](./Story_Bridge \"Story Bridge\").\\n\\n[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/13/StateLibQld_1_130295_Parade_of_RAAF_recruits_through_Queen_Street%2C_Brisbane%2C_August_1940.jpg/250px-StateLibQld_1_130295_Parade_of_RAAF_recruits_through_Queen_Street%2C_Brisbane%2C_August_1940.jpg)](./File:StateLibQld_1_130295_Parade_of_RAAF_recruits_through_Queen_Street,_Brisbane,_August_1940.jpg)\\n\\nParade of [Royal Australian Air Force](./Royal_Australian_Air_Force \"Royal Australian Air Force\") servicemen through [Queen street](./Queen_Street,_Brisbane \"Queen Street, Brisbane\"), c.\\u20091940\\n\\nDuring the [Second World War](./Second_World_War \"Second World War\"), Brisbane became a major Allied headquarters and logistics centre in the [South West Pacific](./South_West_Pacific_theatre_of_World_War_II \"South West Pacific theatre of World War II\"). General Douglas MacArthur established his headquarters in the city at [MacArthur Chambers](./MacArthur_Chambers \"MacArthur Chambers\"), and large numbers of American and Australian personnel were stationed throughout the metropolitan area. Wartime conditions reshaped daily life, from rationing and rapid military construction to social pressures that culminated in incidents such as the [Battle of Brisbane](./Battle_of_Brisbane \"Battle of Brisbane\") in 1942.\\n\\nThe post-war era brought [large-scale immigration](./Immigration_to_Australia \"Immigration to Australia\"), suburban expansion, and rising car ownership. Severe floods such as the [1974 flood](./1974_Brisbane_flood \"1974 Brisbane flood\") caused extensive damage and prompted major changes in water management, including the construction of [Wivenhoe Dam](./Wivenhoe_Dam \"Wivenhoe Dam\").\\n\\nUnder the government of [Joh Bjelke-Petersen](./Joh_Bjelke-Petersen \"Joh Bjelke-Petersen\"), Queensland experienced far-reaching restrictions on civil liberties, including the effective banning of street marches and extensive police enforcement, conditions that catalysed widespread civil rights protests and student activism. In response, an artistic counter-cultural movement took shape, and Brisbane\\'s cultural scene became one of the [earliest punk rock](./Brisbane_punk_rock \"Brisbane punk rock\") centres.\\n\\n[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/ff/Expo_88_%288075991938%29.jpg/330px-Expo_88_%288075991938%29.jpg)](./File:Expo_88_(8075991938).jpg)\\n\\nCrowds at [World Expo 88](./World_Expo_88 \"World Expo 88\"), the international exposition that transformed Brisbane\\'s South Bank precinct\\n\\nThe end of the Bjelke-Petersen era was followed by a period of civic and political renewal in Brisbane, as reforms arising from the [Fitzgerald Inquiry](./Fitzgerald_Inquiry \"Fitzgerald Inquiry\") reshaped policing and governance in the city and supported the expansion of cultural institutions, heritage conservation and urban redevelopment. Following Expo 88, the South Brisbane riverfront was redeveloped into the [South Bank Parklands](./South_Bank_Parklands \"South Bank Parklands\"), which opened in 1992 and became one of the city\\'s major cultural precincts.[[53]](./Brisbane#cite_note-54)\\n\\n### 21st century\\n\\nThe early 21st century has seen sustained population growth, inner-city renewal and major transport investment, including the [South East Busway](./South_East_Busway \"South East Busway\"), [AirportlinkM7](./Airport_Link,_Brisbane \"Airport Link, Brisbane\"), [Legacy Way](./Legacy_Way \"Legacy Way\") and [Cross River Rail](./Cross_River_Rail \"Cross River Rail\"). Significant urban redevelopment occurred across the inner city, with expanding high-rise construction and new riverfront precincts such as [Howard Smith Wharves](./Howard_Smith_Wharves \"Howard Smith Wharves\") and the [Queen\\'s Wharf](./Queen\\'s_Wharf,_Brisbane \"Queen\\'s Wharf, Brisbane\") project.\\n\\nThe city also became increasingly multicultural, with sustained migration from Asia and the Pacific contributing to demographic growth in the outer suburbs and the emergence of new cultural and commercial districts across the metropolitan area.\\nCultural infrastructure grew with the opening of the [Gallery of Modern Art (GOMA)](./Gallery_of_Modern_Art,_Brisbane \"Gallery of Modern Art, Brisbane\") in 2006 and the redevelopment of the [State Library of Queensland](./State_Library_of_Queensland \"State Library of Queensland\") as part of the broader expansion of the [Queensland Cultural Centre](./Queensland_Cultural_Centre \"Queensland Cultural Centre\"). Major flood events in the [2011](./2010–2011_Queensland_floods \"2010–2011 Queensland floods\") and [2022](./2022_eastern_Australia_floods \"2022 eastern Australia floods\") floods renewed focus on resilience and river management, while the severe rainfall associated with [Cyclone Alfred](./Cyclone_Alfred \"Cyclone Alfred\") in 2025 prompted further review of flood-mitigation planning.\\n\\nOngoing development across [South Bank](./South_Bank,_Queensland \"South Bank, Queensland\") and the cultural precinct continued into the 2020s, and Brisbane\\'s selection as host of the [2032 Olympic and Paralympic Games](./2032_Summer_Olympics \"2032 Summer Olympics\") initiated long-term metropolitan planning and redevelopment.\\n\\nGeography and environment\\n-------------------------\\n\\nMain article: [Geography of Brisbane](./Geography_of_Brisbane \"Geography of Brisbane\")\\n\\n[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/54/Sandy_Shores_of_Moreton_Bay.jpg/250px-Sandy_Shores_of_Moreton_Bay.jpg)](./File:Sandy_Shores_of_Moreton_Bay.jpg)\\n\\nSatellite image of Brisbane metropolitan area taken in 2019\\n\\n[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/af/Howard_Smith_Wharves%2C_Brisbane_in_Oct_2019%2C_20.jpg/250px-Howard_Smith_Wharves%2C_Brisbane_in_Oct_2019%2C_20.jpg)](./File:Howard_Smith_Wharves,_Brisbane_in_Oct_2019,_20.jpg)\\n\\nNew Farm Cliffs, formed from [Brisbane tuff](./Brisbane_tuff \"Brisbane tuff\") rock, behind [Howard Smith Wharves](./Howard_Smith_Wharves \"Howard Smith Wharves\")\\n\\n[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3a/Scarborough_Beach%2C_Redcliffe.jpg/250px-Scarborough_Beach%2C_Redcliffe.jpg)](./File:Scarborough_Beach,_Redcliffe.jpg)\\n\\nScarborough Beach at [Scarborough](./Scarborough,_Queensland \"Scarborough, Queensland\") on the [Redcliffe Peninsula](./Redcliffe_Peninsula \"Redcliffe Peninsula\")\\n\\nBrisbane is in the southeast corner of Queensland. The city is centred along the Brisbane River, and its eastern suburbs line the shores of Moreton Bay, a bay of the Coral Sea. The greater Brisbane region is on the coastal plain east of the [Great Dividing Range](./Great_Dividing_Range \"Great Dividing Range\"), with the [Taylor](./Taylor_Range \"Taylor Range\") and [D\\'Aguilar](./D\\'Aguilar_Range \"D\\'Aguilar Range\") ranges extending into the metropolitan area. Brisbane\\'s metropolitan area sprawls along the Moreton Bay floodplain between the [Gold](./Gold_Coast,_Queensland \"Gold Coast, Queensland\") and [Sunshine](./Sunshine_Coast,_Queensland \"Sunshine Coast, Queensland\") coasts, approximately from [Caboolture](./Caboolture \"Caboolture\") in the north to [Beenleigh](./Beenleigh \"Beenleigh\") in the south, and across to [Ipswich](./Ipswich,_Queensland \"Ipswich, Queensland\") in the south west.\\n\\nThe Brisbane River is a wide [tidal](./Tide \"Tide\") [estuary](./Estuary \"Estuary\") and its waters throughout most of the metropolitan area are [brackish](./Brackish \"Brackish\") and [navigable](./Navigable \"Navigable\"). The river takes a winding course through the metropolitan area with many steep curves from the southwest to its mouth at Moreton Bay in the east. The metropolitan area is also traversed by several other rivers and creeks including the [North Pine](./North_Pine_River \"North Pine River\") and [South Pine](./South_Pine_River \"South Pine River\") rivers in the northern suburbs, which converge to form the [Pine River](./Pine_River_(Queensland) \"Pine River (Queensland)\") estuary at [Bramble Bay](./Bramble_Bay \"Bramble Bay\"), the [Caboolture River](./Caboolture_River \"Caboolture River\") further north, the [Logan](./Logan_River \"Logan River\") and [Albert](./Albert_River_(Queensland) \"Albert River (Queensland)\") rivers in the south-eastern suburbs, and [tributaries](./Tributaries \"Tributaries\") of the Brisbane River including the [Bremer River](./Bremer_River_(Queensland) \"Bremer River (Queensland)\") in the south-western suburbs, [Breakfast Creek](./Breakfast_Creek \"Breakfast Creek\") in the inner-north, [Norman Creek](./Norman_Creek_(Queensland) \"Norman Creek (Queensland)\") in the inner-south, [Oxley Creek](./Oxley_Creek \"Oxley Creek\") in the south, [Bulimba Creek](./Bulimba_Creek \"Bulimba Creek\") in the inner south-east and [Moggill Creek](./Moggill_Creek \"Moggill Creek\") in the west. The city is on a low-lying [floodplain](./Floodplain \"Floodplain\"),[[54]](./Brisbane#cite_note-55) with the risk of flooding addressed by various state and local government regulations and plans.[[55]](./Brisbane#cite_note-56)\\n\\nThe waters of Moreton Bay are sheltered from large [swells](./Swell_(ocean) \"Swell (ocean)\") by [Moreton](./Moreton_Island \"Moreton Island\"), [Stradbroke](./North_Stradbroke_Island \"North Stradbroke Island\") and [Bribie](./Bribie_Island \"Bribie Island\") islands, so whilst the bay can become rough in windy conditions, the waves at the Moreton Bay coastline are generally not [surfable](./Surfing \"Surfing\"). Unsheltered surf beaches lie on the eastern coasts of [Moreton](./Moreton_Island \"Moreton Island\"), [Stradbroke](./North_Stradbroke_Island \"North Stradbroke Island\") and [Bribie](./Bribie_Island \"Bribie Island\") islands and on the Gold Coast and Sunshine Coast to the south and north respectively. The southern part of Moreton Bay also contains smaller islands such as [St Helena Island](./St_Helena_Island_National_Park \"St Helena Island National Park\"), [Peel Island](./Peel_Island_(Queensland) \"Peel Island (Queensland)\"), [Coochiemudlo Island](./Coochiemudlo_Island \"Coochiemudlo Island\"), [Russell Island](./Russell_Island_(Moreton_Bay) \"Russell Island (Moreton Bay)\"), [Lamb Island](./Lamb_Island,_Queensland \"Lamb Island, Queensland\") and [Macleay Island](./Macleay_Island \"Macleay Island\").\\n\\nThe city of Brisbane is hilly.[[56]](./Brisbane#cite_note-thenandnow-57) The urban area, including the central business district, are partially elevated by spurs of the [Herbert Taylor Range](./Herbert_Taylor_Range \"Herbert Taylor Range\"), such as the summit of [Mount Coot-tha](./Mount_Coot-tha \"Mount Coot-tha\"), reaching up to 300\\xa0m (980\\xa0ft) and [Enoggera Hill](./Enoggera_Hill \"Enoggera Hill\"). The [D\\'Aguilar National Park](./D\\'Aguilar_National_Park \"D\\'Aguilar National Park\"), encompassing the [D\\'Aguilar Range](./D\\'Aguilar_Range \"D\\'Aguilar Range\"), bounds the north-west of Brisbane\\'s built-up area, and contains the taller peaks of [Mount Nebo](./Mount_Nebo_(Queensland) \"Mount Nebo (Queensland)\"), [Camp Mountain](./Camp_Mountain \"Camp Mountain\"), [Mount Pleasant](./Mount_Pleasant,_Queensland_(Moreton_Bay) \"Mount Pleasant, Queensland (Moreton Bay)\"), [Mount Glorious](./Mount_Glorious \"Mount Glorious\"), [Mount Samson](./Mount_Samson \"Mount Samson\") and [Mount Mee](./Mount_Mee \"Mount Mee\"). Other prominent rises in Brisbane are [Mount Gravatt](./Mount_Gravatt \"Mount Gravatt\"), [Toohey Mountain](./Toohey_Mountain \"Toohey Mountain\"), [Mount Petrie](./Mount_Petrie \"Mount Petrie\"), [Highgate Hill](./Highgate_Hill,_Queensland \"Highgate Hill, Queensland\"), [Mount Ommaney](./Mount_Ommaney \"Mount Ommaney\"), [Stephens Mountain](./Stephens_Mountain \"Stephens Mountain\"), and [Whites Hill](./Whites_Hill \"Whites Hill\"), which are dotted across the city.\\n\\nMuch of the rock upon which Brisbane is located is the characteristic [Brisbane tuff](./Brisbane_tuff \"Brisbane tuff\"), a form of welded [ignimbrite](./Ignimbrite \"Ignimbrite\"),[[57]](./Brisbane#cite_note-wdhs-58) which is most prominently found at the [Kangaroo Point Cliffs](./Kangaroo_Point_Cliffs \"Kangaroo Point Cliffs\") at [Kangaroo Point](./Kangaroo_Point,_Queensland \"Kangaroo Point, Queensland\") and the New Farm Cliffs on the [Petrie Bight](./Petrie_Bight \"Petrie Bight\") reach of the Brisbane River. The stone was used in the construction of historical buildings such as the [Commissariat Store](./Commissariat_Store,_Brisbane \"Commissariat Store, Brisbane\") and [Cathedral of St Stephen](./Cathedral_of_St_Stephen,_Brisbane \"Cathedral of St Stephen, Brisbane\"), and the roadside [kerbs](./Kerbs \"Kerbs\") in inner areas of Brisbane are still manufactured of Brisbane tuff.\\n\\n### Ecology\\n\\n[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/75/Jacaranda_mimosifolia_trees_in_New_Farm_Park%2C_Queensland%2C_07.jpg/250px-Jacaranda_mimosifolia_trees_in_New_Farm_Park%2C_Queensland%2C_07.jpg)](./File:Jacaranda_mimosifolia_trees_in_New_Farm_Park,_Queensland,_07.jpg)\\n\\n[Jacaranda](./Jacaranda_mimosifolia \"Jacaranda mimosifolia\") trees in bloom at [New Farm Park](./New_Farm_Park \"New Farm Park\")\\n\\nBrisbane is located within the [South East Queensland](./South_East_Queensland \"South East Queensland\") [biogeographic region](./Interim_Biogeographic_Regionalisation_for_Australia \"Interim Biogeographic Regionalisation for Australia\"), and is home to numerous [Eucalyptus](./Eucalyptus \"Eucalyptus\") varieties. Common trees in Brisbane include the [Moreton Bay fig](./Moreton_Bay_fig \"Moreton Bay fig\"), an evergreen [banyan](./Banyan \"Banyan\") with large [buttress roots](./Buttress_roots \"Buttress roots\") named for the region which are often lit with [decorative lights](./Christmas_lights \"Christmas lights\") in the inner city, as well as the [jacaranda](./Jacaranda_mimosifolia \"Jacaranda mimosifolia\"), a subtropical tree native to [South America](./South_America \"South America\") which line many avenues and parks and bloom with purple flowers during October.[[58]](./Brisbane#cite_note-59) Other trees common to the metropolitan area include [Moreton Bay chestnut](./Moreton_Bay_chestnut \"Moreton Bay chestnut\"), [broad-leaved paperbark](./Broad-leaved_paperbark \"Broad-leaved paperbark\"), [poinciana](./Delonix_regia \"Delonix regia\"), [weeping lilli pilli](./Weeping_lilli_pilli \"Weeping lilli pilli\") and [Bangalow palm](./Bangalow_palm \"Bangalow palm\"). Some of the banks of the [Brisbane River](./Brisbane_River \"Brisbane River\") and [Moreton Bay](./Moreton_Bay \"Moreton Bay\") are home to [mangrove](./Australian_mangroves \"Australian mangroves\") wetlands. The [red poinsettia](./Poinsettia \"Poinsettia\") is the original official floral emblem of Brisbane, however it is native to Central America.[[59]](./Brisbane#cite_note-:1-60) An additional floral emblem, the [Brisbane wattle](./Acacia_fimbriata \"Acacia fimbriata\"), which is native to the Brisbane area, was added in 2023.[[60]](./Brisbane#cite_note-61)\\n\\nBrisbane is home to numerous bird species, with common species including [rainbow lorikeets](./Rainbow_lorikeet \"Rainbow lorikeet\"), [kookaburras](./Kookaburra \"Kookaburra\"), [galahs](./Galah \"Galah\"), [Australian white ibises](./Australian_white_ibis \"Australian white ibis\"), [Australian brushturkeys](./Australian_brushturkey \"Australian brushturkey\"), [Torresian crows](./Torresian_crow \"Torresian crow\"), [Australian magpies](./Australian_magpie \"Australian magpie\") and [noisy miners](./Noisy_miner \"Noisy miner\"). Common reptiles include [common garden skinks](./Common_garden_skink \"Common garden skink\"), [Australian water dragons](./Australian_water_dragon \"Australian water dragon\"), [bearded dragons](./Bearded_dragons \"Bearded dragons\") and [blue-tongued lizards](./Blue-tongued_skink \"Blue-tongued skink\"). [Common ringtail possums](./Common_ringtail_possum \"Common ringtail possum\") and [flying foxes](./Flying_foxes \"Flying foxes\") are common in parks and yards throughout the city, as are [common crow butterflies](./Euploea_core \"Euploea core\"), [blue triangle butterflies](./Graphium_sarpedon \"Graphium sarpedon\"), [golden orb-weaver spiders](./Nephila \"Nephila\") and [St Andrew\\'s Cross spiders](./Argiope_keyserlingi \"Argiope keyserlingi\"). The [Brisbane River](./Brisbane_River \"Brisbane River\") is home to many fish species including [yellowfin bream](./Acanthopagrus_australis \"Acanthopagrus australis\"), [flathead](./Flathead_(fish) \"Flathead (fish)\"), [Australasian snapper](./Australasian_snapper \"Australasian snapper\"), and [bull sharks](./Bull_shark \"Bull shark\"). The waters of [Moreton Bay](./Moreton_Bay \"Moreton Bay\") are home to [dugongs](./Dugong \"Dugong\"), [humpback whales](./Humpback_whale \"Humpback whale\"), [dolphins](./Dolphin \"Dolphin\"), [mud crabs](./Scylla_serrata \"Scylla serrata\"), [soldier crabs](./Mictyris_longicarpus \"Mictyris longicarpus\"), [Moreton Bay bugs](./Moreton_Bay_bug \"Moreton Bay bug\") and numerous [shellfish](./Shellfish \"Shellfish\") species. The [koala](./Koala \"Koala\") and the [graceful tree frog](./Graceful_tree_frog \"Graceful tree frog\") are the official faunal emblems of Brisbane, however both are increasingly less common due to the effects of increased development and climate change.[[59]](./Brisbane#cite_note-:1-60)[[61]](./Brisbane#cite_note-62)\\n\\n### Climate\\n\\nMain article: [Climate of Brisbane](./Climate_of_Brisbane \"Climate of Brisbane\")\\n\\n[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/ba/Storm_over_the_Brisbane_city_centre.jpg/250px-Storm_over_the_Brisbane_city_centre.jpg)](./File:Storm_over_the_Brisbane_city_centre.jpg)\\n\\nLightning over the Brisbane city centre, February 2020\\n\\nBrisbane has a [humid subtropical climate](./Humid_subtropical_climate \"Humid subtropical climate\") ([Köppen climate classification](./Köppen_climate_classification \"Köppen climate classification\"): *Cfa*)[[62]](./Brisbane#cite_note-63) with hot, wet summers and moderately drier, mild winters.[[63]](./Brisbane#cite_note-64)[[64]](./Brisbane#cite_note-65) Brisbane experiences an annual mean minimum of 16.6\\xa0°C (62\\xa0°F) and mean maximum of 26.6\\xa0°C (80\\xa0°F), making it Australia\\'s second-hottest capital city after [Darwin](./Darwin,_Northern_Territory \"Darwin, Northern Territory\").[[65]](./Brisbane#cite_note-auto1-66) Seasonality is not pronounced, and average maximum temperatures of above 26\\xa0°C (79\\xa0°F) persist from October through to April.\\n\\nDue to its proximity to the Coral Sea and a warm ocean current, Brisbane\\'s overall temperature variability is somewhat less than most Australian capitals. Summers are long, hot, and wet, but temperatures only occasionally reach 35\\xa0°C (95\\xa0°F) or more. Eighty percent of summer days record a maximum temperature of 27 to 33\\xa0°C (81 to 91\\xa0°F). Winters are short and warm, with average maximums of about 22\\xa0°C (72\\xa0°F); maximum temperatures below 20\\xa0°C (68\\xa0°F) are rare.\\n\\nThe city\\'s highest recorded temperature was 43.2\\xa0°C (109.8\\xa0°F) on [Australia Day](./Australia_Day \"Australia Day\") 1940 at the Brisbane Regional Office,[[66]](./Brisbane#cite_note-ReferenceB-67) with the highest temperature at the current station being 41.7\\xa0°C (107.1\\xa0°F) on 22 February 2004;[[67]](./Brisbane#cite_note-68) but temperatures above 38\\xa0°C (100\\xa0°F) are uncommon. On 19 July 2007, Brisbane\\'s temperature fell below the freezing point for the first time since records began, registering −0.1\\xa0°C (31.8\\xa0°F) at the airport station.[[68]](./Brisbane#cite_note-69) The city station has never dropped below 2\\xa0°C (36\\xa0°F),[[69]](./Brisbane#cite_note-ReferenceA-70) with the average coldest night during winter being around 6\\xa0°C (43\\xa0°F), however locations in the west of the metropolitan area such as [Ipswich](./Ipswich,_Queensland \"Ipswich, Queensland\") have dropped as low as −5\\xa0°C (23\\xa0°F) with heavy ground frost.[[70]](./Brisbane#cite_note-71)\\n\\nIn 2009, Brisbane recorded its hottest winter day (from June to August) at 35.4\\xa0°C (95.7\\xa0°F) on 24 August;[[71]](./Brisbane#cite_note-72) The average July day however is around 22\\xa0°C (72\\xa0°F) with sunny skies and low humidity, occasionally as high as 27\\xa0°C (81\\xa0°F), whilst maximum temperatures below 18\\xa0°C (64\\xa0°F) are uncommon and usually associated with brief periods of cloud and winter rain.[[69]](./Brisbane#cite_note-ReferenceA-70) The highest minimum temperature ever recorded in Brisbane was 28.0\\xa0°C (82.4\\xa0°F) on 29 January 1940 and again on 21 January 2017, whilst the lowest maximum temperature was 10.2\\xa0°C (50.4\\xa0°F) on 12 August 1954.[[66]](./Brisbane#cite_note-ReferenceB-67)\\n\\nSleet or snow is exceptionally rare in Brisbane. The Bureau of Meteorology has only three official records of snow in Brisbane: June 1927, June 1932 (witnessed by seven people), and September 1958 (light flakes were seen by four people at 5:15pm in Moorooka, Wooloowin, Bowen Hills and Taringa).\\nUnofficial reports exist of earlier snowfalls, such as follows from July 1882:[*[This quote needs a citation](./Wikipedia:Inline_citation#When_you_must_use_inline_citations \"Wikipedia:Inline citation\")*]\\n\"The snow was most noticeable in Woolloongabba, but in Stanley Street, South Brisbane it was sufficiently heavy to allow of people wiping it from their clothing.\\n\"In the vicinity of the museum the fall was, though very slight, plainly noticeable.\\n\"It is said that snow fell in this city 35 years ago, and the summer following the period of the fall was remarkable for its excessive heat.\"[*[citation needed](./Wikipedia:Citation_needed \"Wikipedia:Citation needed\")*]\\n\\nAnnual precipitation is ample. From November to March, thunderstorms are common over Brisbane, with the more severe events accompanied by large damaging hail stones, torrential rain and destructive winds. To the west of Brisbane, [supercell thunderstorms](./Supercell \"Supercell\") often form during the late spring and summer months. These can include tornadic supercells.[[72]](./Brisbane#cite_note-73) On an annual basis, Brisbane averages 124 clear days, with overcast skies more common in the warmer months.[[73]](./Brisbane#cite_note-74) Dewpoints in the summer average at around 20\\xa0°C (68\\xa0°F); the [apparent temperature](./Apparent_temperature \"Apparent temperature\") exceeds 30\\xa0°C (86\\xa0°F) on almost all summer days.[[69]](./Brisbane#cite_note-ReferenceA-70) Brisbane\\'s wettest day occurred on 21 January 1887, when 465 millimetres (18.3\\xa0in) of rain fell on the city, the highest maximum daily rainfall of Australia\\'s capital cities. The wettest month on record was February 1893, when 1,025.9 millimetres (40.39\\xa0in) of rain fell, although in the last 30 years the record monthly rainfall has been a much lower 479.8 millimetres (18.89\\xa0in) from December 2010. Very occasionally a whole month will pass with no recorded rainfall, the last time this happened was August 1991.[[66]](./Brisbane#cite_note-ReferenceB-67) The city has suffered four major floods since its founding, in [February 1893](./1893_Brisbane_flood \"1893 Brisbane flood\"), [January 1974](./1974_Brisbane_Flood \"1974 Brisbane Flood\") (partially a result of [Cyclone Wanda](./Cyclone_Wanda \"Cyclone Wanda\")), [January 2011](./2010–2011_Queensland_floods \"2010–2011 Queensland floods\") (partially a result of [Cyclone Tasha](./Cyclone_Tasha \"Cyclone Tasha\")) and [February 2022](./2022_eastern_Australia_floods \"2022 eastern Australia floods\").\\n\\nBrisbane is within the southern reaches of the [tropical cyclone](./Tropical_cyclone \"Tropical cyclone\") risk zone. Full-strength tropical cyclones rarely affect Brisbane, but occasionally do so, the most recent being [Cyclone Alfred](./Cyclone_Alfred \"Cyclone Alfred\"), making landfall as a category 1 around [Bribie Island](./Bribie_Island \"Bribie Island\") on the 8th of March, 2025, bringing destructive winds and causing significant flooding throughout parts of south-eastern Queensland and north-eastern New South Wales. The more common risk is from ex-tropical cyclones (tropical low systems), which typically bring destructive winds and flooding rains.[[74]](./Brisbane#cite_note-75)\\n\\nThe temperature of the ocean
