series)\")\\n\\n[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/87/Brisbane_CBD_seen_from_Mount_Coot-tha_Lookout%2C_2025%2C_06.jpg/250px-Brisbane_CBD_seen_from_Mount_Coot-tha_Lookout%2C_2025%2C_06.jpg)](./File:Brisbane_CBD_seen_from_Mount_Coot-tha_Lookout,_2025,_06.jpg)\\n\\nThe [Brisbane CBD](./Brisbane_CBD \"Brisbane CBD\") and surrounds from the [Mount Coot-tha Lookout](./Mount_Coot-tha_Lookout \"Mount Coot-tha Lookout\") in the [Taylor Range](./Taylor_Range \"Taylor Range\")\\n\\nThe [Brisbane central business district](./Brisbane_central_business_district \"Brisbane central business district\") (CBD, colloquially referred to as \"the city\") lies in a curve of the Brisbane river. The CBD covers 2.2\\xa0km2 (0.8\\xa0sq\\xa0mi) and is walkable. Most central streets are named after members of the [House of Hanover](./House_of_Hanover \"House of Hanover\"). [Queen Street](./Queen_Street,_Brisbane \"Queen Street, Brisbane\") (named in honour of [Queen Victoria](./Queen_Victoria \"Queen Victoria\")) is Brisbane\\'s traditional [main street](./Main_street \"Main street\") and contains its largest [pedestrian mall](./Pedestrian_mall \"Pedestrian mall\"), the [Queen Street Mall](./Queen_Street_Mall \"Queen Street Mall\"). Streets named after female members ([Adelaide](./Adelaide_Street,_Brisbane \"Adelaide Street, Brisbane\"), [Alice](./Alice_Street,_Brisbane \"Alice Street, Brisbane\"), [Ann](./Ann_Street,_Brisbane \"Ann Street, Brisbane\"), [Charlotte](./Charlotte_Street,_Brisbane \"Charlotte Street, Brisbane\"), [Elizabeth](./Elizabeth_Street,_Brisbane \"Elizabeth Street, Brisbane\"), [Margaret](./Margaret_Street,_Brisbane \"Margaret Street, Brisbane\"), and [Mary](./Mary_Street,_Brisbane \"Mary Street, Brisbane\")) run parallel to [Queen Street](./Queen_Street,_Brisbane \"Queen Street, Brisbane\") and perpendicular to streets named after male members ([Albert](./Albert_Street,_Brisbane \"Albert Street, Brisbane\"), [Edward](./Edward_Street,_Brisbane \"Edward Street, Brisbane\"), [George](./George_Street,_Brisbane \"George Street, Brisbane\"), and [William](./William_Street,_Brisbane \"William Street, Brisbane\")).\\n\\nThe CBD\\'s [squares](./Town_square \"Town square\") include [King George Square](./King_George_Square \"King George Square\"), [Post Office Square](./Post_Office_Square,_Brisbane \"Post Office Square, Brisbane\") and [ANZAC Square](./ANZAC_Square,_Brisbane \"ANZAC Square, Brisbane\") (home to the city\\'s central [war memorial](./War_memorial \"War memorial\")).\\n\\n[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0d/River_views_of_Brisbane_CBD%2C_October_2018%2C_03.jpg/250px-River_views_of_Brisbane_CBD%2C_October_2018%2C_03.jpg)](./File:River_views_of_Brisbane_CBD,_October_2018,_03.jpg)\\n\\nThe [CBD](./Brisbane_CBD \"Brisbane CBD\") and [South Bank](./South_Bank,_Queensland \"South Bank, Queensland\") fronts the [Brisbane River](./Brisbane_River \"Brisbane River\")\\n\\nAt the broadest level, Brisbane\\'s metropolitan area is informally divided into the northside and the southside, with the dividing line being the [Brisbane River](./Brisbane_River \"Brisbane River\"),[[77]](./Brisbane#cite_note-78) as crossing one of the 15 [bridges across the river](./Bridges_over_the_Brisbane_River \"Bridges over the Brisbane River\") is required to travel to the opposite side by land transport. Due to the river\\'s winding trajectory, this results in many areas which are south of the CBD being classified as located in the northside, and vice versa. At a more specific level, the metropolitan area contains informal regions including the northern, southern, eastern and western suburbs, the bayside suburbs along the Moreton Bay coastline, and the Moreton Bay, Redland, Logan and Ipswich regions in the outer north, east, south and west respectively.\\n\\nGreater Brisbane had a density of 159 inhabitants per square kilometre (410/sq\\xa0mi) in 2021.[[7]](./Brisbane#cite_note-auto5-7) Like most Australian cities, Brisbane has a sprawling metropolitan area which takes in excess of one hour to traverse either north to south or east to west by car without traffic.\\n\\nFrom the 1970s onwards, there has been a large increase in the construction of [apartment](./Apartment \"Apartment\") developments, including [mid-rise](./Mid-rise \"Mid-rise\") and [high rise](./High_rise \"High rise\") buildings, which has quickened in the 21st century. At the 2021 census, 73.4% of residents lived in [separate houses](./Separate_houses \"Separate houses\"), 14.7% lived in [apartments](./Apartment \"Apartment\"), and 11.4% lived in [townhouses](./Townhouse \"Townhouse\"), [terrace houses](./Terrace_house \"Terrace house\"), or [semidetached](./Semidetached \"Semidetached\") houses.[[7]](./Brisbane#cite_note-auto5-7)\\n\\n### Parklands\\n\\n[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/48/Tree_lined_avenue_at_the_City_Botanic_Gardens%2C_Brisbane.jpg/250px-Tree_lined_avenue_at_the_City_Botanic_Gardens%2C_Brisbane.jpg)](./File:Tree_lined_avenue_at_the_City_Botanic_Gardens,_Brisbane.jpg)\\n\\n[Moreton Bay figs](./Moreton_Bay_fig \"Moreton Bay fig\") at the [City Botanic Gardens](./City_Botanic_Gardens \"City Botanic Gardens\")\\n\\nBrisbane\\'s major parklands include the riverside [City Botanic Gardens](./City_Botanic_Gardens \"City Botanic Gardens\") at [Gardens Point](./Gardens_Point \"Gardens Point\"),[[78]](./Brisbane#cite_note-79) [Roma Street Parkland](./Roma_Street_Parkland \"Roma Street Parkland\"), the 27-hectare [Victoria Park](./Victoria_Park,_Brisbane \"Victoria Park, Brisbane\") at [Spring Hill](./Spring_Hill,_Queensland \"Spring Hill, Queensland\") and [Herston](./Herston,_Queensland \"Herston, Queensland\"), [South Bank Parklands](./South_Bank_Parklands \"South Bank Parklands\") along the river at [South Bank](./South_Bank,_Queensland \"South Bank, Queensland\"), the [Brisbane Botanic Gardens](./Brisbane_Botanic_Gardens,_Mount_Coot-tha \"Brisbane Botanic Gardens, Mount Coot-tha\") at [Mount Coot-tha](./Mount_Coot-tha \"Mount Coot-tha\") and the riverside [New Farm Park](./New_Farm_Park \"New Farm Park\") at [New Farm](./New_Farm \"New Farm\").\\n\\nThere are many national parks surrounding the Brisbane metropolitan area. The [D\\'Aguilar National Park](./D\\'Aguilar_National_Park \"D\\'Aguilar National Park\") is a major [national park](./National_park \"National park\") along the northwest of the metropolitan area in the [D\\'Aguilar Range](./D\\'Aguilar_Range \"D\\'Aguilar Range\"). The [Glass House Mountains National Park](./Glass_House_Mountains_National_Park \"Glass House Mountains National Park\") is located to the north of the metropolitan area in the [Glass House Mountains](./Glass_House_Mountains,_Queensland \"Glass House Mountains, Queensland\") and provides green space between the Brisbane metropolitan area and the [Sunshine Coast](./Sunshine_Coast,_Queensland \"Sunshine Coast, Queensland\"). The [Tamborine National Park](./Tamborine_National_Park \"Tamborine National Park\") at [Tamborine Mountain](./Tamborine_Mountain \"Tamborine Mountain\") is located in the [Gold Coast hinterland](./Gold_Coast_hinterland \"Gold Coast hinterland\") to the south of the metropolitan area.\\n\\nThe eastern metropolitan area is built along the [Moreton Bay Marine Park](./Moreton_Bay_Marine_Park \"Moreton Bay Marine Park\"), encompassing [Moreton Bay](./Moreton_Bay \"Moreton Bay\"). Significant areas of [Moreton](./Moreton_Island \"Moreton Island\"), [North Stradbroke](./North_Stradbroke_Island \"North Stradbroke Island\") and [Bribie](./Bribie_Island \"Bribie Island\") islands also covered by the [Moreton Island National Park](./Moreton_Island_National_Park \"Moreton Island National Park\"), [Naree Budjong Djara National Park](./Naree_Budjong_Djara_National_Park \"Naree Budjong Djara National Park\") and the [Bribie Island National Park](./Bribie_Island_National_Park \"Bribie Island National Park\") respectively. The [Boondall Wetlands](./Boondall_Wetlands \"Boondall Wetlands\") in the suburb of [Boondall](./Boondall \"Boondall\") include 1,100 hectares of wetlands which are home to |\\n\\n### Architecture\\n\\nFurther information: [List of tallest buildings in Brisbane](./List_of_tallest_buildings_in_Brisbane \"List of tallest buildings in Brisbane\") and [Queenslander (architecture)](./Queenslander_(architecture) \"Queenslander (architecture)\")\\n\\n[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7a/Commissariat_Store%2C_Brisbane_10.jpg/250px-Commissariat_Store%2C_Brisbane_10.jpg)](./File:Commissariat_Store,_Brisbane_10.jpg)\\n\\nThe [Commissariat Store](./Commissariat_Store,_Brisbane \"Commissariat Store, Brisbane\") dates back to 1828 and was built by convicts.\\n\\nBrisbane has a number of heritage buildings, some of which date back to the 1820s, including [The Old Windmill](./The_Old_Windmill,_Brisbane \"The Old Windmill, Brisbane\") in [Wickham Park](./Wickham_Park,_Brisbane \"Wickham Park, Brisbane\"), built by convict labour in 1824,[[79]](./Brisbane#cite_note-80) which is the oldest surviving building in Brisbane, and the [Commissariat Store](./Commissariat_Store,_Brisbane \"Commissariat Store, Brisbane\") on [William Street](./William_Street,_Brisbane \"William Street, Brisbane\"), built by convict labour in 1828, which was originally used as a grain house, and is now the home of the Royal Historical Society of Brisbane and contains a museum.[[80]](./Brisbane#cite_note-81)[[81]](./Brisbane#cite_note-82)[[82]](./Brisbane#cite_note-83) Other 19th and early 20th-century buildings of architectural significance include the [Treasury Building](./Treasury_Building,_Brisbane \"Treasury Building, Brisbane\"), [City Hall](./Brisbane_City_Hall \"Brisbane City Hall\"), [Customs House](./Customs_House,_Brisbane \"Customs House, Brisbane\"), [Land Administration Building](./Land_Administration_Building \"Land Administration Building\"), [MacArthur Chambers](./MacArthur_Chambers \"MacArthur Chambers\"), [The Mansions](./The_Mansions,_Brisbane \"The Mansions, Brisbane\"), [National Australia Bank Building](./National_Australia_Bank_(308_Queen_Street) \"National Australia Bank (308 Queen Street)\"), the [Old Museum Building](./Old_Museum_Building,_Brisbane \"Old Museum Building, Brisbane\") and the [Federation-style](./Federation_architecture \"Federation architecture\") [People\\'s Palace](./People\\'s_Palace,_Brisbane \"People\\'s Palace, Brisbane\"), a former temperance hotel on [Edward Street](./Edward_Street,_Brisbane \"Edward Street, Brisbane\").\\n\\nOne of the oldest synagogues in the Queensland area is the Brisbane Synagogue located on Margaret Street in Brisbane city. This historic synagogue can be attributed as the \"centerpiece of the Jewish community\\'s presence in the state\" It was established in 1866 and designed by architect Arthur Morry. Another architect by the name of Andrea Stombuco has also been credited as a designer of the synagogue by previous members of the community. The architectural design of this historic synagogue is in the style of Neo-Moorish also known as Byzantine style.[[83]](./Brisbane#cite_note-84)\\n\\n[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/72/Queenslander_style_house_in_Sherwood%2C_Queensland%2C_2022%2C_03.jpg/250px-Queenslander_style_house_in_Sherwood%2C_Queensland%2C_2022%2C_03.jpg)](./File:Queenslander_style_house_in_Sherwood,_Queensland,_2022,_03.jpg)\\n\\n[Queenslander](./Queenslander_(architecture) \"Queenslander (architecture)\")-style house in [Sherwood](./Sherwood,_Queensland \"Sherwood, Queensland\"), a suburb of Brisbane\\n\\n[Queenslander](./Queenslander_(architecture) \"Queenslander (architecture)\")-style housing is common in Brisbane.[[84]](./Brisbane#cite_note-LinOsb-85) Queenslander homes typically feature timber construction with large [verandahs](./Verandah \"Verandah\"), [gabled](./Gable_roof \"Gable roof\") corrugated iron roofs, and high ceilings. Most of these houses are elevated on stumps (also called stilts), traditionally built of timber, which allow for a void under the houses which aids in cooling. The relatively low cost of timber in south-east Queensland meant that until recently, most residences were constructed of timber, rather than brick or stone.[*[citation needed](./Wikipedia:Citation_needed \"Wikipedia:Citation needed\")*] Early legislation decreed a minimum size for residential blocks leading to few [terrace houses](./Terrace_house \"Terrace house\") being constructed in Brisbane.[*[citation needed](./Wikipedia:Citation_needed \"Wikipedia:Citation needed\")*] The high-density housing that historically existed came in the form of miniature [Queenslander](./Queenslander_(architecture) \"Queenslander (architecture)\")-style houses which resemble the much larger traditional styles, but are sometimes only one-quarter the size.[*[citation needed](./Wikipedia:Citation_needed \"Wikipedia:Citation needed\")*] These houses are most common in the inner-city suburbs.\\n\\nBrisbane is home to several of [Australia\\'s tallest buildings](./List_of_tallest_buildings_in_Australia \"List of tallest buildings in Australia\"). All of Brisbane\\'s skyscrapers (buildings with a height greater than 150\\xa0m (490\\xa0ft)) are located within the CBD, but the inner suburbs are also home to a number of high-density buildings, [Torbreck](./Torbreck,_Brisbane \"Torbreck, Brisbane\") being the first high-rise and mix-use residential development in [Queensland](./Queensland \"Queensland\"). Brisbane\\'s 91-metre City Hall was the city\\'s tallest building for decades after its completion in 1930 and was finally surpassed in 1970, which marked the beginning of the widespread construction of high-rise buildings.[*[citation needed](./Wikipedia:Citation_needed \"Wikipedia:Citation needed\")*]\\n\\n[Brisbane\\'s tallest building](./List_of_tallest_buildings_in_Brisbane \"List of tallest Stephen\\'s](./Cathedral_of_St_Stephen,_Brisbane \"Cathedral of St Stephen, Brisbane\") (Catholic).\\n\\nThe most popular non-Christian religions at the 2021 census were [Hindu](./Hinduism \"Hinduism\") (2%), [Buddhist](./Buddhist \"Buddhist\") (1.9%), and [Muslim](./Islam \"Islam\") (1.8%).[[104]](./Brisbane#cite_note-Archived_copy-109)\\n\\nEconomy\\n-------\\n\\nMain articles: [Economy of Brisbane](./Economy_of_Brisbane \"Economy of Brisbane\") and [Port of Brisbane](./Port_of_Brisbane \"Port of Brisbane\")\\n\\n[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/dc/River_views_of_Brisbane_CBD_seen_from_Kangaroo_Point%2C_Queensland_in_April_2019%2C_04.jpg/250px-River_views_of_Brisbane_CBD_seen_from_Kangaroo_Point%2C_Queensland_in_April_2019%2C_04.jpg)](./File:River_views_of_Brisbane_CBD_seen_from_Kangaroo_Point,_Queensland_in_April_2019,_04.jpg)\\n\\nThe Golden Triangle financial precinct surrounding [Eagle Street Pier](./Eagle_Street_Pier_ferry_wharf \"Eagle Street Pier ferry wharf\") in the [CBD](./Brisbane_central_business_district \"Brisbane central business district\")\\n\\n[Categorised as](./Globalization_and_World_Cities_Research_Network \"Globalization and World Cities Research Network\") a [global city](./Global_city \"Global city\"), Brisbane is among [Asia-Pacific](./Asia-Pacific \"Asia-Pacific\") [cities with largest GDPs](./List_of_cities_by_GDP \"List of cities by GDP\") and is one of the major business hubs in [information technology](./Information_technology \"Information technology\"), [real estate](./Real_estate \"Real estate\") and [food](./Food_industry \"Food industry\").[[105]](./Brisbane#cite_note-110)\\n\\nSome of the largest companies headquartered in Brisbane, all among Australia\\'s largest, include [Suncorp Group](./Suncorp_Group \"Suncorp Group\"), [Virgin Australia](./Virgin_Australia \"Virgin Australia\"), [Aurizon](./Aurizon \"Aurizon\"), [Bank of Queensland](./Bank_of_Queensland \"Bank of Queensland\"), [Flight Centre](./Flight_Centre \"Flight Centre\"), [Great Southern Bank](./Great_Southern_Bank \"Great Southern Bank\"), [Australian Retirement Trust](./Australian_Retirement_Trust \"Australian Retirement Trust\"), [Domino\\'s Pizza Enterprises](./Domino\\'s_Pizza_Enterprises \"Domino\\'s Pizza Enterprises\"), [Star Entertainment Group](./Star_Entertainment_Group \"Star Entertainment Group\"), [ALS](./ALS_Limited \"ALS Limited\"), [TechnologyOne](./TechnologyOne \"TechnologyOne\"), [NEXTDC](./NEXTDC \"NEXTDC\"), [Super Retail Group](./Super_Retail_Group \"Super Retail Group\"), [New Hope Coal](./New_Hope_Coal \"New Hope Coal\"), [Jumbo Interactive](./Jumbo_Interactive \"Jumbo Interactive\"), [National Storage](./National_Storage \"National Storage\"), [Collins Foods](./Collins_Foods \"Collins Foods\"), and [Boeing Australia](./Boeing_Australia \"Boeing Australia\").[[106]](./Brisbane#cite_note-111) Most major Australian companies, as well as numerous international companies, have contact offices in Brisbane.\\n\\nBrisbane throughout its history has been one of Australia\\'s most important [seaport](./Seaport \"Seaport\") cities. The [Port of Brisbane](./Port_of_Brisbane \"Port of Brisbane\") is located at the Brisbane River\\'s mouth on [Moreton Bay](./Moreton_Bay \"Moreton Bay\") and on the adjacent Fisherman\\'s Island, created by means of [land reclamation](./Land_reclamation \"Land reclamation\"). It is the 3rd busiest port in Australia for value of goods.[[107]](./Brisbane#cite_note-Port_Technology-112) [Container freight](./Containerization \"Containerization\"), sugar, grain, coal and bulk liquids are the major exports. Most of the port facilities are less than three decades old and some are built on reclaimed [mangroves](./Mangrove \"Mangrove\") and [wetlands](./Wetlands \"Wetlands\"). The Port is a part of the [Australia TradeCoast](./Australia_TradeCoast \"Australia TradeCoast\"), which includes the [Brisbane Airport](./Brisbane_Airport \"Brisbane Airport\") along with large industrial estates located along both banks at the mouth of the Brisbane River.[[108]](./Brisbane#cite_note-TradeCoast-113)\\n\\nWhite-collar industries include information technology, [financial services](./Financial_services \"Financial services\"), higher education and [public sector](./Public_sector \"Public sector\") administration generally concentrated in and around the central business district and satellite hubs located in the inner suburbs such as [South Brisbane](./South_Brisbane \"South Brisbane\"), [Fortitude Valley](./Fortitude_Valley \"Fortitude Valley\"), [Spring Hill](./Spring_Hill,_Queensland \"Spring Hill, Queensland\"), [Milton](./Milton,_Queensland \"Milton, Queensland\"), and [Toowong](./Toowong \"Toowong\"), [Upper Mount Gravatt](./Upper_Mount_Gravatt,_Queensland \"Upper Mount Gravatt, Queensland\") could be considered as a 2nd CBD to the city.\\n\\nBlue-collar industries, including petroleum refining, [stevedoring](./Stevedoring \"Stevedoring\"), paper milling, [metalworking](./Metalworking \"Metalworking\") and [QR](./Queensland_Rail \"Queensland Rail\") railway workshops, tend to be located on the lower reaches of the Brisbane River proximal to the [Port of Brisbane](./Port_of_Brisbane \"Port of Brisbane\") and in new industrial zones on the urban fringe.\\n\\n[Tourism](./Tourism_in_Brisbane \"Tourism in Brisbane\") is an important part of the Brisbane economy, both in its own right and as a gateway to other areas of Queensland,[[109]](./Brisbane#cite_note-114) as is [international education](./International_students \"International students\"), with over 95,000 international students enrolled in universities and other tertiary education institutions in the central [City of Brisbane](./City_of_Brisbane \"City of Brisbane\") [local government area](./Local_government_area \"Local government area\") alone in In addition, its size enables the gallery to exhibit particularly large shows.\\n\\nGOMA houses the [Australian Cinémathèque](./Australian_Cinémathèque \"Australian Cinémathèque\"), a dedicated film facility offering a diverse program of screenings, including international cinema, influential filmmakers, rare prints, restorations and silent films with a live musical accompaniment. Most screenings are free admission.[[111]](./Brisbane#cite_note-116)\\n\\n[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f2/QPAC_Exterior.jpg/250px-QPAC_Exterior.jpg)](./File:QPAC_Exterior.jpg)\\n\\n[Queensland Performing Arts Centre](./Queensland_Performing_Arts_Centre \"Queensland Performing Arts Centre\")\\n\\nDramatic and musical theatre performances are held at the multiple large theatres located at [Queensland Performing Arts Centre](./Queensland_Performing_Arts_Centre \"Queensland Performing Arts Centre\") (QPAC). The [Brisbane Powerhouse](./Brisbane_Powerhouse \"Brisbane Powerhouse\") in [New Farm](./New_Farm \"New Farm\") and the [Judith Wright Arts Centre](./Judith_Wright_Arts_Centre \"Judith Wright Arts Centre\") in [Fortitude Valley](./Fortitude_Valley \"Fortitude Valley\") also feature diverse programs featuring exhibitions and festivals of visual art, music and dance. Brisbane is also home to numerous small theatres including the [Brisbane Arts Theatre](./Brisbane_Arts_Theatre \"Brisbane Arts Theatre\") in [Petrie Terrace](./Petrie_Terrace \"Petrie Terrace\"), the [La Boite Theatre Company](./La_Boite_Theatre_Company \"La Boite Theatre Company\") which performs at the [Roundhouse Theatre](./Roundhouse_Theatre \"Roundhouse Theatre\") at [Kelvin Grove](./Kelvin_Grove,_Queensland \"Kelvin Grove, Queensland\"), the [Twelfth Night Theatre](./Twelfth_Night_Theatre \"Twelfth Night Theatre\") at [Bowen Hills](./Bowen_Hills \"Bowen Hills\"), the [Metro Arts Theatre](./Metro_Arts_Theatre \"Metro Arts Theatre\") in [Edward Street](./Edward_Street,_Brisbane \"Edward Street, Brisbane\"), and the Queensland Theatre Company\\'s [Bille Brown Theatre](./Bille_Brown_Theatre \"Bille Brown Theatre\") in [West End](./West_End,_Queensland \"West End, Queensland\").\\n\\nThe [Queensland Performing Arts Centre](./Queensland_Performing_Arts_Centre \"Queensland Performing Arts Centre\") (QPAC) at [South Bank](./South_Bank,_Queensland \"South Bank, Queensland\"), consists of the Lyric Theatre, the Concert Hall, the Cremorne Theatre and the Playhouse Theatre and is home to the [Queensland Ballet](./Queensland_Ballet \"Queensland Ballet\"), [Opera Queensland](./Opera_Queensland \"Opera Queensland\"), the [Queensland Theatre Company](./Queensland_Theatre_Company \"Queensland Theatre Company\"), and the [Queensland Symphony Orchestra](./Queensland_Symphony_Orchestra \"Queensland Symphony Orchestra\"). The [Queensland Conservatorium](./Queensland_Conservatorium \"Queensland Conservatorium\"), a musical conservatorium in which professional music companies and conservatorium students also stage performances, is located within the [South Bank Parklands](./South_Bank_Parklands \"South Bank Parklands\"). Numerous choirs present performances across the city annually. These choirs include the Brisbane Chorale, Queensland Choir, Brisbane Chamber Choir, Canticum Chamber Choir, ChoirWorks, Imogen Children\\'s Chorale, and [Brisbane Birralee Voices](./Brisbane_Birralee_Voices \"Brisbane Birralee Voices\").\\n\\n[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/fe/Go_between_bridge.jpg/250px-Go_between_bridge.jpg)](./File:Go_between_bridge.jpg)\\n\\n[Go Between Bridge](./Go_Between_Bridge \"Go Between Bridge\"), named after local jangle pop band [the Go-Betweens](./The_Go-Betweens \"The Go-Betweens\")\\n\\nBrisbane\\'s live music scene is diverse and its history is often intertwined with social unrest and authoritarian politics, as retold by journalist Andrew Stafford in [*Pig City: From The Saints to Savage Garden*](./Pig_City_(music_festival)#Pig_City_(book) \"Pig City (music festival)\"). Popular live music venues, including pubs and clubs, can be found within both the CBD and [Fortitude Valley](./Fortitude_Valley \"Fortitude Valley\").[[112]](./Brisbane#cite_note-117)[[113]](./Brisbane#cite_note-118) The [Brisbane Entertainment Centre](./Brisbane_Entertainment_Centre \"Brisbane Entertainment Centre\") at [Boondall](./Boondall \"Boondall\") hosts many musical concerts, with some of the largest being held at [Lang Park](./Lang_Park \"Lang Park\"). Musicians from Brisbane include the [Bee Gees](./Bee_Gees \"Bee Gees\") (raised in [Redcliffe](./Redcliffe,_Queensland \"Redcliffe, Queensland\") and [Cribb Island](./Cribb_Island \"Cribb Island\")), [the Saints](./The_Saints_(Australian_band) \"The Saints (Australian band)\") (based in Brisbane since 1974, one of the first [punk rock](./Punk_rock \"Punk rock\") bands), [the Go-Betweens](./The_Go-Betweens \"The Go-Betweens\") (after whom Brisbane\\'s [Go Between Bridge](./Go_Between_Bridge \"Go Between Bridge\") is named, and whose songs and albums, such as *[Spring Hill Fair](./Spring_Hill_Fair \"Spring Hill Fair\")*, reflect the attitudes of 1980s Brisbane), [Savage Garden](./Savage_Garden \"Savage Garden\"), [Powderfinger](./Powderfinger \"Powderfinger\") (who met at [Brisbane Grammar School](./Brisbane_Grammar_School \"Brisbane Grammar School\") and the [University of Queensland](./University_of_Queensland \"University of Queensland\")), and [the Veronicas](./The_Veronicas \"The Veronicas\") (born and raised in [Albany Creek](./Albany_Creek \"Albany Creek\")). The city is featured in music including the Saints\\' \"[Brisbane (Security City)](./Prehistoric_Sounds \"Prehistoric Sounds\")\" (1978); [the Stranglers](./The_Stranglers \"The Stranglers\")\\' \"[Nuclear Device](./Nuclear_Device_(The_Wizard_of_Aus) \"Nuclear Device (The Wizard of Aus)\")\" (1979) about [Joh Bjelke-Petersen](./Joh_Bjelke-Petersen \"Joh Bjelke-Petersen\"); [Midnight Oil](./Midnight_Oil \"Midnight Oil\")\\'s single \"[Dreamworld](./Dreamworld_(Midnight_Oil_song) \"Dreamworld (Midnight Oil song)\")\" (1987); and Powderfinger\\'s album *[Vulture Street](./Vulture_Street_(album) \"Vulture Street (album)\")* (2003).\\n\\n[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/cc/Exterior_of_the_State_Library_of_Queensland%2C_2021.jpg/250px-Exterior_of_the_State_Library_of_Queensland%2C_2021.jpg)](./File:Exterior_of_the_State_Library_of_Queensland,_2021.jpg)\\n\\n[State Library of Queensland](./State_Library_of_Queensland \"State Library of Queensland\")\\n\\nProminent writers from Brisbane include [David Malouf](./David_Malouf \"David Malouf\") (whose 1975 novel *Johnno* is set in Brisbane and at [Brisbane Grammar School](./Brisbane_Grammar_School \"Brisbane Grammar School\") during [World War II](./World_War_II \"World War II\")), [Nick Earls](./Nick_Earls \"Nick Earls\") (whose 1996 novel *Zigzag Street* is set at Zigzag Street in [Red Hill](./Red_Hill,_Queensland \"Red Hill, Queensland\")), and [Li Cunxin](./Li_Cunxin \"Li Cunxin\"), author of [Mao\\'s Last Dancer](./Mao\\'s_Last_Dancer_(book) \"Mao\\'s Last Dancer (book)\") and artistic director of the Queensland Ballet. *Brisbane* is a 2018 novel by Russian writer [Eugene Vodolazkin](./Eugene_Vodolazkin \"Eugene Vodolazkin\"). A public holiday is held for each [local government area](./Local_government_area \"Local government area\") across Brisbane to enable widespread public attendance.\\n\\nThe [Brisbane Festival](./Brisbane_Festival \"Brisbane Festival\") is held each September at [South Bank Parklands](./South_Bank_Parklands \"South Bank Parklands\"), the [CBD](./Brisbane_central_business_district \"Brisbane central business district\") and surrounding areas. [Tangalooma](./Tangalooma \"Tangalooma\") resort on Moreton Island is popular for its nightly wild dolphin feeding attraction, and for operating Australia\\'s longest running whale watching cruises. The [Fort Lytton National Park](./Fort_Lytton_National_Park \"Fort Lytton National Park\") including a [colonial defence fort](./Fort_Lytton_Historic_Military_Precinct \"Fort Lytton Historic Military Precinct\") and museum is also a historical bayside attraction. Beachside suburbs such as those on the [Redcliffe Peninsula](./Redcliffe_Peninsula \"Redcliffe Peninsula\"), as well as [Shorncliffe](./Shorncliffe,_Queensland \"Shorncliffe, Queensland\"), [Sandgate](./Sandgate,_Queensland \"Sandgate, Queensland\"), [Wynnum](./Wynnum \"Wynnum\"), [Manly](./Manly,_Queensland \"Manly, Queensland\") and [Wellington Point](./Wellington_Point \"Wellington Point\") are also popular attractions for their bayside beaches, piers, and infrastructure for boating, sailing, fishing and [kitesurfing](./Kitesurfing \"Kitesurfing\").\\n\\nThere are many [national parks](./National_park \"National park\") surrounding the Brisbane metropolitan area which are popular recreational attractions for hiking and bushwalking. The [D\\'Aguilar National Park](./D\\'Aguilar_National_Park \"D\\'Aguilar National Park\") runs along the northwest of the metropolitan area in the [D\\'Aguilar Range](./D\\'Aguilar_Range \"D\\'Aguilar Range\"), and contains popular bushwalking and hiking peaks at [Mount Nebo](./Mount_Nebo_(Queensland) \"Mount Nebo (Queensland)\"), [Camp Mountain](./Camp_Mountain \"Camp Mountain\"), [Mount Pleasant](./Mount_Pleasant,_Queensland_(Moreton_Bay) \"Mount Pleasant, Queensland (Moreton Bay)\"), [Mount Glorious](./Mount_Glorious \"Mount Glorious\"), [Mount Samson](./Mount_Samson \"Mount Samson\") and [Mount Mee](./Mount_Mee \"Mount Mee\"). The [Glass House Mountains National Park](./Glass_House_Mountains_National_Park \"Glass House Mountains National Park\") is located to the north of the metropolitan area in the [Glass House Mountains](./Glass_House_Mountains,_Queensland \"Glass House Mountains, Queensland\") between it and that of the [Sunshine Coast](./Sunshine_Coast,_Queensland \"Sunshine Coast, Queensland\"). The [Tamborine National Park](./Tamborine_National_Park \"Tamborine National Park\") at [Tamborine Mountain](./Tamborine_Mountain \"Tamborine Mountain\") is located in the [Gold Coast hinterland](./Gold_Coast_hinterland \"Gold Coast hinterland\") to the south of the metropolitan area. [Moreton](./Moreton_Island \"Moreton Island\"), [North Stradbroke](./North_Stradbroke_Island \"North Stradbroke Island\") and [Bribie](./Bribie_Island \"Bribie Island\") islands are substantially covered by the [Moreton Island National Park](./Moreton_Island_National_Park \"Moreton Island National Park\"), [Naree Budjong Djara National Park](./Naree_Budjong_Djara_National_Park \"Naree Budjong Djara National Park\") and the [Bribie Island National Park](./Bribie_Island_National_Park \"Bribie Island National Park\") respectively. The [Boondall Wetlands](./Boondall_Wetlands \"Boondall Wetlands\") in the suburb of [Boondall](./Boondall \"Boondall\") are protected [mangrove](./Australian_mangroves \"Australian mangroves\") wetlands with floating walking trails.\\n\\nImmediately to the south and north of Brisbane are the [Gold Coast](./Gold_Coast,_Queensland \"Gold Coast, Queensland\") and [Sunshine Coast](./Sunshine_Coast,_Queensland \"Sunshine Coast, Queensland\") respectively, which are home to several of Australia\\'s most popular swimming and surfing beaches, and are popular day and weekend destinations for Brisbanites.\\n\\nIn 2015, a competition by travel guidebook *[Rough Guides](./Rough_Guides \"Rough Guides\")* saw Brisbane elected as one of the top ten most beautiful cities in the world, citing reasons such as \"its winning combination of high-rise modern architecture, lush green spaces and the enormous Brisbane River that snakes its way through the centre before emptying itself into the azure Moreton Bay\".[[130]](./Brisbane#cite_note-135)\\n\\nGovernance\\n----------\\n\\nMain articles: [City of Brisbane](./City_of_Brisbane \"City of Brisbane\"), [Logan City](./Logan_City \"Logan City\"), [City of Moreton Bay](./City_of_Moreton_Bay \"City of Moreton Bay\"), [City of Ipswich](./City_of_Ipswich \"City of Ipswich\"), [Redland City](./Redland_City \"Redland City\"), [Scenic Rim Region](./Scenic_Rim_Region \"Scenic Rim Region\"), and [Government of Queensland](./Government_of_Queensland \"Government of Queensland\")\\n\\n[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/68/CoA_of_Brisbane.svg/120px-CoA_of_Brisbane.svg.png)](./File:CoA_of_Brisbane.svg)\\n\\n[City of Brisbane coat of flag](./Flag_of_Brisbane \"Flag of Brisbane\")\\n\\nUnlike other Australian capital cities, a large portion of the greater metropolitan area, or Greater Capital City Statistical Area (GCCSA) of Brisbane is controlled by a single [local government area](./Local_government_in_Australia \"Local government in Australia\"), the [City of Brisbane](./City_of_Brisbane \"City of Brisbane\"), which is the largest local government area (in terms of population and budget) in Australia, serving more than 40% of the GCCSA\\'s population. It was formed by the merger of twenty smaller LGAs in 1925, and covers an area of 1,367\\xa0km2 (528\\xa0sq\\xa0mi). The remainder of the metropolitan area falls into the LGAs of [Logan City](./Logan_City \"Logan City\") to the south, [City of Moreton Bay](./City_of_Moreton_Bay \"City of Moreton Bay\") in the northern suburbs, the [City of Ipswich](./City_of_Ipswich \"City of Ipswich\") to the south west, [Redland City](./Redland_City \"Redland City\") to the south east, and into the [Somerset](./Somerset_Region \"Somerset Region\"), [Scenic Rim](./Scenic_Rim_Region \"Scenic Rim Region\") and [Lockyer Valley](./Lockyer_Valley_Region \"Lockyer Valley Region\") regions on the urban periphery. Several of these are also among the nation\\'s most populous LGAs.\\n\\nEach LGA is governed under a similar structure, including a directly elected mayor (including the [Lord Mayor of Brisbane](./Lord_Mayor_of_Brisbane \"Lord Mayor of Brisbane\")), as well as a council composed of councillors representing geographical wards. [Brisbane City Hall](./Brisbane_City_Hall \"Brisbane City Hall\") is the seat of the [Brisbane City Council](./Brisbane_City_Council \"Brisbane City Council\"), the governing corporation of the City of Brisbane LGA, and the bulk of its executive offices are located at the [Brisbane Square](./Brisbane_Square \"Brisbane Square\") skyscraper.\\n\\n[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4a/Government_House_seen_from_street%2C_Brisbane%2C_Queensland%2C_2019%2C_01.jpg/250px-Government_House_seen_from_street%2C_Brisbane%2C_Queensland%2C_2019%2C_01.jpg)](./File:Government_House_seen_from_street,_Brisbane,_Queensland,_2019,_01.jpg)\\n\\n[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/77/Christmas_tree_in_2019_at_Parliament_House%2C_Brisbane%2C_Queensland_03.jpg/250px-Christmas_tree_in_2019_at_Parliament_House%2C_Brisbane%2C_Queensland_03.jpg)](./File:Christmas_tree_in_2019_at_Parliament_House,_Brisbane,_Queensland_03.jpg)\\n\\n[Government House, Brisbane](./Government_House,_Brisbane \"Government House, Brisbane\"), home to the [Governor of Queensland](./Governor_of_Queensland \"Governor of Queensland\") and [Parliament House](./Parliament_House,_Brisbane \"Parliament House, Brisbane\"), home of the [Parliament of Queensland](./Parliament_of_Queensland \"Parliament of Queensland\")\\n\\nAs the capital city of [Queensland](./Queensland \"Queensland\"), Brisbane is home to the [Parliament of Queensland](./Parliament_of_Queensland \"Parliament of Queensland\") at [Parliament House](./Parliament_House,_Brisbane \"Parliament House, Brisbane\") at [Gardens Point](./Gardens_Point \"Gardens Point\") in the [CBD](./Brisbane_central_business_district \"Brisbane central business district\"), adjacent to [Old Government House](./Old_Government_House,_Queensland \"Old Government House, Queensland\"). Queensland\\'s current [Government House](./Government_House,_Brisbane \"Government House, Brisbane\") is located in [Paddington](./Paddington,_Queensland \"Paddington, Queensland\"). The bulk of the state government\\'s executive offices are located at the [1 William Street](./1_William_Street,_Brisbane \"1 William Street, Brisbane\") skyscraper. The Queensland [Supreme](./Supreme_Court_of_Queensland \"Supreme Court of Queensland\") and [District](./District_Court_of_Queensland \"District Court of Queensland\") courts are located at the [Queen Elizabeth II Courts of Law](./Queen_Elizabeth_II_Courts_of_Law,_Brisbane \"Queen Elizabeth II Courts of Law, Brisbane\") in [George Street](./George_Street,_Brisbane \"George Street, Brisbane\"), while the [Magistrates](./Magistrates_Court_of_Queensland \"Magistrates Court of Queensland\") court is located at the adjacent [Brisbane Magistrates Court building](./Brisbane_Magistrates_Court_building \"Brisbane Magistrates Court building\"). The various federal courts are located at the [Commonwealth Law Courts](./Commonwealth_Law_Courts \"Commonwealth Law Courts\") building on [North Quay](./North_Quay,_Brisbane \"North Quay, Brisbane\").\\n\\nThe [Australian Army](./Australian_Army \"Australian Army\")\\'s [Enoggera Barracks](./Enoggera_Barracks \"Enoggera Barracks\") is located in [Enoggera](./Enoggera,_Queensland \"Enoggera, Queensland\"), while the historic [Victoria Barracks](./Victoria_Barracks,_Brisbane \"Victoria Barracks, Brisbane\") in [Petrie Terrace](./Petrie_Terrace \"Petrie Terrace\") now hosts a military museum. The [Royal Australian Navy](./Royal_Australian_Navy \"Royal Australian Navy\")\\'s [HMAS Moreton](./HMAS_Moreton \"HMAS Moreton\") base is located at [Bulimba](./Bulimba \"Bulimba\"). The [Royal Australian Air Force](./Royal_Australian_Air_Force \"Royal Australian Air Force\")\\'s [RAAF Base Amberley](./RAAF_Base_Amberley \"RAAF Base Amberley\") is located in [Amberley](./Amberley,_Queensland \"Amberley, Queensland\") in the outer south-west of the metropolitan area.\\n\\nBrisbane\\'s largest prisons and correctional facilities, the [Brisbane Correctional Centre](./Brisbane_Correctional_Centre \"Brisbane Correctional Centre\"), [Brisbane Women\\'s Correctional Centre](./Brisbane_Women\\'s_Correctional_Centre \"Brisbane Women\\'s Correctional Centre\"), [Arthur Gorrie Correctional Centre](./Arthur_Gorrie_Correctional_Centre \"Arthur Gorrie Correctional Centre\") and [Wolston Correctional Centre](./Wolston_Correctional_Centre \"Wolston Correctional Centre\") are located at [Wacol](./Wacol \"Wacol\"), while the city\\'s main historical prison, the [Boggo Road Gaol](./Boggo_Road_Gaol \"Boggo Road Gaol\"), is now a museum.\\n\\n### Politics\\n\\nGreater Brisbane is represented by five [local government areas](./Local_government_areas_of_Queensland \"Local government areas of Queensland\") (LGAs): the [City of Brisbane](./City_of_Brisbane \"City of Brisbane\"), the [City of Ipswich](./City_of_Ipswich \"City of Ipswich\"), [Logan City](./Logan_City \"Logan City\"), the [City of Moreton Bay](./City_of_Moreton_Bay \"City of Moreton Bay\") and [Redland City](./Redland_City \"Redland City\"). The City of Brisbane is by far the largest and the most populated of the four, and [Brisbane City Council](./Brisbane_City_Council \"Brisbane City Council\") has 27 members: 26 councillors elected from single-member [wards](./Ward_(electoral_subdivision) \"Ward (electoral subdivision)\") and one directly elected [Lord Mayor](./Lord_Mayor_of_Brisbane \"Lord Mayor of Brisbane\").\\n\\nIn the [Queensland Legislative Assembly](./Queensland_Legislative_Assembly \"Queensland Legislative Assembly\"), Brisbane is represented by 41 single-member [electoral districts](./Electoral_districts_of_Queensland \"Electoral districts of Queensland\"). In the [House of Representatives](./Australian_House_of_Representatives \"Australian House of Representatives\"), Brisbane is represented by 13 single-member [electoral divisions](./Divisions_of_the_Australian_House_of_Representatives \"Divisions of the Australian House of Representatives\").\\n\\nBrisbane has a diverse political climate. On the federal level, the [centre-left](./Centre-left \"Centre-left\") [Labor Party](./Australian_Labor_Party \"Australian Labor Party\") holds 11 Brisbane-based seats, while the [centre-right](./Centre-right \"Centre-right\") [Liberal National Party](./Liberal_National_Party_of_Queensland \"Liberal National Party of Queensland\") (LNP) and the [left-wing](./Left-wing \"Left-wing\") [Greens](./Australian_Greens \"Australian Greens\") each hold one ([Bowman](./Division_of_Bowman \"Division of Bowman\") and [Ryan](./Division_of_Ryan \"Division of Ryan\"), respectively). On the state level, Labor holds the vast majority of Brisbane-based seats, while the LNP holds nine and the Greens hold one ([Maiwar](./Electoral_district_of_Maiwar \"Electoral district of Maiwar\")). On the local level, LNP hold the Lord Mayoralty of Brisbane (with [Adrian Schrinner](./Adrian_Schrinner \"Adrian Schrinner\") as Lord Mayor) and 18 of the 26 wards of the City of Brisbane, while Labor holds five, the Greens hold two and an independent hold one ([Tennyson Ward](./Tennyson_Ward \"Tennyson Ward\")).\\n\\nEducation\\n---------\\n\\nSee also: [Lists of schools in and [Bridges over the Brisbane River](./Bridges_over_the_Brisbane_River \"Bridges over the Brisbane River\")\\n\\n### Transport\\n\\nBrisbane has an extensive transport network within the city, as well as connections to regional centres, interstate and to overseas destinations. Like all Australian cities, the most popular mode of transport is private car.[[138]](./Brisbane#cite_note-143) Public transport is provided by rail, bus and ferry services and is coordinated by [Translink](./TransLink_(South_East_Queensland) \"TransLink (South East Queensland)\"), which provides a unified ticketing and electronic payment system (known as *[go card](./Go_card \"Go card\")*) for [South East Queensland](./South_East_Queensland \"South East Queensland\"). The region is divided into seven [fare zones](./Fare \"Fare\") radiating outwards from the [Brisbane central business district](./Brisbane_central_business_district \"Brisbane central business district\") (CBD), with Brisbane\\'s built-up area falling within zones 1–3. Bus services are operated by public and private operators whereas trains and ferries are operated by public agencies. The CBD is the central hub for all public transport services with services focusing on [Roma Street](./Roma_Street_railway_station \"Roma Street railway station\"), [Central](./Central_railway_station,_Brisbane \"Central railway station, Brisbane\") and [Fortitude Valley](./Fortitude_Valley_railway_station \"Fortitude Valley railway station\") railway stations; [King George Square](./King_George_Square_busway_station \"King George Square busway station\"), [Queen Street](./Queen_Street_bus_station \"Queen Street bus station\") and [Roma Street](./Roma_Street_busway_station \"Roma Street busway station\") busway stations; and [North Quay](./North_Quay_ferry_wharf \"North Quay ferry wharf\"), [Riverside](./Riverside_ferry_wharf \"Riverside ferry wharf\") and [QUT Gardens Point](./QUT_Gardens_Point_ferry_wharf \"QUT Gardens Point ferry wharf\") ferry wharves.\\n\\n#### Roads\\n\\n[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5f/Hornibrook_april_2011_%28181%29.jpg/250px-Hornibrook_april_2011_%28181%29.jpg)](./File:Hornibrook_april_2011_(181).jpg)\\n\\n[Houghton Highway](./Houghton_Highway \"Houghton Highway\") and [Ted Smout Memorial Bridge](./Ted_Smout_Memorial_Bridge \"Ted Smout Memorial Bridge\") crossing [Bramble Bay](./Bramble_Bay \"Bramble Bay\"), Queensland\\'s longest bridges\\n\\nBrisbane is served by a large network of urban and inter-urban motorways. The [Pacific Motorway](./Pacific_Motorway_(Brisbane–Brunswick_Heads) \"Pacific Motorway (Brisbane–Brunswick Heads)\") (M3/M1) connects the inner-city with the southern suburbs, [Gold Coast](./Gold_Coast,_Queensland \"Gold Coast, Queensland\") and [New South Wales](./New_South_Wales \"New South Wales\"). The [Ipswich Motorway](./Ipswich_Motorway \"Ipswich Motorway\") (M7/M2) connects the inner-city with the outer south-western suburbs. The [Western Freeway](./Western_Freeway,_Brisbane \"Western Freeway, Brisbane\") and [Centenary Motorway](./Centenary_Motorway \"Centenary Motorway\") (M5) connect the city\\'s inner-west and outer south-west. The [Bruce Highway](./Bruce_Highway \"Bruce Highway\") and [Gympie Arterial Road](./Gympie_Arterial_Road \"Gympie Arterial Road\") (M1/M3) connect the city\\'s northern suburbs with the [Sunshine Coast](./Sunshine_Coast,_Queensland \"Sunshine Coast, Queensland\") and northern Queensland. The [Logan Motorway](./Logan_Motorway \"Logan Motorway\") (M2/M6) connects the southern and south-western suburbs. The [Gateway Motorway](./Gateway_Motorway \"Gateway Motorway\") is a [toll road](./Toll_road \"Toll road\") which connects the Gold and [Sunshine Coast](./Sunshine_Coast,_Queensland \"Sunshine Coast, Queensland\"). The [Port of Brisbane Motorway](./Port_of_Brisbane_Motorway \"Port of Brisbane Motorway\") links the Gateway Motorway to the [Port of Brisbane](./Port_of_Brisbane \"Port of Brisbane\"). The [Inner City Bypass](./Inner_City_Bypass,_Brisbane \"Inner City Bypass, Brisbane\") and [Riverside Expressway](./Riverside_Expressway \"Riverside Expressway\") serve as an inner ring freeway system to prevent motorists from travelling through the city\\'s congested centre.[[139]](./Brisbane#cite_note-144)\\n\\nBrisbane also has a large network of major road tunnels under the metropolitan area, known as the [TransApex](./TransApex \"TransApex\") network, which include the [Clem Jones Tunnel](./Clem_Jones_Tunnel \"Clem Jones Tunnel\") between the inner-north and inner-south, the [Airport Link tunnel](./Airport_Link,_Brisbane \"Airport Link, Brisbane\") in the north-east and the [Legacy Way tunnel](./Legacy_Way \"Legacy Way\") in the south-west. They are the three longest road tunnels in Australia.\\n\\n#### Bridges\\n\\n[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/26/Story_Bridge_%28Explore%29_-_Flickr_-_Fishyone1.jpg/250px-Story_Bridge_%28Explore%29_-_Flickr_-_Fishyone1.jpg)](./File:Story_Bridge_(Explore)_-_Flickr_-_Fishyone1.jpg)\\n\\nThe 777-metre [Story Bridge](./Story_Bridge \"Story Bridge\"), completed in 1940\\n\\nThe Brisbane River creates a barrier to road transport routes. In total there are [eighteen bridges](./Bridges_over_the_Brisbane_River \"Bridges over the Brisbane River\") over the river, mostly concentrated in the inner city area. The road bridges (which usually also include provision for pedestrians and cyclists) by distance from the river mouth are the [Sir Leo Hielscher Bridges](./Sir_Leo_Hielscher_Bridges \"Sir Leo Hielscher Bridges\"), the [Story Bridge](./Story_Bridge \"Story Bridge\"), the [Captain Cook Bridge](./Captain_Cook_Bridge,_Brisbane \"Captain Cook Bridge, Brisbane\"), the [Victoria Bridge](./Victoria_Bridge,_Brisbane \"Victoria Bridge, Brisbane\"), the [William Jolly Bridge](./William_Jolly_Bridge \"William Jolly Bridge\"), the [Go Between Bridge](./Go_Between_Bridge \"Go Between Bridge\"), the [Eleanor Schonell Bridge](./Eleanor_Schonell_Bridge \"Eleanor Schonell Bridge\"), the [Walter Taylor Bridge](./Walter_Taylor_Bridge \"Walter Taylor Bridge\") the [Centenary Bridge](./Centenary_Bridge \"Centenary Bridge\"), and the [Colleges Crossing](./Colleges_Crossing \"Colleges Crossing\"). There are three railway bridges, namely the [Merivale Bridge](./Merivale_Bridge \"Merivale Bridge\"), the [Albert Bridge](./Albert_Bridge,_Brisbane \"Albert Bridge, Brisbane\") and the [Indooroopilly Railway Bridge](./Indooroopilly_Railway_Bridge \"Indooroopilly Railway Bridge\"). There are also five pedestrian only bridges: the [Kangaroo Point Bridge](./Kangaroo_Point_Green_Bridge \"Kangaroo Point Green Bridge\"), the [Goodwill Bridge](./Goodwill_Bridge \"Goodwill Bridge\"), the [Neville Bonner Bridge](./Neville_Bonner_Bridge \"Neville Bonner Bridge\"), the [Kurilpa Bridge](./Kurilpa_Bridge \"Kurilpa Bridge\") and the [Jack Pesch Bridge](./Jack_Pesch_Bridge \"Jack Pesch Bridge\").\\n\\nThe [Houghton Highway](./Houghton_Highway \"Houghton Highway\") (northbound) and [Ted Smout Memorial Bridge](./Ted_Smout_Memorial_Bridge \"Ted Smout Memorial Bridge\") (southbound) bridges, over [Bramble Bay](./Bramble_Bay \"Bramble Bay\") between [Brighton, Queensland](./Brighton,_Queensland \"Brighton, Queensland\") and the [Redcliffe Peninsula](./Redcliffe_Peninsula \"Redcliffe Peninsula\"), are the longest bridges in the state. The abutment arches of the original crossing The [Hornibrook Bridge](./Hornibrook_Bridge \"Hornibrook Bridge\") still remain in place.\\n\\n#### Rail\\n\\n[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/94/Train_approaching_Roma_Street_railway_station%2C_Brisbane%2C_2021.jpg/250px-Train_approaching_Roma_Street_railway_station%2C_Brisbane%2C_2021.jpg)](./File:Train_approaching_Roma_Street_railway_station,_Brisbane,_2021.jpg)\\n\\nA [Queensland Rail NGR](./New_Generation_Rollingstock \"New Generation Rollingstock\") train approaching [Roma Street station](./Roma_Street_railway_station \"Roma Street railway station\")\\n\\nThe [Queensland Rail City network](./Queensland_Rail_City_network \"Queensland Rail City network\") consists of 154 train stations along 13 suburban and interurban rail lines and across the metropolitan area, namely: the [Airport](./Airport_railway_line,_Brisbane \"Airport railway line, Brisbane\"), [Beenleigh](./Beenleigh_railway_line \"Beenleigh railway line\"), [Caboolture](./Caboolture_railway_line \"Caboolture railway line\"), [Cleveland](./Cleveland_railway_line \"Cleveland railway line\"), [Doomben](./Doomben_railway_line \"Doomben railway line\"), [Ferny Grove](./Ferny_Grove_railway_line \"Ferny Grove railway line\"), [Ipswich/Rosewood](./Ipswich_and_Rosewood_railway_line \"Ipswich and Rosewood railway line\"), [Redcliffe Peninsula](./Redcliffe_Peninsula_railway_line \"Redcliffe Peninsula railway line\"), [Shorncliffe](./Shorncliffe_railway_line \"Shorncliffe railway line\"), and [Springfield](./Springfield_railway_line \"Springfield railway line\") lines, as well as the [Exhibition line](./Exhibition_railway_line \"Exhibition railway line\") which is used only for events at the [Brisbane Showgrounds](./Brisbane_Showgrounds \"Brisbane Showgrounds\"), as well as an inner-city bypass for freight and a turnback for long-distance services. The network extends to the [Gold](./Gold_Coast,_Queensland \"Gold Coast, Queensland\") and [Sunshine](./Sunshine_Coast,_Queensland \"Sunshine Coast, Queensland\") coasts, which are fully integrated into the network on the [Gold Coast line](./Gold_Coast_line \"Gold Coast line\") and [Sunshine Coast line](./Sunshine_Coast_railway_line \"Sunshine Coast railway line\"). The [Airtrain](./Airport_railway_line,_Brisbane \"Airport railway line, Brisbane\") service which runs on the [Airport line](./Airport_railway_line,_Brisbane \"Airport railway line, Brisbane\") is jointly operated between [Queensland Rail](./Queensland_Rail \"Queensland Rail\") and [Airtrain Citylink](./Airtrain_Citylink \"Airtrain Citylink\").\\n\\n55\\xa0million passenger trips were taken across the network in 2018–19.[[140]](./Brisbane#cite_note-145)\\n\\nConstruction of the network began in 1865[[141]](./Brisbane#cite_note-146) and has been progressively expanded in the subsequent centuries. [Electrification of the network](./Rail_electrification_in_Queensland \"Rail electrification in Queensland\") was completed between 1979 and 1988.\\n\\nThe [Cross River Rail](./Cross_River_Rail \"Cross River Rail\") project includes a twin rail tunnel (5.9\\xa0km (3.7\\xa0mi) long) which will pass under the Brisbane River to link two new railway stations at [Albert Street](./Albert_Street,_Brisbane \"Albert Street, Brisbane\") in the CBD and [Woolloongabba](./Woolloongabba \"Woolloongabba\"); it is under construction and scheduled to be completed in early 2025.[[142]](./Brisbane#cite_note-todo-147)\\n\\n#### Bus\\n\\n[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/72/Translink_Bus_Queensland_Australia.jpg/250px-Translink_Bus_Queensland_Australia.jpg)](./File:Translink_Bus_Queensland_Australia.jpg)\\n\\nTranslink bus\\n\\n[Brisbane\\'s busway network](./Busways_in_Brisbane \"Busways in Brisbane\") is a large dedicated [bus rapid transit](./Bus_rapid_transit \"Bus rapid transit\") network. The network comprises the [South East Busway](./South_East_Busway \"South East Busway\"), the [Northern Busway](./Northern_Busway,_Brisbane \"Northern Busway, Brisbane\") and the [Eastern Busway](./Eastern_Busway,_Brisbane \"Eastern Busway, Brisbane\"). The main network hubs are the [King George Square](./King_George_Square_busway_station \"King George Square busway station\"), [Queen Street](./Queen_Street_bus_station \"Queen Street bus station\"), and [Roma Street](./Roma_Street_busway_station \"Roma Street busway station\") busway stations.\\n\\nThere are also numerous suburban bus routes operating throughout the metropolitan area, including the high-frequency blue and maroon [CityGlider](./CityGlider \"CityGlider\") routes which run between [Newstead](./Newstead,_Queensland \"Newstead, Queensland\") and [West End](./West_End,_Queensland \"West End, Queensland\") (blue), and [Ashgrove](./Ashgrove,_Queensland \"Ashgrove, Queensland\") and [Coorparoo](./Coorparoo \"Coorparoo\") (maroon) respectively.\\n\\n[Brisbane Metro](./Brisbane_Metro \"Brisbane Metro\") is a [bus rapid transit](./Bus_rapid_transit \"Bus rapid transit\") (BRT) project which will initially consist of two routes (Metro 1 and 2) running between [Eight Mile Plains](./Eight_Mile_Plains_busway_station \"Eight Mile Plains busway station\") and [Roma Street](./Roma_Street_busway_station \"Roma Street busway station\"), and [UQ St Lucia (UQ Lakes)](./UQ_Lakes_busway_station \"UQ Lakes busway station\") and the [Royal Brisbane and Women\\'s Hospital](./Royal_Brisbane_and_Women\\'s_Hospital \"Royal Brisbane and Women\\'s Hospital\") respectively. It is set to open in 2024.\\n\\n#### Ferry\\n\\n[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/22/CityCat_Gootcha_%28ship%2C_2010%29_in_January_2019_in_Brisbane.jpg/250px-CityCat_Gootcha_%28ship%2C_2010%29_in_January_2019_in_Brisbane.jpg)](./File:CityCat_Gootcha_(ship,_2010)_in_January_2019_in_Brisbane.jpg)\\n\\n[CityCat](./Transdev_Brisbane_Ferries \"Transdev Brisbane Ferries\") ferry passing the [City Botanic Gardens](./City_Botanic_Gardens \"City Botanic Gardens\") at [Gardens Point](./Gardens_Point \"Gardens Point\")\\n\\n[RiverCity Ferries](./RiverCity_Ferries \"RiverCity Ferries\") operates three ferry services along the [Brisbane River](./Brisbane_River \"Brisbane River\"), [CityCat](./CityCat \"CityCat\"), [Cross River](./Cityferry \"Cityferry\") and [CityHopper](./CityHopper \"CityHopper\"). Brisbane\\'s ferries, and particularly its [catamaran](./Catamaran \"Catamaran\") CityCats, are considered iconic to the city.[[143]](./Brisbane#cite_note-148)\\n\\nThe CityCat high-speed [catamaran](./Catamaran \"Catamaran\") ferry service, popular with tourists and commuters, operates services along the [Brisbane River](./Brisbane_River \"Brisbane River\") between the [University of Queensland](./University_of_Queensland \"University of Queensland\") and [Northshore Hamilton](./Northshore_Hamilton_ferry_wharf \"Northshore Hamilton ferry wharf\"), with wharves at [UQ St Lucia](./University_of_Queensland_ferry_wharf \"University of Queensland ferry wharf\"), [West End](./West_End_ferry_wharf \"West End ferry wharf\"), [Guyatt Park](./Guyatt_Park_ferry_wharf \"Guyatt Park ferry wharf\"), [Regatta](./Regatta_ferry_wharf \"Regatta ferry wharf\"), [Milton](./Milton_ferry_wharf \"Milton ferry wharf\"), [North Quay](./North_Quay_ferry_wharf \"North Quay ferry wharf\"), [South Bank](./South_Bank_ferry_wharf \"South Bank ferry wharf\"), [QUT Gardens Point](./QUT_Gardens_Point_ferry_wharf \"QUT Gardens Point ferry wharf\"), [Riverside](./Riverside_ferry_wharf \"Riverside ferry wharf\"), [Sydney Street](./Sydney_Street_ferry_wharf \"Sydney Street ferry wharf\"), [Mowbray Park](./Mowbray_Park_ferry_wharf \"Mowbray Park ferry wharf\"), [New Farm Park](./New_Farm_Park_ferry_wharf \"New Farm Park ferry wharf\"), [Hawthorne](./Hawthorne_ferry_wharf \"Hawthorne ferry wharf\"), [Bulimba](./Bulimba_ferry_wharf \"Bulimba ferry wharf\"), [Teneriffe](./Teneriffe_ferry_wharf \"Teneriffe ferry wharf\"), [Bretts Wharf](./Bretts_Wharf \"Bretts Wharf\"), [Apollo Road](./Apollo_Road_ferry_wharf \"Apollo Road ferry wharf\"), and [Northshore Hamilton](./Northshore_Hamilton_ferry_wharf \"Northshore Hamilton ferry wharf\").\\n\\nThe Cross River services operate smaller vessels for popular cross-river routes, namely: [Bulimba](./Bulimba_ferry_wharf \"Bulimba ferry wharf\")–[Teneriffe](./Teneriffe_ferry_wharf \"Teneriffe ferry wharf\") and [Holman Street](./Holman_Street_ferry_wharf \"Holman Street ferry wharf\")–[Riverside](./Riverside_ferry_wharf \"Riverside ferry wharf\").\\n\\nThe free CityHopper service operates smaller vessels along a route between [North Quay](./North_Quay_ferry_wharf \"North Quay ferry wharf\") and [Sydney Street](./Sydney_Street_ferry_wharf \"Sydney Street ferry wharf\"), stopping at [South Bank](./South_Bank_ferry_wharf \"South Bank ferry wharf\"), [Maritime Museum](./Maritime_Museum_ferry_wharf \"Maritime Museum ferry wharf\"), [Riverside](./Riverside_ferry_wharf \"Riverside ferry wharf\") and [Holman Street](./Holman_Street_ferry_wharf \"Holman Street ferry wharf\").\\n\\nThere are tourist passenger ferries that depart the Brisbane River at [Pinkenba](./Pinkenba \"Pinkenba\") to [Tangalooma](./Tangalooma \"Tangalooma\") on Moreton Island four times daily, and Micat 4WD car ferries that depart from the [Port of Brisbane](./Port_of_Brisbane \"Port of Brisbane\") daily.[[144]](./Brisbane#cite_note-149)\\n\\n#### Pedestrian\\n\\nAn extensive network of pedestrian and cyclist pathways span the banks of the [Brisbane River](./Brisbane_River \"Brisbane River\") in the inner suburbs to form the [Riverwalk](./Brisbane_River#Brisbane_Riverwalk \"Brisbane River\") network.[[145]](./Brisbane#cite_note-150) In some segments, the Riverwalk is built over the river. The longest span of the Riverwalk connects [Newstead](./Newstead,_Queensland \"Newstead, Queensland\") in the east with [Toowong](./Toowong \"Toowong\") in the west.\\n\\n#### Airports\\n\\n[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/97/Brisbane_Airport_domestic_terminal_Vabre.jpg/250px-Brisbane_Airport_domestic_terminal_Vabre.jpg)](./File:Brisbane_Airport_domestic_terminal_Vabre.jpg)\\n\\nDomestic terminal at [Brisbane Airport](./Brisbane_Airport \"Brisbane Airport\")\\n\\n[Brisbane Airport](./Brisbane_Airport \"Brisbane Airport\") ([IATA](./IATA_airport_code \"IATA airport code\"): **BNE**, [ICAO](./ICAO_airport_code \"ICAO airport code\"): **YBBN**) is the city\\'s main airport, the [third busiest in Australia](./List_of_the_busiest_airports_in_Australia \"List of the busiest airports in Australia\") after [Sydney Airport](./Sydney_Airport \"Sydney Airport\") and [Melbourne Airport](./Melbourne_Airport \"Melbourne Airport\"). It is located north-east of the city centre on Moreton Bay and provides domestic and international passenger services. In 2017, Brisbane Airport handled over 23\\xa0million passengers.[[146]](./Brisbane#cite_note-AirportTraffic-151) The airport is the main [hub](./Airline_hub \"Airline hub\") for [Virgin Australia](./Virgin_Australia \"Virgin Australia\") as well as a number of minor and freight airlines, and a focus city for [Qantas](./Qantas \"Qantas\") and [Jetstar](./Jetstar \"Jetstar\"). The airport is served by the Airtrain service which runs on the [Airport line](./Airport_railway_line,_Brisbane \"Airport railway line, Brisbane\"), providing a direct service to the [CBD](./Brisbane_central_business_district \"Brisbane central business district\").\\n\\n[Archerfield Airport](./Archerfield_Airport \"Archerfield Airport\") in Brisbane\\'s southern suburbs, [Redcliffe Airport](./Redcliffe_Airport_(Queensland) \"Redcliffe Airport (Queensland)\") on the [Redcliffe Peninsula](./Redcliffe_Peninsula \"Redcliffe Peninsula\") and [Caboolture Airfield](./Caboolture_Airfield \"Caboolture Airfield\") in the far north of the metropolitan area serve Brisbane as [general aviation](./General_aviation \"General aviation\") airports.\\n\\nBrisbane is also served by other major airports in [South East Queensland](./South_East_Queensland \"South East Queensland\"), including [Gold Coast Airport](./Gold_Coast_Airport \"Gold Coast Airport\") at [Coolangatta](./Coolangatta \"Coolangatta\"), [Sunshine Coast Airport](./Sunshine_Coast_Airport \"Sunshine Coast Airport\") at [Marcoola](./Marcoola \"Marcoola\"), and [Toowoomba Wellcamp Airport](./Toowoomba_Wellcamp_Airport \"Toowoomba Wellcamp Airport\") at [Wellcamp](./Wellcamp \"Wellcamp\").\\n\\n#### Seaport\\n\\n[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/02/Brisbane_Docks_2004_-_panoramio.jpg/250px-Brisbane_Docks_2004_-_panoramio.jpg)](./File:Brisbane_Docks_2004_-_panoramio.jpg)\\n\\nThe [Port of Brisbane](./Port_of_Brisbane \"Port of Brisbane\"), Australia\\'s third-busiest seaport\\n\\nThe [Port of Brisbane](./Port_of_Brisbane \"Port of Brisbane\") is located on the south side of the mouth of the Brisbane River on [Moreton Bay](./Moreton_Bay \"Moreton Bay\") and on the adjacent Fisherman\\'s Island, an [artificial island](./Artificial_island \"Artificial island\") created by [land reclamation](./Land_reclamation \"Land reclamation\"). It is the third busiest port in Australia for value of goods.[[107]](./Brisbane#cite_note-Port_Technology-112) The port is the endpoint of the main shipping channel across Moreton Bay which extends 90 kilometres north near [Mooloolaba](./Mooloolaba \"Mooloolaba\"). The port has 29 operating berths including nine deep-water container [berths](./Berth_(moorings) \"Berth (moorings)\") and three deep-water bulk berths as well as 17 bulk and general cargo berths.\\n\\nThere are two [cruise ship](./Cruise_ship \"Cruise ship\") terminals in Brisbane. [Portside Wharf](./Portside_Wharf \"Portside Wharf\") on the north side of the river at [Hamilton](./Hamilton,_Queensland \"Hamilton, Queensland\") is an international standard facility for cruise liners. Due to the height of the [Gateway Bridge](./Gateway_Bridge \"Gateway Bridge\") which must be passed to reach the terminal, the wharf services small and medium-sized cruise ships. The [Brisbane International Cruise Terminal](./Brisbane_International_Cruise_Terminal \"Brisbane International Cruise Terminal\") at Luggage Point in [Pinkenba](./Pinkenba \"Pinkenba\") on the north side of the river opposite the Port of Brisbane is able to accommodate the largest cruise vessels in the world.[[147]](./Brisbane#cite_note-152)\\n\\n### Healthcare\\n\\n[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4e/Queensland_Children%27s_Hospital_in_Brisbane%2C_November_2019.jpg/250px-Queensland_Children%27s_Hospital_in_Brisbane%2C_November_2019.jpg)](./File:Queensland_Children\\'s_Hospital_in_Brisbane,_November_2019.jpg)\\n\\nThe [Queensland Children\\'s Hospital](./Queensland_Children\\'s_Hospital \"Queensland Children\\'s Hospital\") at [South Brisbane](./South_Brisbane \"South Brisbane\")\\n\\nBrisbane is covered by [Queensland Health\\'s](./Queensland_Health \"Queensland Health\") Hospital and Health Services (divided in Metro North, Metro South and Children\\'s Health Queensland).[[148]](./Brisbane#cite_note-153) Within the greater Brisbane area there are eight major [public hospitals](./Public_hospital \"Public hospital\"), four major [private hospitals](./Private_hospital \"Private hospital\"), and numerous smaller public and private facilities. The [Royal Brisbane and Women\\'s Hospital](./Royal_Brisbane_and_Women\\'s_Hospital \"Royal Brisbane and Women\\'s Hospital\") and the [Princess Alexandra Hospital](./Princess_Alexandra_Hospital,_Brisbane \"Princess Alexandra Hospital, Brisbane\") are two of Queensland\\'s three major trauma centres. Standing alone, they are the largest hospitals in Australia. The [Princess Alexandra Hospital](./Princess_Alexandra_Hospital,_Brisbane \"Princess Alexandra Hospital, Brisbane\") houses the [Translational Research Institute (Australia)](./Translational_Research_Institute_(Australia) \"Translational Research Institute (Australia)\") along with the state\\'s renal and liver transplant services. The [Royal Brisbane and Women\\'s Hospital](./Royal_Brisbane_and_Women\\'s_Hospital \"Royal Brisbane and Women\\'s Hospital\") includes a specialist burns unit.[[149]](./Brisbane#cite_note-154) [The Prince Charles Hospital](./The_Prince_Charles_Hospital \"The Prince Charles Hospital\") is the state\\'s major cardiac transplant centre. Other major public hospitals include the [Queensland Children\\'s Hospital](./Queensland_Children\\'s_Hospital \"Queensland Children\\'s Hospital\"), the [Queen Elizabeth II Jubilee Hospital](./Queen_Elizabeth_II_Jubilee_Hospital \"Queen Elizabeth II Jubilee Hospital\"), and the [Mater Hospital](./Mater_Group \"Mater Group\").\\n\\nSpecialist and [general medical practices](./General_practitioner \"General practitioner\") are located in the CBD, and most suburbs and localities.\\n\\nBrisbane is also home to the headquarters of the [Queensland Ambulance Service](./Queensland_Ambulance_Service \"Queensland Ambulance Service\") central executive, located at the Emergency Services Complex Kedron Park, along with the headquarters of the [Queensland Fire and Emergency Services](./Queensland_Fire_and_Emergency_Services \"Queensland Fire and Emergency Services\") and the Queensland Emergency Operations Centre.\\n\\n### Other utilities\\n\\n[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9a/Toowong_Cemetery_1a.jpg/250px-Toowong_Cemetery_1a.jpg)](./File:Toowong_Cemetery_1a.jpg)\\n\\n[Toowong Cemetery](./Toowong_Cemetery \"Toowong Cemetery\"), opened in 1875, Queensland\\'s largest cemetery\\n\\nWater in Brisbane is managed by two [statutory authorities](./Statutory_authority \"Statutory authority\"): [Seqwater](./Seqwater \"Seqwater\") and [Urban Utilities](./Queensland_Urban_Utilities \"Queensland Urban Utilities\"). Bulk water storage, treatment and transportation for South East Queensland is managed by [Seqwater](./Seqwater \"Seqwater\"), with [Urban Utilities](./Queensland_Urban_Utilities \"Queensland Urban Utilities\") (previously Brisbane Water) responsible for distribution to the greater Brisbane area. Water for the area is stored in three major dams to the north-west of the metropolitan area: [Wivenhoe](./Wivenhoe_Dam \"Wivenhoe Dam\"), [Somerset](./Lake_Somerset \"Lake Somerset\") and [North Pine](./North_Pine_Dam \"North Pine Dam\").\\n\\nThe provision of electricity in Brisbane is managed by government and private bodies. Generators (some private and some owned by the Queensland government) sell energy into the wholesale market for eastern Australia known as the [National Electricity Market](./National_Electricity_Market \"National Electricity Market\"). Transmission and distribution of electricity is managed by the Queensland government owned corporations [Energex](./Energex \"Energex\") and [Powerlink Queensland](./Powerlink_Queensland \"Powerlink Queensland\") respectively. [Private retailers](./Electricity_retailing \"Electricity retailing\") then purchase electricity from the wholesale [market](./Electricity_market \"Electricity market\") and sell it to consumers, which have the ability to choose between different retailers in a partially de-regulated market.[[150]](./Brisbane#cite_note-155)\\n\\nThe supply of [gas](./Natural_gas \"Natural gas\") to users is more heavily privatised, with the private [APA Group](./APA_Group_(Australia) \"APA Group (Australia)\") distributing gas in Brisbane, which is then bought and sold by retailers (mainly [Origin Energy](./Origin_Energy \"Origin Energy\") and [AGL Energy](./AGL_Energy \"AGL Energy\")) in a partially de-regulated market.[[151]](./Brisbane#cite_note-156)\\n\\nMetropolitan Brisbane is serviced by all major and most minor telecommunications companies and their networks, including [Telstra](./Telstra \"Telstra\"), [Optus](./Optus \"Optus\"), and [Vodafone Australia](./Vodafone_Australia \"Vodafone Australia\").\\n\\nBrisbane is home to numerous [cemeteries](./Cemeteries \"Cemeteries\") including the following large 19th-century historical cemeteries: the 44-hectare [Toowong Cemetery](./Toowong_Cemetery \"Toowong Cemetery\") (the largest cemetery in Queensland, which is a popular destination for walkers and joggers), [Balmoral Cemetery](./Balmoral_Cemetery,_Brisbane \"Balmoral Cemetery, Brisbane\"), [Lutwyche Cemetery](./Lutwyche_Cemetery \"Lutwyche Cemetery\"), [Nudgee Cemetery](./Nudgee_Cemetery \"Nudgee Cemetery\"), [Nundah Cemetery](./Nundah_Cemetery \"Nundah Cemetery\"), and [South Brisbane Cemetery](./South_Brisbane_Cemetery \"South Brisbane Cemetery\").\\n\\nMedia\\n-----\\n\\n### Print\\n\\nThe main local print newspapers of Brisbane are *[The Courier-Mail](./The_Courier-Mail \"The Courier-Mail\")* and its sibling *[The Sunday Mail](./The_Sunday_Mail_(Brisbane) \"The Sunday Mail (Brisbane)\")*, both owned by [News Corporation](./News_Corporation \"News Corporation\"). Brisbane also receives the national daily, *[The Australian](./The_Australian \"The Australian\")* and its sibling the *Weekend Australian.*\\n\\nThe *[Brisbane Times](./Brisbane_Times \"Brisbane Times\")* is Brisbane\\'s second major local news source, owned by [Nine](./Nine_Entertainment_Co. \"Nine Entertainment Co.\"), and is online only. Its sibling papers, *[The Sydney Morning Herald](./The_Sydney_Morning_Herald \"The Sydney Morning Herald\")* and Melbourne\\'s *[The Age](./The_Age \"The Age\")* are sometimes sold in print in Brisbane in small numbers. The national broadsheet *[Australian Financial Review](./Australian_Financial_Review \"Australian Financial Review\")*, also owned by Nine, is sold in print in Brisbane.\\n\\nThere are community and suburban newspapers throughout the metropolitan area, including *Brisbane News* and *City News*, many of which are produced by [Quest Community Newspapers](./Quest_Community_Newspapers \"Quest Community Newspapers\").\\n\\n### Television\\n\\n[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/30/OIC_river_view_of_toowong_and_mt_coot-tha.jpg/250px-OIC_river_view_of_toowong_and_mt_coot-tha.jpg)](./File:OIC_river_view_of_toowong_and_mt_coot-tha.jpg)\\n\\nTelevision [transmission towers](./Transmission_tower \"Transmission tower\") atop [Mount Coot-tha](./Mount_Coot-tha \"Mount Coot-tha\")\\n\\nBrisbane is served by all five major television networks in Australia, which broadcast from prominent [television transmission towers](./Transmission_tower \"Transmission tower\") on the summit of [Mount Coot-tha](./Mount_Coot-tha \"Mount Coot-tha\"). The three commercial stations, [Seven](./Seven_Network \"Seven Network\"), [Nine](./Nine_Network \"Nine Network\"), and [Ten](./Network_10 \"Network 10\"), are accompanied by two government networks, [ABC](./Australian_Broadcasting_Corporation \"Australian Broadcasting Corporation\") and [SBS](./Special_Broadcasting_Service \"Special Broadcasting Service\"). Channels provided by these networks include [10 HD](./10_HD \"10 HD\") (10 broadcast in HD), [10 Drama](./10_Drama \"10 Drama\"), [10 Comedy](./10_Comedy \"10 Comedy\"), [Nickelodeon](./Nickelodeon_(Australian_TV_channel) \"Nickelodeon (Australian TV channel)\"), [TVSN](./TVSN \"TVSN\"), [ABC TV HD](./ABC_HD_(Australian_TV_channel) \"ABC HD (Australian TV channel)\") (ABC TV broadcast in HD), [ABC Family](./ABC_Family_(Australian_TV_channel) \"ABC Family (Australian TV channel)\")/[ABC Kids](./ABC_Kids_(Australia) \"ABC Kids (Australia)\"), [ABC Entertains](./ABC_Entertains \"ABC Entertains\"), [ABC News](./ABC_News_(TV_channel) \"ABC News (TV channel)\"), [SBS HD](./SBS_HD \"SBS HD\") (SBS broadcast in HD), [SBS World Movies](./SBS_World_Movies \"SBS World Movies\"), [SBS Viceland HD](./SBS_Viceland_HD \"SBS Viceland HD\") (SBS Viceland broadcast in HD), [SBS Food](./SBS_Food \"SBS Food\"), [NITV](./NITV \"NITV\"), [SBS WorldWatch](./SBS_WorldWatch \"SBS WorldWatch\"), [7HD](./7HD \"7HD\") (Seven broadcast in HD), [7two](./7two \"7two\"), [7mate](./7mate \"7mate\"), [7flix](./7flix \"7flix\"), [7mate HD](./7mate_HD \"7mate HD\") (7mate broadcast in HD), [Racing.com](./Racing.com \"Racing.com\"), [9HD](./9HD \"9HD\") (Nine broadcast in HD), [9Gem](./9Gem \"9Gem\"), [9Go!](./9Go! \"9Go!\"), [9Life](./9Life \"9Life\"), [9Gem HD](./9Gem_HD \"9Gem HD\") (9Gem broadcast in HD) and [9Rush](./9Rush \"9Rush\"). [31 Digital](./31_Digital \"31 Digital\"), a community station, also broadcast in Brisbane until 2017. [Optus](./Optus \"Optus\") and [Foxtel](./Foxtel \"Foxtel\") operates Pay TV services in Brisbane, via [cable](./Cable_television \"Cable television\") and [satellite](./Satellite_television \"Satellite television\") means.\\n\\n### Radio\\n\\nBrisbane is serviced by five major public radio stations including major commercial radio stations, including [ABC Radio Brisbane](./ABC_Radio_Brisbane \"ABC Radio Brisbane\") (local news, current affairs and talk); ([Swedish](./Swedish_language \"Swedish language\"): *Jämtlands län*, [Southern Sami](./Southern_Sami_language \"Southern Sami language\"): *Jiemthen leene*) is a [county](./Counties_of_Sweden \"Counties of Sweden\") or *[län](./Län \"Län\")* in [Sweden](./Sweden \"Sweden\"). It consists of the provinces of [Jämtland](./Jämtland \"Jämtland\") and [Härjedalen](./Härjedalen \"Härjedalen\"), along with minor parts of [Hälsingland](./Hälsingland \"Hälsingland\") and [Ångermanland](./Ångermanland \"Ångermanland\"), plus two small strips of [Lapland](./Lapland,_Sweden \"Lapland, Sweden\") and [Dalarna](./Dalarna \"Dalarna\"). It borders the counties of [Dalarna](./Dalarna_County \"Dalarna County\"), [Gävleborg](./Gävleborg_County \"Gävleborg County\"), [Västernorrland](./Västernorrland_County \"Västernorrland County\"), and [Västerbotten](./Västerbotten_County \"Västerbotten County\"), as well as the Norwegian county of [Trøndelag](./Trøndelag \"Trøndelag\"). It measures 49,443\\xa0km2 (19,090\\xa0sq\\xa0mi) and constitutes 12% of Sweden\\'s total area, making it the country\\'s third largest county. The capital is [Östersund](./Östersund \"Östersund\"). The [county governor](./List_of_governors_of_Jämtland_County \"List of governors of Jämtland County\") and leader of the [administrative board](./County_Administrative_Boards_of_Sweden \"County Administrative Boards of Sweden\"), as appointed by the Swedish government, has been Marita Ljung since 2021.[[3]](./Jämtland_County#cite_note-3)\\n\\nThe county was established in 1810, at the time it consisted only of the provinces of Jämtland and Härjedalen, which is why the [coat of arms](./Coat_of_arms \"Coat of arms\") is a shield parted per fess with their provincial arms. [King Carl XVI Gustaf](./Carl_XVI_Gustaf \"Carl XVI Gustaf\") is occasionally referred to as Duke of Jämtland after his title of king.\\n\\nProvince\\n--------\\n\\nFor history, geography and culture, see [Jämtland](./Jämtland \"Jämtland\") and [Härjedalen](./Härjedalen \"Härjedalen\").\\n\\nJämtland County consists of primarily the provinces of Jämtland and Härjedalen, though minor parts of [Hälsingland](./Hälsingland \"Hälsingland\") and [Ångermanland](./Ångermanland \"Ångermanland\") are also included, along with small uninhabited areas in [Lapland](./Lapland,_Sweden \"Lapland, Sweden\") and [Dalarna](./Dalarna \"Dalarna\").[*[citation needed](./Wikipedia:Citation_needed \"Wikipedia:Citation needed\")*]\\n\\nAdministration\\n--------------\\n\\nThe main aim of the [County Administrative Board](./County_Administrative_Boards_of_Sweden \"County Administrative Boards of Sweden\") is to fulfill the goals set in national politics by the [Riksdag](./Riksdag \"Riksdag\") and the [Government](./Government_of_Sweden \"Government of Sweden\"), to coordinate the interests and promote the development of the county, to establish regional goals and safeguard the due process of law in the handling of each case. The County Administrative Board is a [Government Agency](./Government_Agencies_in_Sweden \"Government Agencies in Sweden\") headed by a Governor. See [List of Jämtland Governors](./List_of_Jämtland_Governors \"List of Jämtland Governors\").[*[citation needed](./Wikipedia:Citation_needed \"Wikipedia:Citation needed\")*]\\n\\nDemography\\n----------\\n\\nJämtland County is sparsely populated and more than one-third of the population lives in the [countryside](./Countryside \"Countryside\"), making Jämtland County the second largest rural region in Sweden, after [Gotland County](./Gotland_County \"Gotland County\"). However, most of the population lives in the rather densely populated region surrounding lake [Storsjön](./Storsjön \"Storsjön\"), commonly called *Storsjöbygden*, \"the Storsjö district/countryside\".[*[citation needed](./Wikipedia:Citation_needed \"Wikipedia:Citation needed\")*]\\n\\nPolitics\\n--------\\n\\nThe county is dominated by the [Swedish Social Democratic Party](./Swedish_Social_Democratic_Party \"Swedish Social Democratic Party\") and the [Centre Party](./Centre_Party_(Sweden) \"Centre Party (Sweden)\"), which is unique in Sweden, but corresponds to the situation in the bordering Norwegian county of Nord-Trøndelag. The county is rather contrastive in the political field. While a majority of the municipalities are governed by [liberal](./Liberalism \"Liberalism\")-[conservative](./Conservatism \"Conservatism\") ([Swedish](./Swedish_language \"Swedish language\"): *borgerlig*, lit. \"[bourgeois](./Bourgeois \"Bourgeois\")\") majorities or by coalitions overstepping the bloc border, the [county council](./County_Councils_of_Sweden \"County Councils of Sweden\") is controlled by a [red-green](./Red-Greens_(Sweden) \"Red-Greens (Sweden)\") majority and the Social Democrats receive two out of four [mandates](./Mandate_(politics) \"Mandate (politics)\") to the [Riksdag](./Riksdag \"Riksdag\").\\n\\nAfter the Swedish county council election in 2022, the following [political parties](./List_of_political_parties_in_Sweden \"List of political parties in Sweden\") are represented in the Jämtland county council ([Swedish](./Swedish_language \"Swedish language\"): *Region Jämtland Härjedalen*):[[4]](./Jämtland_County#cite_note-4)\\n\\n| Party | | Seats | Votes | % |\\n| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |\\n|  | [Social Democrats](./Swedish_Social_Democratic_Party \"Swedish Social Democratic Party\") | 21 | 30,702 | 36.95% |\\n|  | [Moderate Party](./Moderate_Party \"Moderate Party\") | 9 | 12,941 | 15.57% |\\n|  | [Centre Party](./Centre_Party_(Sweden) \"Centre Party (Sweden)\") | 7 | 10,486 | 12.62% |\\n|  | [Sweden Democrats](./Sweden_Democrats \"Sweden Democrats\") | 7 | 10,343 | 12.45% |\\n|  | [Christian Democrats](./Christian_Democrats_(Sweden) \"Christian Democrats (Sweden)\") | 5 | 7,280 | 8.76% |\\n|  | [Left Party](./Left_Party_(Sweden) \"Left Party (Sweden)\") | 4 | 5,992 | 7.21% |\\n|  | [Green Party](./Green_Party_(Sweden) \"Green Party (Sweden)\") | 2 | 2,688 | 3.23% |\\n|  | [Liberals](./Liberals_(Sweden) \"Liberals (Sweden)\") | -
